ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --no-fail-on-findings

The flag takes precedence over the config, and --fail-on-findings turns the gate back on whatever the config says. The scan still exits 1 when it is incomplete or a database is stale.

docs.title: Incomplete scans
docs.text:
With fail_on_incomplete_scanners on, the default, a scan exits 1 when a scanner it selected did not finish: ERROR (it failed, or its tool could not start, as when a sandbox the configuration asks for cannot be provided), MISSING (its tool is not installed), or a scanner that lost some of its targets. It also exits 1 when no scanner ran or a converter failed. The message names each scanner and its status.

Turn a scanner you cannot run off, or exclude it, rather than turning this gate off: a SKIPPED scanner is recorded as not measured, and the gate stays on for the others. fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false or --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners accepts an incomplete scan; with it off, a scan in which no scanner ran, or in which no selected scanner had a file to scan, exits 0.

docs.title: Stale content databases
docs.text:
grype, trivy, and the offline semgrep and opengrep rulesets read databases that age. ASH measures each one after the scanner runs, treats a database it cannot date as stale, and fails the scan when one is past its age bound; Content databases lists the databases and their bounds.

With content_db_staleness: fail, the default, a stale database fails the scan with exit 1, before fail_on_findings is considered, and the message says how to refresh it. A scanner that passed against the stale database is recorded ERROR, with the database named, and one that failed its threshold stays FAILED. The scan reports the stale database once, as the cause of the exit code, and does not list the scanner as incomplete as well. With warn, the scan continues and the reports carry the warning. To relax one database for a limited time, add an override; it applies until 00:00 UTC on its expiration date and is then ignored with a warning:

content_db_staleness: fail
content_db_staleness_overrides:
  - database: grype-db
    policy: warn
    expiration: "2027-03-31"
    reason: Offline runners get a new image every week

--allow-stale-content-db sets warn for one scan, and --no-allow-stale-content-db sets fail. Either flag replaces the config's policy and clears its overrides. Content databases explains the bounds, and Run offline covers keeping the databases fresh.

docs.title: Who can change the gate
docs.text:
On the command line, a repository's own config is honored for every setting on this page except the stale content database policy, which it can only make stricter (Configuration trust model). A repository you scan can set fail_on_findings: false, raise thresholds, turn scanners off, and add suppressions, and none of it is marked in the results.

When the repository is not yours to trust, keep these settings yours:

  • Pass your own config with --config, from a file the repository's authors cannot change. In a scan of one directory, ASH then does not read the repository's config at all. In workspace mode, every setting your --config makes is final for every project (Scan a multi-project workspace).
  • Pass the gate flags explicitly. --fail-on-findings, --fail-on-incomplete-scanners, and --no-allow-stale-content-db take precedence over any config file, and --config-overrides beats the file for the global threshold. A per-scanner threshold in the repository's config still replaces the global one for its scanner, which is why the first point matters.
  • Pass --ignore-suppressions to report findings that suppressions, ignore paths, and ash-ignore comments would hide. It lifts yours as well as the repository's, and every scanner reads the files under an ignore path. In container mode it reaches the scan inside the container and works there as in a local scan. To drop only the repository's ignore paths, pass --config-overrides 'global_settings.ignore_paths=[]' instead.

The repository still affects the results in other ways. Its inline suppressions apply: ASH's ash-ignore comments unless you pass --ignore-suppressions, and the scanners' own comments, such as bandit's # nosec (set scanners.bandit.options.ignore_nosec: true in your config to ignore those). Its .gitignore and .ignore files also remove files from the set that several scanners read, with or without --ignore-suppressions; Coverage lists which scanners use that set. Configuration trust model lists the rest.

A config file that an MCP client delivers to the ASH MCP server cannot set fail_on_findings, fail_on_incomplete_scanners, content_db_staleness, or content_db_staleness_overrides to a value other than the server's own: the server refuses the whole file. Under the server's default policy such a file can still raise thresholds and turn scanners off. Configuration trust model covers both tiers.

docs.title: CI recipes
docs.text:
Report findings, but fail when the scan is incomplete or a database is stale:

ash --source-dir . --no-fail-on-findings

To try it without every scanner's tool, run detect-secrets alone. Its finding is reported, and the scan exits 0:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --no-fail-on-findings

Fail on HIGH and CRITICAL findings, with the gate set by the pipeline rather than by the repository:

ash --source-dir . --config "$RUNNER_TEMP/ash-gate.yaml" \
  --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db

where the pipeline writes ash-gate.yaml outside the checkout (here, in the GitHub Actions runner's temporary directory):

project_name: payments-api
global_settings:
  severity_threshold: HIGH

To fail on HIGH and above while still using the repository's config, override the threshold instead: ash --source-dir . --config-overrides global_settings.severity_threshold=HIGH.

In a sharded scan, gate on ash merge, which recomputes the verdict over all shards; see Scale to large repositories.

docs.title: Suppress findings
docs.text:
When a finding is a false positive or an accepted risk, suppress it so it stops failing the scan. A suppression keeps the finding in the results, marked suppressed, with your reason. An ignore path drops findings in a path from the results entirely. Suppressions, ignore paths, and scanner exclusions explains how they differ and how they interact with the gate and the reports.

To write a suppression you need the finding's rule ID and file. Both are in .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.flat.json (rule_id, file_path, line_start) and in the SARIF report ash.sarif (ruleId).

docs.title: Suppress a finding in the config
docs.text:
Add an entry to global_settings.suppressions:

global_settings:
  suppressions:
    - path: src/deploy.py
      rule_id: B602
      line_start: 40
      line_end: 48
      reason: The command is a constant; no user input reaches it
      expiration: "2027-01-31"
    - path: tests/**
      rule_id: B101
      reason: assert is how the tests check results
Field Required Meaning path yes The file, or a pattern, relative to the scanned directory reason yes Why the finding is suppressed. It appears in the reports. rule_id no The rule to suppress, as ASH reports it. Without it, the entry suppresses every rule in its path. line_start, line_end no Lines the finding must overlap, inclusive. line_start alone runs to the end of the file. expiration no The date, YYYY-MM-DD, from which the suppression stops matching symbol no Only findings inside this function, class, or method; see Scope a suppression to a symbol package_name, package_version, package_path no Only findings about this dependency, for dependency scanners such as grype and npm-audit
  • Paths match case-sensitively: tests/** does not match Tests/. In a pattern without **, * also matches across directory separators, so src/*.py matches src/sub/app.py; ** matches any depth. A path that starts with ./ matches nothing, and neither does an empty path, . or ./. A trailing slash is literal, unlike in an ignore path: tests/ matches no finding, and the scan warns that it matched nothing and gives tests/**/*, the pattern for the files under the directory. A bare directory name such as tests names only the path tests itself and matches nothing inside it. When the directory exists in the scanned directory, ash config validate and ash config lint warn about either one with that pattern and exit 0. They warn in the same way, saying what to write instead, about a path that starts with ./ (./src/app.py is src/app.py) and about an empty path or .. A path whose leading names match the tree only in another case (tests/** against Tests/) gets a warning that names the tree's spelling and says that patterns match case-sensitively.
  • A file whose name is not valid UTF-8 is reported with each such byte written as \udcNN (a latin-1 secr\xe9t.py as secr\udce9t.py). A path matches it written that way, since the \ of a \udcNN escape is part of the name and not a separator, or with ? for that \ (secr?udce9t.py), or by a glob such as secr*t.py. An ignore path matches such a file the same way when ASH lists the files to scan. A UTF-8 file name that spells the same \udcNN text reads as the same name, so in a tree that holds both files, both are reported under that name, and a path that matches one matches both.
  • rule_id is a case-insensitive pattern with no scanner prefix. It matches any scanner that reports that rule ID.
  • Quote the expiration date. YAML reads an unquoted 2027-01-31 as a date, not a string, and ASH then refuses the whole config (exit 3). ash config lint and ash config get name the problem.
  • A key that is not in the table makes the config invalid (exit 3), and when a known key is close, the error names it: ruleId fails with Unknown key 'ruleId' (did you mean 'rule_id'?). The same holds for an ignore path.

To try a suppression before you write it into the file, pass it for one run. In a repository where detect-secrets reports SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD in app.py, this run passes:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"path": "app.py", "rule_id": "SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password"}]'

With rule_id misspelled, the same run is refused instead of suppressing every rule in app.py:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"path": "app.py", "ruleId": "SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password"}]'

docs.title: Expiration
docs.text:
On its expiration date, by the local clock of the machine that runs the scan (UTC in the container image, which sets TZ=UTC), a suppression stops matching, and the finding fails the next scan again. At the start of a scan, ASH logs one warning that lists every suppression and ignore path that has expired, including those whose date is today, and then a warning for the ignore paths and one for the suppressions that expire within the next 30 days. With --ignore-suppressions, these warnings leave suppressions out. ash config lint reports suppressions that have expired, and ash config lint --fix removes them.

An expired suppression no longer applies, so this run fails on the finding and names the entry:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"path": "app.py", "rule_id": "SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password", "expiration": "2020-01-01"}]'

The following ignore paths and suppressions have expired and no longer apply:
  - Suppression of rule 'SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD' for 'app.py' expired on 2020-01-01. Reason: Fixture value, not a real password
Remove them, or move their expiration dates, in your ASH configuration file.

docs.title: Scope a suppression to a symbol
docs.text:
symbol limits a suppression to findings inside one definition in the file, named with dots from the top of the file, such as Deployer.run_hook. The name is exact and case-sensitive. A suppression with symbol keeps matching when the code around the definition moves, where a line range would not.

global_settings:
  suppressions:
    - path: src/deploy.py
      rule_id: B602
      symbol: Deployer.run_hook
      reason: run_hook only runs commands from the deploy manifest

ASH finds the definition by parsing the file with tree-sitter, for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and Java files. The parsers are in the symbols extra, which is not installed by default; without it, a suppression with symbol matches nothing and the scan logs a warning that names the extra. The container image includes it.

docs.title: Installing the extra
docs.text:
When the extra is missing, the scan warning and ash config lint print a command that installs the extra's packages. The command is read from the metadata of the ASH you run, so it fits that ASH whatever its version or source. It runs the uv that ASH depends on through the Python interpreter that runs ASH and installs into that interpreter's environment, so it reaches a virtualenv, a uv tool install or pipx install environment, and a checkout's uv sync environment alike. The hint prints the interpreter's full path where this shows <python>:

<python> -m uv pip install --python <python> 'tree-sitter>=0.26,<0.27' 'tree-sitter-java>=0.23.5,<0.24' 'tree-sitter-javascript>=0.25,<0.26' 'tree-sitter-python>=0.25,<0.26' 'tree-sitter-typescript>=0.23.2,<0.24'

A plain pip install of those packages does not do the same: environments made by uv have no pip, so pip runs whichever pip comes next on PATH, usually another Python's.

You can also reinstall ASH with [symbols] added to the source you installed it from. For uvx that is the only way that lasts: uvx rebuilds its cached environment from its own arguments, so an extra installed into it is dropped.

The symbols extra is available from the next release, the first after v3.7.1. v3.7.1 and earlier define only cdk, and asking one of them for [symbols] installs it without the extra, with only a warning. Until that release, install from the main branch, as Install from main shows, with [symbols] after the package name:

uv tool install --force "automated-security-helper[symbols] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@main"

main moves, so this command also replaces the ASH you run with the newest code. To stay on one version, or to use a checkout, put that source after the first @ instead: a commit SHA from main, or file:///path/to/checkout. Keep the @ and the source. ASH is not published on PyPI, and the PyPI project with ASH's name is unrelated and has no symbols extra, so asking for the extra by the bare name installs that project instead.

docs.title: Suppress a finding in the source
docs.text:
An ash-ignore comment on the finding's line suppresses it, and ash-ignore-next-line suppresses a finding on the line below:

import subprocess

DEPLOY_COMMAND = "make deploy"
subprocess.call(DEPLOY_COMMAND, shell=True)  # ash-ignore: B602 fixed command

# ash-ignore-next-line: B108 the build container's own scratch directory
SCRATCH_DIR = "/tmp/ash-build"
  • Write the comment with # or //. Other comment styles, such as /* */ and <!-- -->, are not recognized.
  • Name exactly one rule ID, as ASH reports it, for example B602, SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD, or zizmor/unpinned-uses. It is compared without case but is not a pattern. A comment without a rule ID suppresses nothing.
  • The comment must be on the line where the finding starts (or the line above it, for ash-ignore-next-line). Scanners report different start lines for the same code; check line_start in ash.flat.json.
  • The text after the rule ID is the reason. It is optional, and the reports show it after (ASH inline).

docs.title: The scanners' own comments
docs.text:
Most scanners have their own inline syntax. ASH runs bandit, semgrep, opengrep, checkov, cdk-nag, cfn-nag, and detect-secrets in a way that honors it. For cfn-guard, cfn-lint, gitleaks, and zizmor, ASH turns the tools' own ignore comments off unless an operator source turns them on for that scanner, so a repository cannot hide its own findings that way; use ASH's suppressions instead:

Scanner Comment In ASH's results bandit # nosec, # nosec B602 Not reported. Set scanners.bandit.options.ignore_nosec: true to make bandit ignore these comments. semgrep, opengrep # nosemgrep, # nosemgrep: <rule-id> Reported as suppressed checkov # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_18:reason, or checkov: skip: in a CloudFormation resource's Metadata Reported as suppressed, with checkov's reason cdk-nag cdk_nag: rules_to_suppress: in a resource's Metadata Reported as suppressed, with the reason cfn-guard guard: SuppressedRules: in a resource's Metadata Reported, unless an operator turns the comments on; then not reported cfn-lint cfn-lint: config: ignore_checks: in a resource's Metadata Reported, unless an operator turns the comments on; then not reported cfn-nag cfn_nag: rules_to_suppress: in a resource's Metadata Not reported detect-secrets pragma: allowlist secret, pragma: allowlist nextline secret Not reported. Setting scan_settings.filters_used replaces detect-secrets' default filters and turns these comments off. gitleaks gitleaks:allow Reported, unless an operator turns the comments on; then not reported zizmor # zizmor: ignore[<rule>] Reported, unless an operator turns the comments on; then not reported

A finding that is not reported never reaches ASH, so it leaves no trace in any report and --ignore-suppressions cannot bring it back.

docs.title: Ignore a path
docs.text:
An ignore path drops every finding located in a path:

global_settings:
  ignore_paths:
    - path: vendor/**
      reason: Third-party code, scanned upstream
    - path: tests/fixtures/**
      reason: Deliberately vulnerable test inputs

path and reason are required, and paths match the way suppression paths do. The findings an ignore path drops include a dependency scanner's findings about a package installed under it: a node_modules/ ignore path also drops grype's findings located in node_modules/<package>/package.json.

An ignore path can also have an expiration, which works the way a suppression's does: on that date the ignore path stops applying, so the files it covered are scanned again and their findings count on the next scan. The same holds for the entries of bandit excluded_paths, checkov skip_path, and syft exclude. This expired ignore path no longer drops the finding in app.py:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.ignore_paths+=[{"path": "app.py", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password", "expiration": "2020-01-01"}]'

A trailing slash names the files under a directory. With a copy of app.py in vendor/, the ignore path vendor/ drops the copy's finding, and the suppression from the earlier example covers the original, so the run passes:

mkdir -p vendor && cp app.py vendor/app.py
ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.ignore_paths+=[{"path": "vendor/", "reason": "Third-party code"}]' \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"path": "app.py", "rule_id": "SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password"}]'
rm -r vendor

ASH does not read a .ashignore file. It does apply the repository's .gitignore and .ignore files to the files it hands several scanners; see Coverage. Several scanners also have their own exclusion options, such as bandit's excluded_paths, checkov's skip_path, and semgrep's exclude; the scanner reference lists them.

docs.title: Find suppressions that no longer match
docs.text:
The unused-suppressions reporter, on by default, writes .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.unused-suppressions.json and ash.unused-suppressions.md. They list each entry in global_settings.suppressions that matched no finding in the scan, including expired ones. They do not cover ignore paths or inline suppressions.

After a scan, ash config lint --fix-unused comments out the entries that the report lists, with the date. When it comments out every entry, it leaves suppressions: [] above them, so the file still loads; remove the [] when you turn an entry back on. A suppression can look unused in one environment and still be needed in another, for example when a scanner whose finding it covers is not installed locally but runs in CI. Check the report before you remove entries.

docs.title: Add a suppression while you review findings
docs.text: ash inspect findings opens the last scan's findings in your terminal. Select a finding and press x to suppress it: ASH asks for a reason and an optional expiration, and adds an entry with the finding's path and rule ID, and its line as line_start and line_end, to the config file (the --config file, else the config ASH discovers, else a new .ashrc.yaml in the current directory). It keeps the comments of a YAML file, except one whose global_settings is written inline (global_settings: {...}), which it rewrites in full, and it writes a JSON config back as JSON. If the file already has an identical entry, nothing is added, and the status bar says so; an entry for another line, reason, or expiration with the same rule ID and path is added. It does not edit TOML files, or a file that uses extends but has no suppressions list of its own.

docs.title: See every finding
docs.text:
--ignore-suppressions reports findings as if no suppression existed, so you can review what the suppressions hide. With the suppression from the earlier example, the finding fails the scan again:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --ignore-suppressions \
  --config-overrides 'global_settings.suppressions+=[{"path": "app.py", "rule_id": "SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD", "reason": "Fixture value, not a real password"}]'

It lifts config suppressions, ignore paths, ash-ignore comments, and cdk-nag's Metadata suppressions. Every scanner reads the files under an ignore path, and their findings are reported; to drop only the ignore paths for one run, pass --config-overrides 'global_settings.ignore_paths=[]' instead. It does not bring back what a scanner never reported (findings hidden by the scanner's own comments or its exclusion options), and findings that semgrep and checkov report as suppressed stay suppressed. The repository's .gitignore and .ignore files still apply, and findings in ASH's own output directory stay out of the results. In container mode the flag reaches the scan inside the container and works there as in a local scan.

When an MCP client delivers the config, its suppressions, ignore paths, and scanner exclusions are marked client-supplied in the results; see Configuration trust model. ASH applies all of them itself, so in a local scan with --ignore-suppressions none of them applies, and the findings they would have marked are ordinary findings.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: Find the symptom, then read its cause and fix. Two places hold most of what you need: the console output of the scan, and ash.log in the output directory (.ash/ash_output/ash.log by default), which has every warning, including the ones the console summary leaves out.

docs.title: A scanner shows MISSING
docs.text:
Symptom: a row in the summary table has the result MISSING, and the scan ends with:

ERROR (1) Exiting because the scan was incomplete: 1 selected scanner(s) did not
evaluate everything they were given
  grype: MISSING
    its tool grype was not found on PATH or in /home/me/.ash/bin, /home/me/.local/share/uv/tools/automated-security-helper/bin, /usr/local/bin; install it with `ash dependencies install` or exclude grype with --exclude-scanners

Cause: ASH could not find the scanner's tool, or could not install it. The line under each MISSING scanner gives the reason, and so does its missing_reason in ash_aggregated_results.json. A warning in ash.log names what is missing too, for example Grype executable not found in PATH. Please ensure grype is installed. The console shows it when the progress display is off (--no-progress). For the scanners ASH installs with uv, one or both of these warnings mean ASH found no uv, neither the copy installed with ASH, beside the Python interpreter that runs it, nor one on your PATH, so it cannot install them during the scan:

UV tool validation failed - UV is not available but required
UV tool execution is required but UV is not available for checkov

A scanner with nothing to scan in the project, such as cdk-nag with no CloudFormation template, npm-audit with no lockfile beside a package.json, or actionlint with no workflows, shows SKIPPED instead, whether or not its tool is installed. Scanners that have no such check, such as grype and semgrep, show MISSING whenever their tool is missing.

Fix: install the tool, usually with ash dependencies install --tool grype (using the scanner's name). When a scanner shows MISSING lists the exceptions: detect-secrets, cdk-nag, npm-audit, and cfn-nag. If you do not need the scanner, leave it out with ash --exclude-scanners grype, which records it as SKIPPED.

docs.title: A tool inside the scanned directory is not run
docs.text:
Symptom: a scanner shows MISSING although its tool is installed, and after the list of incomplete scanners the scan names each tool it found only inside the scanned directory:

Found only inside the scanned tree, so not run: grype (/home/me/repo/.venv/bin/grype). To use them, install it outside the scanned tree, or set ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS=1 or pass --allow-in-tree-tools to allow tools from the tree.

ash.log has a warning for each one (the console shows it too when the progress display is off):

Not running grype from inside the scanned tree /home/me/repo: /home/me/repo/.venv/bin/grype. To use it, install it outside the scanned tree, or set ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS=1 or pass --allow-in-tree-tools to allow tools from the tree.

The scanner's missing_reason in ash_aggregated_results.json records the reason, as "grype was found only inside the scanned tree, at ...".

Cause: during a scan, ASH does not run programs found inside the directory it scans. The usual case is a scanner installed in the project's virtual environment or node_modules, which uv run or npm run put first on PATH.

Fix: install the tool outside the repository, for example with ash dependencies install or uv tool install. To use the in-tree copies for one scan, pass --allow-in-tree-tools or set ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS=1. ash mcp ignores both. See Tools inside the scanned directory.

docs.title: A scanner is ERROR with an exit code it does not accept
docs.text:
Symptom: a scanner's row is ERROR, and its error names the tool's exit code:

Failed to execute semgrep scanner on source: SemgrepScanner scan failed: its tool exited with code 7, which this scanner does not accept as a completed run, so its results file is not graded (exit code 7: not an accepted exit code; success_exit_codes=[0, 1]). No stderr captured; checked .ash/ash_output/scanners/semgrep/source/SemgrepScanner.stderr.log, which the tool did not write. .ash/ash_output/scanners/semgrep/source/results_sarif.sarif reports: Invalid YAML file ...

Cause: the tool reported that it failed. Each scanner accepts the exit codes its tool uses for a run that completed, with or without findings, and nothing else. A failed tool can still leave a results file (semgrep exits 7 and writes SARIF holding only error notifications when it cannot read a rule configuration; grype exits 1 and writes a zero-byte report when it cannot load its database), so ASH does not read the file of a run with any other code: an empty or error-only file would otherwise be graded PASSED with no findings. A tool ended by a signal shows as 128 + N (129 for SIGHUP, 130 for SIGINT, 137 for SIGKILL). 127 is a tool the OS could not start, or a run ASH itself failed to carry out (the scanner's errors name ASH's error).

Scanner Accepted exit codes What the tool uses other codes for bandit 0, 1 (issues found) 2: any error (bandit/cli/main.py) checkov 0, 1 (failed checks) 2: the run crashed (checkov/main.py) grype 0, 2 (a match at or above grype --fail-on) 1: any error, such as a database it cannot load (grype's cmd/grype/cli package) semgrep 0, 1 (findings) 2: fatal; 3 and up: specific failures, 7 for a rule configuration it cannot read (semgrep/error.py) opengrep 0, 1 the same values as semgrep (src/osemgrep/core/Exit_code.ml) trivy, trivy-repo 0 1: any error (trivy's cmd/trivy package) syft 0 1: any error (syft's cmd/syft package) ferret-scan 0, 3 (coverage cut short under fail_on_incomplete: the findings are reported and the row is ERROR, as its target counts as failed) 1: any error snyk-code 0, 1 (issues found) 2: an error; 3: no supported project (src/cli/exit-codes.ts) gitleaks 0, 2 (leaks found: ASH runs gitleaks --exit-code=2) 1: any error, such as an unreadable config; gitleaks exits 1 for leaks too unless told otherwise, which is why ASH moves the leaks code zizmor 0, 3 (nothing it could audit; findings never set the status because ASH runs zizmor --no-exit-codes) any other status actionlint 0, 1 (problems found) 2: a bad command line; 3: a fatal error, such as an unreadable file cfn-lint 0 and the even values up to 14: 2 error, 4 warning and 8 informational, added together for a run with more than one level (cfnlint/runner/cli.py) 1: a fatal error, so any odd status; anything above 15 cfn-guard 0, 19 (at least one rule failed) any other status, such as 255 for a parse error or a missing rules path

trivy exits 0 for a run with findings unless its exit-code setting names another code. ASH runs trivy and trivy-repo with trivy --exit-code=0, which outranks an exit-code in the operator's trivy config and TRIVY_EXIT_CODE (measured with trivy 0.75.0), and neither scanner reads a trivy.yaml from the scanned directory, so a run with findings exits 0 and a nonzero exit only ever means trivy failed. ASH decides the scan's exit code from the findings itself.

cfn-nag, npm audit, detect-secrets and cdk-nag are not in this table. cfn-nag exits with its count of failing violations and is judged per template; npm audit exits 1 both for advisories and for errors and is judged by whether it wrote a report; detect-secrets and cdk-nag run in ASH's own worker processes.

Fix: read what the message quotes, and fix what the tool reported: its stderr, or, when it wrote none (semgrep and opengrep report a rule file they cannot read only in their SARIF), the error-level notifications from its results file, which the message names. The full text is in the <Scanner>.stderr.log, the <Scanner>.stdout.log and the results file under scanners/<name>/<target>/ in the output directory; the message names the ones the tool wrote. For semgrep and opengrep under --offline, see Seeding the semgrep and opengrep rule cache. For grype, see What each scanner does offline.

The scan exits 1 for an ERROR scanner while fail_on_incomplete_scanners is on, which is the default. With it off, the exit code comes from the findings alone, so a scan whose only problem is the failed scanner exits 0; see Incomplete scans.

docs.title: semgrep and opengrep show SKIPPED on Windows
docs.text:
Cause: both are off by default on Windows, and semgrep publishes no Windows build, so it is SKIPPED even when you turn it on. A SKIPPED scanner does not fail the scan, so the scan passes without them, as long as another selected scanner runs.

Fix: to run them, scan from WSL or in a container. See Platform limits.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: ASH exits 0 when nothing is actionable, 1 when the scan is incomplete or failed, 2 when it has actionable findings at or above the threshold, 3 for a configuration it cannot use or an input it refuses before scanning, such as a linked output directory, 4 for a workspace error, and 5 for a usage error. When a scan is both incomplete and has findings, it exits 1 (a workspace scan exits 2). See Exit codes.

docs.title: The scan exits 1 with no findings
docs.text:
Cause: the scan is incomplete, or it stopped before running. The last lines say which:

  • Exiting because the scan was incomplete, followed by the scanners: a scanner is MISSING, or it ran and failed (ERROR), or it could not read some of its inputs. For ERROR, the scanner's own messages are in ash.log and in its stderr log under scanners/ in the output directory.
  • Exiting because conversion was incomplete: see the next entry.
  • Exiting because N content database(s) are past their declared age bound: see A content database is stale.
  • Exiting because no scanner ran: every scanner was SKIPPED, so the scan shows nothing about the code. Each scanner's skipped_reason in ash_aggregated_results.json says why. Check --scanners, --exclude-scanners, and the enabled settings in your configuration.
  • A message that no selected scanner had a file to scan: see No selected scanner had a file to scan.
  • Exiting because N rule(s) could not be evaluated: cdk-nag rules failed with an error on your templates, so the scan says nothing about them. Fix the template the rule fails on, or suppress that rule's findings for the template.

Fix: fix the cause named in the message. To accept an incomplete scan, pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners, as the scan's message says, or set fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false at the top level of your configuration. Excluding the scanner is usually better, because the reports then say it did not run.

docs.title: No selected scanner had a file to scan
docs.text:
Symptom: the scan exits 1 with no findings, every selected scanner is SKIPPED, and the error names the scanners that had nothing to scan:

No selected scanner had a file to scan: bandit was SKIPPED with nothing to scan, so this run has shown the target to be neither clean nor dirty. To accept a run that scanned nothing, set fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false or pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners.

When the config sets global_settings.ignore_paths, the error also shows its first three patterns, with a count of any others, and suggests narrowing them:

No selected scanner had a file to scan: detect-secrets was SKIPPED with nothing to scan, so this run has shown the target to be neither clean nor dirty. The config's global_settings.ignore_paths ('**') leaves every path it matches out of what the scanners read, which can leave them nothing to scan; narrow it to have those files scanned. To accept a run that scanned nothing, set fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false or pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners.

A run whose scanners were all SKIPPED for another reason, such as a --scanners name that matches no scanner on this platform, or every selected scanner turned off in the configuration, reports Scan ran no scanners: instead, with each scanner and its status; see The scan exits 1 with no findings.

Cause: each selected scanner had nothing to read, so the scan shows nothing about the code. A scanner that reads only some files, such as cfn-nag with no CloudFormation template or bandit with no Python file, has nothing to read in a project without them, and no scanner has anything to read when the scan set is empty. Two cases are ERROR instead, and the error gives a count. semgrep and opengrep are ERROR when their own exclusions, rather than ignore_paths, left out every file they found. bandit is ERROR when it scanned no file although Python files that nothing excludes are there; when ignore_paths or bandit's own excluded_paths leave out every Python file, bandit is SKIPPED.

Fix: check that --source-dir names the project, that ignore_paths, and the repository's .gitignore and .ignore files, leave the files you mean to scan, and that the scanners you selected read them; Scanner coverage lists what each scanner reads. To accept such a scan, pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners or set fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false; it then exits 0. ash merge gives the same verdict over the shards.

docs.title: The scan exits 1 because conversion was incomplete
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR (1) Exiting because conversion was incomplete: 1 converter(s) did not process the files they were given

Cause: ASH converts Jupyter notebooks to Python, and extracts .zip, .tar, and .gz archives, before it scans them. A notebook that nbconvert could not convert, or an archive that cannot be read, fails the scan so that its content is not silently left unscanned. The lines after the message name each converter and up to five of the files it could not convert, or, for a converter that crashed, its error as <Type>: <message>. ash.log has a line for each file with the reason, Could not convert '<file>': <reason> (the console shows it too when the progress display is off), and each converter's failed_inputs in ash_aggregated_results.json records the same reason. A reason that comes from an unexpected error is the error's type and message, such as BadZipFile: Bad CRC-32 for file 'app.py'. For a notebook, the reason says that nbconvert exited with a non-zero code, did not finish within 60 seconds, or wrote no output, or that uv could not run nbconvert and no jupyter-nbconvert was found.

A notebook in an offline scan with no nbconvert installed gives jupyter: dependencies unavailable, so it never ran, because ASH does not install nbconvert offline.

Fix: for notebooks, install nbconvert ahead of time with ash dependencies install --tool jupyter, or let ASH install it during an online scan. To see nbconvert's own error output, run the scan again with --debug. For a corrupt archive, fix or remove the file. To skip a file, add it to global_settings.ignore_paths with a reason; see Suppress findings.

docs.title: The scan exits 2
docs.text:
Cause: the scan found at least one finding at or above the severity threshold, which is MEDIUM unless you change it. The scan ends with ERROR (2) Exiting due to 2 actionable findings found in ASH scan.

Fix: fix or suppress the findings (Suppress findings). To report findings without failing, pass --no-fail-on-findings, or set fail_on_findings: false at the top level of your configuration, not under global_settings. To fail only on more severe findings, set global_settings.severity_threshold. See Set the gate.

docs.title: The command exits 5
docs.text:
Symptom: the command stops before anything runs and writes no report. A mistyped option prints an Error box:

Usage: ash scan [OPTIONS]
Try 'ash scan --help' for help.
╭─ Error ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ No such option: --fail-on-finding (Possible options: --fail-on-findings,     │
│ --no-fail-on-findings)                                                       │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

Cause: a usage error. Every ash command exits 5 when its command line is wrong: an option or argument the command does not take, a value an option does not accept (such as an invalid --output-formats, --mode, --strategy, or --min-severity), a --scanners list that names no scanner, a --source-dir that does not exist or cannot be entered, an --output-dir that ASH cannot create, enter, or write in, --use-existing with no results to use, or an ash report --format that no reporter answers to. The code is not 2, so a CI gate does not read a mistyped flag as a scan with findings. Two selections exit 2 instead: an ash dependencies install --tool name that it has no plugin for, and a --plugin-type other than converter, scanner, or reporter (Exit codes).

ash scan --output-formats nosuch

ash report with a format no reporter answers to lists the ones it has, whether or not there are results to report:

ash report --format nosuch

Error: Reporter plugin 'nosuch' not found.
Available reporter formats:
  - csv
  - cyclonedx
  - github-ghas
  ...

Fix: correct the command line; ash <command> --help lists each command's options. Scanner and reporter names use hyphens, as ash plugin list shows them. A single misspelled name among valid ones in --scanners is not a usage error: ASH logs No registered scanner matches ... and runs the others.

docs.title: The scan exits 3
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR (3) Invalid configuration: Configuration validation failed for '/home/me/repo/.ashrc.yaml': Invalid value at 'global_settings.fail_on_findings': Extra inputs are not permitted. Run: ash config lint --config /home/me/repo/.ashrc.yaml

Cause: the configuration file has a key ASH does not know below the top level, or a value of the wrong type anywhere, top level included. A suppression, an ignore path, or a plugin's options with a key ASH does not know is refused too, and the message lists the keys it accepts:

cat > .ashrc.yaml <<'EOF'
global_settings:
  suppressions:
    - rule_id: B602
      path: app.py
      reason: Commands come from a fixed allowlist
      expires: "2027-04-30"
EOF
ash config validate

❌ 1 error(s); a scan refuses the configuration because of these:
  1. Invalid value at 'global_settings.suppressions[0]': Value error, Unknown key 'expires' (did you mean 'expiration'?) in a suppression. Accepted keys: expiration, line_end, line_start, package_name, package_path, package_version, path, reason, rule_id, symbol.

A common case is an unquoted expiration date in a suppression: YAML reads it as a date, and ASH expects text. Quote it, as in "2027-04-30".

Fix: correct the key or value that the message names. ash config validate and ash config lint check the file the way a scan does and report the same errors, with exit code 3; lint marks each one [blocks the scan]. See Configure ASH.

docs.title: Your configuration has no effect
docs.text:
Symptom: the scan behaves as if your configuration file were not there: suppressions do not apply, or a setting is ignored. The scan does not exit 3.

Cause: one of these. A file that does not exist or does not parse is not one of them: the scan refuses it with exit 3.

  • A top-level key is misspelled, such as fail_on_finding. ASH ignores unknown keys at the top level.
  • ASH found a different file first. ash config get prints the configuration a scan would use.
  • A suppression's or an ignore path's expiration date has passed. The entry then stops applying, and the scan starts with a warning that names it (see below).
  • The setting is one a repository's file may not set; see the next entry.

An ignore path that expired lets its files back into the scan, so the finding in app.py counts again here:

cat > .ashrc.yaml <<'EOF'
global_settings:
  ignore_paths:
    - path: app.py
      reason: Generated file, scanned upstream
      expiration: "2026-01-31"
EOF
ash scan --scanners detect-secrets --no-progress

The following ignore paths and suppressions have expired and no longer apply:
  - Ignore path 'app.py' expired on 2026-01-31. Reason: Generated file, scanned upstream
Remove them, or move their expiration dates, in your ASH configuration file.

Fix: run ash config validate, which checks the file the way a scan does and warns about unknown top-level keys and a missing project_name, and ash config get, which prints the configuration a scan would use. ash config lint also lists expired suppressions and ignore paths.

docs.title: A setting in the repository's config file is ignored
docs.text:
Symptom: a warning such as:

Ignoring sandbox.network_scanners from /home/me/repo/.ash/.ash.yaml: that config is inside a git checkout or the scanned tree, or was delivered by an MCP client. ...

Cause: some settings decide what ASH may run, read, or send, or whether a stale database fails the scan: sandbox grants, plugin modules, reporter destinations and credentials, options that name a scanner's own configuration or ignore file, tool_version, trivy-repo's disable_telemetry: false, and a relaxed content_db_staleness. A config file inside the scanned directory, or inside any git checkout, could have been written by someone other than you, so ASH ignores those settings from it, even from a config you keep in an ops repository of its own. These settings count as yours only from --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. The warning names each setting and the file, says why, and says how to keep the setting. For a plugin module found inside a git checkout or the scanned directory, it also gives where Python found the module and which checkout or directory that is. For other modules, it says that the module is not importable, or what ASH's AWS or Snyk plugin package would send off the host.

Under ash mcp, a config file that an MCP client names as a scan's config_path, outside the directories ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_CONFIG_ROOTS names, is held to the same limits. Under the default policy, a config file an MCP client delivered is refused instead when its own sandbox section gives a scanner a network or an extra_read_paths entry the server's settings do not, or changes a sandbox mode other than off that the server sets, or when its own ash_plugin_modules list adds a module this check would drop; see What a delivered config cannot set.

Fix: pass the setting with --config-overrides, or move the file outside every git checkout, such as under /etc/ash, and name it with --config. A file inside the scanned directory has to move out of it as well. Name a plugin module with --ash-plugin-modules, or install it outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. A config inside a checkout cannot add ASH's AWS or Snyk plugin package at all, so name those with --ash-plugin-modules or one of the two ways above. For some scanners, the file such an option names must also be outside the scanned tree; Options only the operator can set says which. See Configuration trust model.

docs.title: The scan exits 4
docs.text:
Cause: a workspace scan (--workspace) could not start, or a workspace option was used without one. The message names the problem. The causes are:

  • the workspace file is missing or is not valid JSON;
  • --workspace auto finds more than one workspace file;
  • a project path contains .., or a project directory does not exist;
  • --source-dir is given with --workspace;
  • --dry-run, --allow-missing-projects, or --workspace-config is given without --workspace.

Fix: correct the workspace file or the command line, or pass --allow-missing-projects to skip projects that do not exist. See Scale to large repositories.

docs.title: The scan stops because the output directory is a symlink
docs.text:
Symptom: the scan exits 3 before writing anything, with one of:

ERROR (3) The output directory /home/me/out is a symlink. ASH does not write to, clear or mount its output directory through a link, whatever the sandbox mode. Pass --output-dir with a directory that is not a link, or replace the link with a directory.
ERROR (3) /home/me/repo/.ash is a symlink, on the way to the output directory /home/me/repo/.ash/ash_output. ...
ERROR (3) /home/me/out/reports is a symlink. ...

Cause: the output directory, a directory on the way to it inside the scanned directory, or something ASH writes inside it, such as reports, is a symbolic link. ASH clears and writes its output directory, so it does not do that through a link. This check applies whether or not the sandbox is on. In an ash --workspace scan, a link at projects/<project> fails only that project, and a link at projects or .workspace-spool stops the whole run. Output files lists every path ASH checks.

Fix: pass --output-dir with a real directory, which can be outside the project, or replace the link with a directory. Turning the sandbox off does not change this.

docs.title: The scan stops because a report file is a link
docs.text:
Symptom: the run exits 1 before any reporter writes, with this message (ash merge prints the same text after Refusing to write reports:):

ERROR (1) /home/me/out/reports/ash.sarif is a symlink. ASH does not write a report through a link. Remove the link and run ASH again.

Cause: a file a reporter is about to write in reports/ is a symbolic link or a directory junction. A scan clears reports/ first, so this usually comes from ash scan --use-existing or ash merge writing into an output directory that already holds the link.

Fix: remove the link and run the command again, or write to a new output directory.

docs.title: A content database is stale
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR (1) Exiting because 1 content database(s) are past their declared age bound
  Content database semgrep-offline-rules (semgrep) is stale: downloaded 2026-08-31T22:43:12Z, 40d 0h old, past its 720h bound ...

Cause: grype, trivy, and offline semgrep and opengrep read databases that go out of date. ASH fails a scan whose database is past its age bound, or whose age it cannot read; Content databases lists the bounds. Online scans keep grype's and trivy's databases current, so this usually happens offline or with an old image.

Fix: refresh the database. For an offline image, rebuild it with ash build-image --offline. For offline rules on your machine, download them again (Seeding the semgrep and opengrep rule cache). To scan with the old database anyway, pass --allow-stale-content-db or set content_db_staleness: warn: the stale database then no longer fails the scan, and every report names it. With warn, a scan passes even when a database is missing, so its vulnerability results can be incomplete. See Content databases and Run ASH offline.

docs.title: The first scan is slow
docs.text:
Cause: the first scan downloads grype's vulnerability database, which can take a minute or more, and installs any uv-based scanner that is not installed yet. Later scans reuse both.

Fix: run ash dependencies install ahead of time. In CI, cache the scanners' cache directories, such as ~/.cache/grype and ~/.cache/trivy, between runs.

docs.title: A scanner hangs
docs.text:
Symptom: the scan stops making progress. Every 60 seconds the log shows which scanners are still running:

bandit still running on source (60s elapsed)

Cause: each scanner has a time limit, scan_timeout, which defaults to 1800 seconds (30 minutes). A scanner that reaches it is stopped and shows as ERROR. With scan_timeout set to 65, for example:

(bandit @ source) timed out after 65.0s and was killed. Raise scanners.bandit.options.scan_timeout if this target legitimately needs longer.

There is no limit on the scan as a whole.

Fix: find the scanner in the "still running" lines or in ash.log, and look at its stderr log under scanners/<scanner>/ in the output directory. Then do one of these:

  • Exclude it for now: ash --exclude-scanners bandit.
  • Lower or raise its limit: ash --config-overrides 'scanners.bandit.options.scan_timeout=600'.
  • Run scanners one at a time to see where time goes: ash --strategy sequential.
  • Get more detail with ash --verbose or ash --debug.

docs.title: The install fails while building rtoml
docs.text:
Symptom: uvx or uv tool install fails with Failed to build rtoml and a message that the Python version (3.15) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version.

Cause: uv chose Python 3.15, which some of ASH's dependencies do not support yet.

Fix: pass a supported Python version, as in uv tool install --python 3.12. See Install ASH.

docs.title: The install fails because git is missing
docs.text:
Symptom: uv stops with an error whose causes end in:

  cause: Git operation failed
  cause: Git executable not found. Ensure that Git is installed and available.

Cause: uv and pip fetch ASH from its git repository, which needs git.

Fix: install git and run the command again.

docs.title: ash is not found after installing
docs.text:
Cause: the directory where uv or pipx puts commands is not on your PATH in the current shell.

Fix: open a new terminal. If that does not help, run uv tool update-shell (for uv) or pipx ensurepath (for pipx), then open a new terminal.

docs.title: ash runs a different program on Windows
docs.text:
Symptom: in Git Bash or an MSYS2 shell, ash --version prints an error such as ash: 0: Illegal option --, and ash dependencies install reports cannot open dependencies.

Cause: Git for Windows and MSYS2 ship an unrelated shell named ash, and it comes first on your PATH.

Fix: use ashv3 or automated-security-helper, which are the same program as ASH's ash.

docs.title: Results differ between your machine and CI
docs.text:
Cause: the two runs differ in something ASH does not control:

  • Scanner versions. A scanner on your PATH is used if its version is in range, so your machine and CI can run different versions.
  • Database age. grype's and trivy's databases change daily.
  • Platform. On Windows, semgrep and opengrep are SKIPPED.
  • Diff scans. With --changed-files-only, ASH reports findings in every file when git cannot list the changes: the base ref does not exist, as in a shallow clone, the directory is not in a git repository, or git is not installed. The log says which, such as git diff against origin/main failed (rc=128); falling back to full scan.
  • Mode. ash --mode precommit runs a smaller set of scanners.

Fix: run the same scanner versions in both places, for example with the same container image, and fetch enough history in CI for the diff.

docs.title: The container image does not build
docs.text:
Container mode builds ASH's image on your machine before it scans. Common causes:

  • No container runtime. The scan exits 1 with Unable to resolve an OCI runner. ASH tries finch, docker, nerdctl, and podman, in that order. Install one, or name it with --oci-runner.
  • A non-numeric user or group ID: Container UID must be a numeric value. Pass numbers to --container-uid and --container-gid.
  • No revision to install. A package that recorded no commit, such as one built from a source tarball, installs the release tag of its version, and a development or pre-release version has none, so the build stops and asks for --ash-revision-to-install. Pass a tag, a branch, or a full commit ID. Which ASH goes into the image lists where the revision comes from for each kind of install.
  • No access to the base image registry or the internet. The build pulls a Python base image and downloads ASH and its scanners. To use a mirror of the base image, set ASH_BASE_IMAGE_OVERRIDE.

Run container mode from a directory other than the project you scan, and name the project with --source-dir.

To scan offline with an image you already built, add --no-build, as in ash scan --mode container --offline --no-build. Without it, container mode builds the image first, and the first offline build of a UTC day downloads the databases again, which needs network access. See Run ASH offline.

With --custom-containerfile, ASH builds the ci target, which runs as root, even if you pass --build-target non-root. On Windows, ASH builds ci unless you name a target. A non-root build that would give its user UID 0 or GID 0, as a job running as root does, stops with exit code 3 before anything is built: pass --build-target ci there.

See Run ASH in a container.

docs.title: Run ASH in GitHub Actions
docs.text: ASH ships two reusable workflows. run-ash-security-scan.yml installs ASH and its scanner tools, scans the repository, and reports the result on the pull request. upload-ash-sarif.yml uploads the SARIF report to code scanning. You can call them, or write the steps yourself. For a first setup, follow Add ASH to a GitHub Actions pipeline.

docs.title: Call the reusable workflows
docs.text:
name: ASH
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  ash:
    uses: awslabs/automated-security-helper/.github/workflows/run-ash-security-scan.yml@v3.7.0
    permissions:
      contents: read
      checks: write
      pull-requests: write
    with:
      ash-version: v3.7.0
      ash-args: --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
      collect-sarif-report: false
  sarif:
    needs: ash
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ash.outputs.artifact-id != '' }}
    uses: awslabs/automated-security-helper/.github/workflows/upload-ash-sarif.yml@v3.7.0
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write

One thing in this file is required: grant the scan job contents: read, checks: write, and pull-requests: write. The called workflow declares all three, and GitHub refuses to start the run when the calling job grants less, even if you turn off the comment and the check.

The uses: ref selects the workflow file only. The ASH it installs is ash-version from ash-repo, which default to main of awslabs/automated-security-helper, so pass the same tag or commit as ash-version, as the example does, to run the ASH the workflow was written for. The install-* inputs default to true, so a call that sets none of them installs every tool that the scanners on by default need from the runner.

To leave a tool out, turn its scanner off and do not install the tool, for example with --exclude-scanners trivy in ash-args and install-trivy: false. In local mode, an input set to false while its scanner is on leaves that scanner MISSING when the repository has files it scans, and the incomplete-scan gate fails the job with exit code 1.

ASH's zizmor scanner reports each uses: line that names a tag as zizmor/unpinned-uses at HIGH, so a scan of a repository that holds this file fails until you pin both lines to a commit. git ls-remote https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper refs/tags/v3.7.0 prints the commit that v3.7.0 names. Replace the v3.7.0 after each @, and the ash-version value, with that SHA, and end each uses: line with the comment # v3.7.0.

A pull request scan reads the configuration in the branch it scans, so the branch can change the gate. The workflow passes the fail-on-findings choice on the command line, and the ash-args line above does the same for incomplete scans and stale content databases, so the branch cannot turn those three off. It can still raise a severity threshold, add suppressions, or turn scanners off, and the config input names a file in the checkout, which the branch can edit too. To read the config from a commit the branch cannot change, such as the pull request's base commit, pass that commit as config-ref (see the table below). Who can change the gate lists what a repository can still affect.

docs.title: Inputs of run-ash-security-scan.yml
docs.text:
Input Defaults to Effect ash-version empty Git tag, branch, or commit of ASH to install. When empty, the job installs the ASH of the commit it was called at: a caller of a release tag gets that release, and a caller of @main gets that commit of main. The job resolves the value to one commit before it installs anything, and every step uses that commit; the job summary names it. A value that starts with - or holds a space, that names nothing in ash-repo, or that is both a branch and a tag on different commits fails the job. Every run installs it again. ash-repo empty Repository (owner/repo) to install ASH from. When empty, the job uses the repository the workflow file comes from. A value other than that repository needs ash-version too. The owner and the name may hold letters, digits, ., _, and -; any other form fails the job. ash-mode local Value of --mode. container builds ASH's image on the runner and scans inside it; see Run ASH in a container. config empty Path to an ASH config file, passed as --config and as ASH_CONFIG. When empty, ASH finds the config in the checkout. config-ref empty Commit, branch, or tag of the scanned repository to read the config file from, instead of the checkout. Needs config. The workflow writes the file under $RUNNER_TEMP and passes it as --config, and the tool config files it names by a relative path (config_file, and opengrep's and semgrep's config) come from the same commit. ASH treats it as the operator's config only while $RUNNER_TEMP is outside every git checkout and outside the scanned directory, as it is on GitHub-hosted runners; on a self-hosted runner, keep $RUNNER_TEMP outside them. A config that extends another file fails, and so does one at that commit that is missing, unless config-ref-missing is defaults. A value that starts with - or holds a space fails the job before git reads it. config-ref-missing refuse What config-ref does when that commit has no config file: refuse fails the job, and defaults scans with ASH's default config and logs a warning, for the pull request that adds a repository's first config. skip-unknown-tools false With config-ref, lets ash dependencies install name and skip a requested tool that the installed ASH has no plugin for, instead of failing the install. output-dir .ash/ash_output Output directory. The reporting job downloads the scan's artifact into the same path. fail-on-findings true Passes --fail-on-findings or --no-fail-on-findings. Either one overrides fail_on_findings in the repository's config. verbose true Passes --verbose. ash-args empty More ash scan options, on one line; a value of more than one line fails the job (see How the workflow checks its inputs). They are split on spaces with no quoting or glob expansion, and passed last, so they override the workflow's own --mode, --config, --base-ref, and fail-on-findings choice. collect-sarif-report true Upload ash.ghas.sarif to code scanning from the reporting job. It works on pull requests from branches of the same repository only, and is skipped on merge_group; for other events set it to false and call upload-ash-sarif.yml, as in Upload SARIF. collect-junit-xml-report true Publish ash.junit.xml as the check run ASH Scan JUnit Test Report from the reporting job. Every actionable finding is a failed test, so the check is red when there are findings. This step does not fail the job. post-pr-comment true Post ash.summary.md as a pull request comment, and update that comment on later runs. repository-owner ${{ github.repository_owner }} Post the comment only when the repository owner equals this value. python-version 3.12 Python version that actions/setup-python installs. install-grype true Install grype, and cache its vulnerability database. install-syft true Install syft. install-opengrep true Install opengrep, and cache the binary for a week. install-cfn-nag true Set up Ruby and install cfn-nag from the Gemfile and Gemfile.lock of the ASH commit the workflow installs. install-actionlint true Install actionlint. install-cfn-guard true Install cfn-guard and the rule files it evaluates. install-gitleaks true Install gitleaks. install-trivy true Install trivy. trivy downloads its vulnerability database during each scan. changed-files-only false Passes --changed-files-only and --base-ref, and checks out the repository's whole history to compute the changed files; see Scan only the files a pull request changes. Not supported with ash-mode: container: the scan stops with exit code 5. base-ref origin/main The base for changed-files-only on events other than pull_request and merge_group, which use their own base commit. artifact-name ash_output Name of the artifact the scan's output directory is uploaded as. A matrix, or a caller that calls this workflow more than once in one run, must give each call its own name: in the first attempt a second upload under a name already taken fails, and in a re-run it replaces the earlier upload.

The workflow has one output, artifact-id: the ID of the ash_output artifact the scan job uploaded, or empty when the scan failed before ASH wrote its reports. Start a job that reads the artifact, such as one calling upload-ash-sarif.yml, only when it is set.

The workflow at v3.7.0 and v3.7.1 has fewer inputs: no config-ref, config-ref-missing, or skip-unknown-tools, and of the install-* inputs only install-grype, install-syft, and install-opengrep, which default to false there. The install-* steps other than cfn-nag's run ash dependencies install --tool, which ASH 3.7.1 and earlier do not have, so with ash-version set to one of those releases, set those inputs to false.

The binary tools come from ash dependencies install, which downloads the versions that the installed ASH pins and checks each download against its pinned SHA256 before installing it. bandit, checkov, and semgrep need no input: ASH installs them from PyPI with uv tool install during the scan. detect-secrets is part of ASH, and cdk-nag and npm-audit use the Node.js and npm that GitHub's Ubuntu runners include.

Each install runs on every run, apart from what the workflow caches (see Cache tools and databases). For the versions ASH pins, each one downloads:

Input Downloads install-grype grype, about 32 MB, and during the scan its vulnerability database, about 190 MB compressed on 2026-10-12, unless the workflow restores a cached copy inside grype's bound install-syft syft, about 31 MB install-opengrep opengrep, about 46 MB, unless the workflow restores the cached binary install-cfn-nag Ruby, and the gems that cfn-nag's Gemfile.lock pins install-actionlint actionlint, about 2.4 MB install-cfn-guard cfn-guard, about 3.4 MB, and its rules install-gitleaks gitleaks, about 8.2 MB install-trivy trivy, about 52 MB, and during the scan its vulnerability database, about 133 MB compressed on 2026-10-12

Set an input to false when the scan does not need its tool, for example with ash-mode: container or with the scanner turned off.

docs.title: How the workflow checks its inputs
docs.text:
The scan job's first step checks every string input before any other step can print one. The runner reads a line of a step's log as a workflow command when the line starts with :: or holds ##[, and it starts a new line at a carriage return as well as at a line feed, so an input holding either could add a command of its own to a line that shows it.

The step drops one line feed at the end of a value. YAML ends a block of one line, such as ash-args: | or ash-args: > followed by one line of options, with that line feed, so such a block works. The step then refuses a value that holds a carriage return, a line feed, another control character, a Unicode line or paragraph separator, or ##[, so a value of more than one line, or one that ends in two line feeds, is refused. It checks the value byte by byte, so the answer does not depend on the runner's locale. The error names the input and does not print its value:

the ash-args input holds a line break, another control character or the legacy command marker, so it is refused without being printed. A block scalar of one line is fine; more than one line is refused.

A value that is only a line feed is refused with:

the ash-args input is only a line feed; leave it empty instead.

Every later step, and the reporting job, uses the checked value, not the input as given.

The step that resolves ash-version to a commit refuses two more values first, without printing them. An ash-repo that is not owner/name fails with:

ash-repo must be owner/name: letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', one '/' between them.

An ash-version that is empty, starts with -, or holds a space fails with:

ash-version is not a branch, tag or commit name: it is empty, starts with '-', or holds a space or a control character.

With config-ref set, the step that reads the config refuses a config-ref that starts with - or holds a space, before git reads it as an option:

config-ref is not a branch, tag or commit name: it starts with '-', or holds a space or a control character.

Each of these refusals fails the job before it installs anything.

ASH, and the git, uv, curl, bundle, gem, and cfn-nag commands the job runs, run with workflow commands stopped. Before each one, the step prints ::stop-commands:: with a new random token, and after it, on a line of its own, the token, also when the step is cancelled, as GitHub describes under "Stopping and starting workflow commands" in Workflow commands. A file name or a finding's text from the scanned tree in their output is then shown as text, not read as a command. When no random token can be read, the command does not run, and the step logs the error:

no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run

The job also checks that each commit ID and git ls-tree entry git reports has the form git gives it before printing it, and fails the step on one that does not.

docs.title: What the workflow does
docs.text:
The workflow runs two jobs on ubuntu-latest; neither the runner nor the timeouts are inputs. The scan job, SAST, SCA, and IaC Scan, has a 30-minute timeout and holds only contents: read, so nothing it runs, ASH and the scanners included, holds a token that can write.

Its first step checks the inputs, as How the workflow checks its inputs says. Before the checkout, a step resolves ash-version in ash-repo to one commit with git ls-remote. A full commit ID is used as given, and a tag gives the commit it points to. Every later step installs ASH from that commit, and cfn-nag's Gemfile comes from it too, so a branch that moves during the run cannot give two steps two different versions of ASH. The job summary names the commit.

The job then checks out the calling repository, with the whole history when changed-files-only is true, reads the config from config-ref when that is set, and installs the tools that the install-* inputs select. It runs ASH with uvx --reinstall, passing --source-dir ., the output directory, --no-progress, the fail-on-findings choice, --build-target ci, --mode, and --config when a config is set; --verbose unless verbose is false; --changed-files-only and --base-ref when changed-files-only is true; and then ash-args.

After the scan, whether it passed or failed, the scan job appends ash.summary.md to the job summary and uploads the artifact ash_output, kept for 7 days. The artifact holds reports/ and ash_aggregated_results.json from the output directory, and the same two from each project of a workspace scan. The rest of the output directory, such as each scanner's raw output under scanners/, is left out, because ASH does not mask secrets there.

The reporting job, Report ASH results, runs after a scan that passed or failed and uploaded its artifact, and only when post-pr-comment, collect-junit-xml-report, or collect-sarif-report is true. It holds checks: write and pull-requests: write, runs nothing from the scan, and downloads the artifact to:

  • post ash.summary.md as a pull request comment;
  • publish the JUnit check run;
  • upload ash.ghas.sarif to code scanning with category ash, when collect-sarif-report is true and the event is not merge_group.

Its result is a check run of its own, so a reporting failure does not fail the scan's check.

On a pull request from a fork, GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only, so the reporting job skips the comment and the check run and prints a notice. The scan, its exit code, the job summary, and the artifact are unchanged. On a push, the comment goes to the pull request that the pushed commit came from, if there is one.

docs.title: Upload SARIF with upload-ash-sarif.yml
docs.text:
run-ash-security-scan.yml does not declare security-events: write, and a called workflow can only narrow the token its caller grants, so the upload step inside it never holds that permission. Its upload works on pull requests from branches of the same repository; on workflow_dispatch, for example, the step fails with Resource not accessible by integration, which fails the reporting job's check but not the scan's. It is skipped on merge_group. collect-sarif-report: true is enough in a workflow that runs on pull requests from the same repository alone. The workflow does not declare the permission, because GitHub checks every permission a called workflow declares when the run starts, so every caller that does not grant it would fail before any job ran.

To upload on every trigger, set collect-sarif-report: false and add a job that calls upload-ash-sarif.yml, as in the example above. That workflow:

  • downloads the artifact that the scan job uploaded in the same workflow run, and uploads reports/ash.ghas.sarif from it with category ash;
  • takes two optional inputs: artifact-id, the scan workflow's artifact-id output, which names exactly the artifact that scan uploaded, and artifact-name, the name to download by when artifact-id is empty, ash_output by default;
  • skips merge_group events;
  • declares contents: read and security-events: write, which the calling job must grant.

Give the calling job if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.ash.outputs.artifact-id != '' }}. The scan job sets artifact-id once it has uploaded its reports, which it does when the scan fails on findings too. A job-level if: with no status function such as !cancelled() or always() is skipped whenever a job it needs failed, so the condition alone would never let the upload run after a scan with findings.

Code scanning is available for public repositories. A private repository needs a GitHub Code Security license. GitHub's SARIF upload documentation also lists actions: read for workflows in private repositories; upload-ash-sarif.yml does not declare it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Job Permission Needed for Scan contents: read Checking out the repository Scan checks: write The JUnit check run Scan pull-requests: write The pull request comment SARIF upload contents: read The checkout in the upload job SARIF upload security-events: write Uploading to code scanning SARIF upload actions: read Private repositories only, per GitHub's upload documentation

Set permissions: contents: read at the top of the workflow, as the example does, and grant the rest per job. Inside run-ash-security-scan.yml, only the reporting job holds checks: write and pull-requests: write; the scan job, which runs ASH and the scanners, holds contents: read alone.

docs.title: Write the steps yourself
docs.text:
This job does what the reusable workflows do, without the comment, the check run, and the job summary:

name: ASH
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  ash:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read # private repositories only
    env:
      INSTALL_SPEC: "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@18d369b23da25a81e9458561248e1aafff6a70fa # v10.3.1
        with:
          version: latest
          enable-cache: true
      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@b1da4809b005e0178fe08a1d57317bffc00b7b4c # v1.332.0
        with:
          ruby-version: "3.3"
      - name: Install ASH
        run: |
          token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
          if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
            echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
          status=0
          {
            uv tool install "${INSTALL_SPEC}" &&
              uv tool dir --bin >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"
          } 2>&1 || status=$?
          printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
          exit "${status}"
      - name: Install scanner tools
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: |
          token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
          if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
            echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
          status=0
          ash dependencies install \
            --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag \
            --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy \
            2>&1 || status=$?
          printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
          exit "${status}"
      - name: Run ASH
        run: |
          token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
          if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
            echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
          status=0
          ash scan --mode local --no-progress \
            --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db \
            2>&1 || status=$?
          printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
          exit "${status}"
      - name: Upload the reports and the results file
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ash-output
          # Not the whole output directory: scanners/ and converted/ hold each
          # tool's raw output, which is not masked.
          path: |
            .ash/ash_output/reports
            .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json
      - name: Upload SARIF to code scanning
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@9b3254085494b55a0f7c4c2b3d2d52cc712ce370 # v4.39.1
        with:
          sarif_file: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.ghas.sarif
          category: ash

Notes on the steps:

  • version: latest installs the newest uv, as the reusable workflow does. Without it, astral-sh/setup-uv installs the uv version that a required-version in a uv.toml or pyproject.toml at the repository root asks for.
  • Install ASH outside the checkout, as uv tool install does. ASH does not run tools it finds inside the directory it scans, so an ASH installed into a virtual environment in the repository loses the scanners that need uv; see Tools inside the scanned directory.
  • Run ash dependencies install outside the checkout too, as working-directory does here, so a config in the repository cannot change what it installs.
  • ASH installs bandit, checkov, and semgrep during the scan with the uv installed with it, or with a uv on PATH.
  • ruby/setup-ruby is there for cfn-nag, which ash dependencies install installs with gem and which builds native extensions.
  • The three gate flags keep a pull request's own config from turning off the gate for findings, incomplete scans, and stale content databases. A branch's config can still raise thresholds, add suppressions, and turn scanners off; to keep those yours, pass --config with a file outside the checkout. See Who can change the gate.
  • if: ${{ !cancelled() }} keeps both uploads running when the scan step fails, which is what it does when it finds something.
  • Each step that runs uv or ash stops workflow commands around it, as the reusable workflow does (How the workflow checks its inputs): it prints ::stop-commands:: with a new random token before the command, sends the command's error output to the same stream, and prints the token on a line of its own after it, so the runner reads workflow commands again once the command ends. The step exits with the command's exit code. Install ASH runs uv tool dir --bin only when uv tool install succeeds. The caching and changed-files steps below do the same.

docs.title: Cache tools and databases
docs.text:
The reusable workflow caches three things:

  • uv's package cache, through astral-sh/setup-uv. It is saved from any push.
  • The opengrep binary, for a week. A restored binary is used only if it hashes to the SHA256 that ASH pins.
  • grype's vulnerability database. The cache key changes daily, and a restored database older than ASH's bound for it (120 hours) is deleted before the scan, so grype downloads a new one.

It restores them on every event except pull_request and merge_group.
