On those two, another job that runs the pull request's code in the same cache scope could have written the entry, so the workflow downloads and checks each one as on a cache miss. Every other tool that the workflow installs, and trivy's database, is downloaded each time. It saves the opengrep binary and grype's database only from a push to the repository's default branch, so pull requests do not each write a copy. A repository that never runs the workflow on such a push never saves those two, and every run downloads them.

In your own steps, cache ASH's tool directory and grype's database. These steps replace the install and scan steps of the job above:

- name: Restore ASH's scanner tools
  id: tools
  uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
  with:
    path: ~/.ash/bin
    key: ash-tools-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-v3.7.0
- name: Install scanner tools
  working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
  run: |
    token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
    if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
      echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
      exit 1
    fi
    printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
    status=0
    ash dependencies install \
      --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag \
      --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy \
      2>&1 || status=$?
    printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
    exit "${status}"
- name: Save ASH's scanner tools
  if: steps.tools.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
  uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
  with:
    path: ~/.ash/bin
    key: ${{ steps.tools.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
- name: Today's date, for the grype database cache key
  id: date
  run: echo "today=$(date -u +%F)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
- name: Restore grype's database
  id: grype-db
  uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/grype/db
    key: grype-db-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.date.outputs.today }}
- name: Run ASH
  run: |
    token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
    if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
      echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
      exit 1
    fi
    printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
    status=0
    ash scan --mode local --no-progress \
      --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db \
      2>&1 || status=$?
    printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
    exit "${status}"
- name: Save grype's database
  if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.grype-db.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
  uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/grype/db
    key: ${{ steps.grype-db.outputs.cache-primary-key }}

Keep ash dependencies install after the restore. It checks each binary it finds against the pinned SHA256, skips the ones that match, and installs again over any that do not, so a restored cache cannot substitute a different tool. Key the tool cache on the ASH version, because each version pins its own tool versions. cfn-nag is the exception: it is a Ruby gem, not a pinned binary, so it is installed again on every run. Cache ~/.ash/bin and nothing else under ~/.ash: ash dependencies install downloads the cfn-guard rules into ~/.ash/share/cfn-guard-rules again on each run, and keeps its install records in ~/.ash/install-receipts.

The save steps are separate because the combined actions/cache action saves only when the job succeeds, and a scan with findings fails the job. Do not add restore-keys to the database cache: a database past its bound only makes grype download a new one.

Do not cache trivy's database. Its bound is 24 hours, and ASH declares it not cacheable in CI. Before each online scan that runs trivy, ASH updates it in $TRIVY_CACHE_DIR, or, when that is not set, in trivy under the user cache directory ($XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache on Linux, ~/Library/Caches on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows), and passes that directory to trivy with trivy --cache-dir. Leave it out of your cache steps.

Content databases explains the bounds and what happens when a database is past one.

docs.title: Scan only the files a pull request changes
docs.text:
--changed-files-only runs every scanner on the whole tree, then keeps only the findings in files changed between the merge base with --base-ref and HEAD. It does not make the scan faster. The filter applies to every report, the summary, and the exit code. Scale to large repositories has the details.

It needs the base branch's history. actions/checkout fetches a single commit unless told otherwise, and without the base ref ASH logs a warning and scans in full. The changed-files-only input of run-ash-security-scan.yml fetches that history itself. It diffs a pull request against its base commit and a merge group against the queue's base commit, and on other events against base-ref. The job fails before the scan when that base is not in the checkout, or names a ref with characters ASH does not accept, rather than scanning in full. In your own steps, fetch the history and name the base branch. These two steps replace the checkout and Run ASH steps of the job in Write the steps yourself:

- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
    persist-credentials: false
- name: Run ASH
  env:
    BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
  run: |
    token="$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
    if [ "${#token}" -ne 32 ]; then
      echo "::error::no random token could be read for stop-commands, so the command did not run"
      exit 1
    fi
    set --
    if [ -n "${BASE_REF}" ]; then
      set -- --changed-files-only --base-ref "origin/${BASE_REF}"
    fi
    printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${token}"
    status=0
    ash scan --mode local --no-progress \
      --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db \
      "$@" \
      2>&1 || status=$?
    printf '\n::%s::\n' "${token}"
    exit "${status}"

github.base_ref is set on a pull request and empty on a push, so the one step filters a pull request to its changed files and scans a push in full, and the SARIF upload has its file on both events.

Code scanning already shows a pull request only the alerts on lines it changed, so for the SARIF upload alone you do not need this option.

docs.title: Run ASH in GitLab CI
docs.text:
This page adds an ASH job to .gitlab-ci.yml that publishes ASH's findings as a GitLab SAST report and its JUnit file as a test report, and a second job that fails the pipeline when ASH found something.

Prerequisites:

  • A runner with the Docker executor, or any runner whose job image is based on Debian or Ubuntu, runs as root, and has Python 3.10 or later and git. The before_script below installs packages with apt-get.
  • Network access from the job to GitHub, PyPI, and the scanners' download sites.

GitLab reads the SAST report on every tier, and offers it as a download. Showing the findings in the merge request widget, the vulnerability report, and the security dashboard needs GitLab Ultimate.

docs.title: Add the jobs
docs.text:
ash-scan:
  stage: test
  image: python:3.12
  variables:
    INSTALL_SPEC: "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
  before_script:
    - apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs npm ruby ruby-dev libyaml-dev
    - python -m venv /opt/ash
    - /opt/ash/bin/pip install --quiet "$INSTALL_SPEC"
    - export PATH="/opt/ash/bin:$PATH"
    - >-
      (cd "$(mktemp -d)" && ash dependencies install
      --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag
      --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy)
  script:
    - ash_exit=0
    - >-
      ash scan --mode local --no-progress
      --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
      || ash_exit=$?
    - echo "$ash_exit" > ash-exit-code.txt
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - .ash/ash_output/reports/
      - .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json
      - ash-exit-code.txt
    reports:
      sast: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.gl-sast-report.json
      junit: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml

ash-gate:
  stage: test
  image: python:3.12
  needs: [ash-scan]
  script:
    - exit "$(cat ash-exit-code.txt)"

Why two jobs: GitLab always uploads report artifacts, but it ingests a security report's findings only when the job that produced it succeeds. A failed job does not count, even with allow_failure. So ash-scan records ASH's exit code and succeeds, and ash-gate reads the code and fails with it: 2 for actionable findings, 1 for a scan that did not complete, 5 for a command line ASH refused. The exit codes page lists them all.

What the before_script does:

  • Installs Node.js and npm, which cdk-nag and npm-audit need when the repository has files they scan, and Ruby with its headers and libyaml, which ash dependencies install needs to build cfn-nag. Without them, those scanners are SKIPPED in a repository with nothing for them to scan, and MISSING in one that has something.
  • Installs ASH into a virtual environment at /opt/ash, outside the checkout. ASH does not run tools it finds inside the directory it scans, and the virtual environment carries the uv that ASH uses to install bandit, checkov, semgrep, cfn-lint, and zizmor during the scan.
  • Installs the binary scanner tools at the versions that ASH pins, checking each download against its pinned SHA256. It runs in an empty directory, so a config in the repository cannot change what it installs.

To skip a scanner instead of installing what it needs, drop it from the install list and name it in --exclude-scanners on ash scan, for example ash scan --mode local --no-progress --exclude-scanners cfn-nag.

A merge request pipeline scans the configuration in the branch it scans, so the branch's author can change the gate. The three gate flags on ash scan keep the branch from turning off the gate for findings, incomplete scans, and stale content databases. The branch's config can still raise thresholds, add suppressions, and turn scanners off; to keep those yours, pass --config with a file outside the checkout. See Who can change the gate.

docs.title: The report files
docs.text:
File in .ash/ash_output/reports/ GitLab keyword What GitLab does with it ash.gl-sast-report.json artifacts:reports:sast SAST findings (schema 15.2.2) ash.junit.xml artifacts:reports:junit Test summary in the merge request and the pipeline's Tests tab, one failed test per actionable finding ash.gl-dependency-scanning-report.cdx.json artifacts:reports:cyclonedx Dependency list (Ultimate); built from syft's SBOM, so it is empty when syft did not run

The SAST report keeps suppressed findings at severity Info, with the reason in their solution field. Export reports shows how to leave them out and how the other formats map to other tools.

--output-formats takes the GitLab reporters' names, gitlab-sast and gitlab-cyclonedx. A list you pass writes only the reports it names, so include them when you set the option. This scan writes the SAST report and the JUnit file and no other report:

ash scan --mode local --no-progress --offline --scanners detect-secrets \
  --output-formats gitlab-sast,junitxml

It exits 2 here because detect-secrets finds a hardcoded password in app.py. Both files are in reports/:

ls .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.gl-sast-report.json .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml

Choose which reports to write lists every format name.

docs.title: Use your own ASH image
docs.text:
Instead of installing ASH in every job, build ASH's container image once, push it to your registry, and use it as the job image. The image has every scanner tool, so the job only runs the scan. Build the ci target, which runs as root like most job images, and see Build and host your own image:

ash-scan:
  stage: test
  image: registry.example.com/security/automated-security-helper:ci
  script:
    - ash_exit=0
    - >-
      ash scan --mode local --no-progress
      --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
      || ash_exit=$?
    - echo "$ash_exit" > ash-exit-code.txt
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - .ash/ash_output/reports/
      - .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json
      - ash-exit-code.txt
    reports:
      sast: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.gl-sast-report.json
      junit: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml

ash-gate:
  stage: test
  image: registry.example.com/security/automated-security-helper:ci
  needs: [ash-scan]
  script:
    - exit "$(cat ash-exit-code.txt)"

ash-gate is the first example's job on this example's image, so the pipeline pulls no other image. The scanners download their vulnerability databases during the scan, as they do in the first example. An image built with OFFLINE=YES carries the databases instead. It holds trivy's database to warn: past trivy's 24-hour bound its scans still pass, and the reports record the stale database. grype's database and the offline rulesets still fail the scan past their bounds, so rebuild the image within them; see Refresh cadence. --no-allow-stale-content-db, as in the job above, holds trivy's database to its bound too. The bound counts from when the database was built upstream, so with that flag scans that include trivy start failing less than a day after the image build.

docs.title: Scan only what a merge request changes
docs.text:
--changed-files-only keeps only the findings in files changed since the merge base with --base-ref. GitLab clones 20 commits by default, which may not reach the merge base, and ASH then scans everything and logs a warning. In a merge request pipeline, clone the full history and pass GitLab's diff base, which is that merge base.

Add this to the ash-scan job, and give ash-gate the same rules:. GitLab does not create a pipeline in which a job's needs: names a job that the rules left out, so with the rule on ash-scan alone, branch pipelines stop starting:

ash-scan:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
  variables:
    GIT_DEPTH: "0"
  script:
    - ash_exit=0
    - >-
      ash scan --mode local --no-progress
      --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
      --changed-files-only --base-ref "$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA"
      || ash_exit=$?
    - echo "$ash_exit" > ash-exit-code.txt

ash-gate:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

Both jobs then run in merge request pipelines only. To scan branch pipelines as well, keep the jobs from the first example under other names, with the opposite rule.

The option filters every report, including ash.gl-sast-report.json and ash.junit.xml, so they list only findings in changed files. On a branch that adds one clean file, the password finding in app.py, a file the branch did not change, is left out:

git switch -q -c add-version
echo 'VERSION = "1.0"' > version.py
git add version.py
git commit -q -m "Add version.py"
ash scan --mode local --no-progress --offline --scanners detect-secrets \
  --changed-files-only --base-ref main

The scan exits 0, and the SAST report lists no vulnerabilities:

python3 -c "import json; report = json.load(open('.ash/ash_output/reports/ash.gl-sast-report.json')); assert not report['vulnerabilities'], report['vulnerabilities']"

Scale to large repositories has the details.

docs.title: Run ASH in Jenkins, CodeBuild, Azure Pipelines, CircleCI, and other CI systems
docs.text: Every CI integration does the same things: install ASH outside the checkout, install the scanner tools, run the scan, keep the reports whatever the exit code, and let the exit code fail the build. This page gives that recipe as plain shell, then shows it in Jenkins, AWS CodeBuild, Azure Pipelines, and CircleCI. GitHub Actions and GitLab CI have their own pages: Run ASH in GitHub Actions and Run ASH in GitLab CI.

docs.title: The recipe
docs.text:
python3 -m venv "$HOME/ash-venv"
"$HOME/ash-venv/bin/pip" install --quiet \
  "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
export PATH="$HOME/ash-venv/bin:$PATH"
(cd "$(mktemp -d)" && ash dependencies install \
  --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag \
  --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy)
ash scan --mode local --no-progress \
  --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db

Run it from the root of the checkout. The reports land in .ash/ash_output/reports/.

  • Keep the virtual environment outside the checkout. ASH does not run tools it finds inside the directory it scans, and the virtual environment's bin holds the uv that ASH uses to install bandit, checkov, semgrep, cfn-lint, and zizmor during the scan; see Tools inside the scanned directory.
  • Run ash dependencies install outside the checkout too, as the empty directory does here, so a config in the repository cannot change what it installs. It downloads the tool versions that this ASH version pins, checks each against its pinned SHA256, and installs it into ~/.ash/bin, where the scan finds it. A binary that is already there and matches is not downloaded again, so ~/.ash/bin is safe to cache between builds. Cache it and nothing else under ~/.ash: the cfn-guard rules in ~/.ash/share/cfn-guard-rules are downloaded again on each run, and ~/.ash/install-receipts holds the install records. Restore the cache with the files' execute bits: ash dependencies install downloads a binary there again if it has lost its execute bit, and a scan run without that step skips it. cfn-nag is the exception: it is a Ruby gem, not a pinned binary, and it is installed again on every run.
  • Install ASH from a git URL as shown. The automated-security-helper name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project; see Install ASH.
  • The three gate flags keep a pull request's or merge request's own config from turning off the gate for findings, incomplete scans, and stale content databases. A branch's config can still raise thresholds, add suppressions, and turn scanners off; to keep those yours, pass --config with a file outside the checkout. See Who can change the gate.

docs.title: What the build host needs
docs.text:
Scanners Needs on the host detect-secrets Nothing; it is part of ASH bandit, checkov, semgrep, cfn-lint, zizmor Access to PyPI during the scan grype, syft, opengrep, actionlint, cfn-guard, gitleaks, trivy The binary, from ash dependencies install cfn-nag Ruby, with the headers and a C compiler to build gems, so that ash dependencies install can install it cdk-nag The cdk extra, which the recipe installs, and Node.js npm-audit Node.js and npm

A scanner whose requirements are missing is reported MISSING when the repository has files it scans, and the scan exits 1. With none, it is SKIPPED, whether or not its tool is installed. In a repository with no npm lockfile, npm-audit is SKIPPED, and this scan exits 2 for the hardcoded password that detect-secrets finds in app.py:

ash scan --mode local --no-progress --offline --scanners detect-secrets --scanners npm-audit

To run without a scanner, name it in --exclude-scanners, for example ash scan --mode local --no-progress --exclude-scanners cfn-nag. Several scanners also use the network during the scan, for their vulnerability databases, rules, or registries; What each scanner does offline lists them.

docs.title: Local mode or container mode
docs.text:
The recipe uses local mode: the scanners run on the build host, which needs the tools above.

Container mode (--mode container) runs the scan inside ASH's container image instead, so the host needs only ASH and a container runtime. In CI that costs time on every build: ASH publishes no image, so each container-mode run on a fresh host builds one, downloading every tool. Two more things differ in CI:

  • A job that runs as root, as AWS CodeBuild and container-based jobs do, needs --build-target ci: ASH refuses to build the non-root image, whose user would get UID 0.
  • --changed-files-only is not supported in container mode: the scan stops with exit code 5 before anything is built or run, also when ASH_CHANGED_FILES_ONLY sets it.

For many repositories, build the image once, push it to your registry, and use it as the build image, running ash scan --mode local inside it. Nothing is installed per build. See Run ASH in a container and Roll out ASH across repositories.

docs.title: Use the exit code as the gate
docs.text:
ASH exits 0 when nothing actionable was found or fail_on_findings is off, 1 when the scan did not complete or was refused, 2 for actionable findings, 3 for a configuration it cannot use or an input it refuses before scanning, such as a linked output directory, 4 for a workspace error, and 5 for a command-line usage error, such as an unknown option or an unknown --output-formats value. When a scan is both incomplete and has findings, it exits 1. Exit codes lists every condition behind each code.

A usage error stops ASH before it scans anything, so a mistyped value cannot pass as a finding or as a clean scan:

ash scan --mode local --no-progress --offline --scanners detect-secrets --min-severity hihg

Fail the build on any non-zero code, and keep the reports when it fails: the build tools below all have a way to do that. The scan itself decides which findings count, from the severity threshold and suppressions; see Set the gate.

docs.title: Jenkins
docs.text:
A declarative pipeline for an agent that has Python 3.10 or later, git, Node.js, npm, and Ruby:

pipeline {
  agent { label 'linux' }
  environment {
    INSTALL_SPEC = 'automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0'
  }
  stages {
    stage('ASH') {
      steps {
        sh '''
          mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tools"
          python3 -m venv "$WORKSPACE_TMP/ash"
          "$WORKSPACE_TMP/ash/bin/pip" install --quiet "$INSTALL_SPEC"
          export PATH="$WORKSPACE_TMP/ash/bin:$PATH"
          (cd "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tools" && ash dependencies install --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy)
          ash scan --mode local --no-progress --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
        '''
      }
    }
  }
  post {
    always {
      junit allowEmptyResults: true, testResults: '.ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml'
      archiveArtifacts allowEmptyArchive: true, artifacts: '.ash/ash_output/reports/**, .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json'
    }
  }
}

WORKSPACE_TMP is a directory next to the workspace, so the virtual environment stays out of the checkout. A non-zero exit from sh fails the stage, and post { always { ... } } publishes the JUnit file and archives the reports anyway. The junit step marks the build unstable when any test failed, and every actionable finding is a failed test.

If you run the stage in a container with agent { docker { ... } }, Jenkins starts the container as the agent's user, not root, so the image has to have the tools already, or the recipe has to install everything under a directory that user can write. Your own ASH image from Build and host your own image has the tools.

docs.title: AWS CodeBuild
docs.text:
A buildspec.yml for a standard Linux image, for example aws/codebuild/amazonlinux-x86_64-standard:5.0, the image ASH's own CDK templates use:

version: 0.2
env:
  variables:
    INSTALL_SPEC: "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
phases:
  install:
    runtime-versions:
      python: 3.12
      nodejs: 22
      ruby: 3.3
    commands:
      - python -m venv /opt/ash
      - /opt/ash/bin/pip install --quiet "$INSTALL_SPEC"
      - export PATH="/opt/ash/bin:$PATH"
      - (cd "$(mktemp -d)" && ash dependencies install --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy)
  build:
    commands:
      - ash scan --mode local --no-progress --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
reports:
  ash-findings:
    base-directory: .ash/ash_output/reports
    files:
      - ash.junit.xml
    file-format: JUNITXML
artifacts:
  base-directory: .ash/ash_output
  files:
    - "**/*"

Name all three runtimes: when runtime-versions lists any, CodeBuild provides only those. Buildspec version 0.2 runs every command in one shell, so the PATH change carries into the build phase. CodeBuild attempts to upload the artifacts even when the build phase fails.

Container mode needs privileged mode on the CodeBuild project, because it runs Docker. Local mode, as above, does not.

docs.title: Azure Pipelines
docs.text:
An azure-pipelines.yml for a Microsoft-hosted Ubuntu agent:

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest
variables:
  INSTALL_SPEC: "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
steps:
  - task: UsePythonVersion@0
    inputs:
      versionSpec: "3.12"
  - script: |
      sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ruby-dev libyaml-dev
      python -m venv "$(Agent.TempDirectory)/ash"
      "$(Agent.TempDirectory)/ash/bin/pip" install --quiet "$INSTALL_SPEC"
      echo "##vso[task.prependpath]$(Agent.TempDirectory)/ash/bin"
    displayName: Install ASH
  - script: ash dependencies install --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy
    workingDirectory: $(Agent.TempDirectory)
    displayName: Install scanner tools
  - script: ash scan --mode local --no-progress --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
    displayName: Run ASH
  - task: PublishTestResults@2
    condition: succeededOrFailed()
    inputs:
      testResultsFormat: JUnit
      testResultsFiles: .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml
  - script: |
      mkdir -p "$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/sarif"
      cp .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif "$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/sarif/"
    condition: succeededOrFailed()
    displayName: Stage the SARIF report
  - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
    condition: succeededOrFailed()
    inputs:
      targetPath: $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)/sarif
      artifact: CodeAnalysisLogs
  - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
    condition: succeededOrFailed()
    inputs:
      targetPath: .ash/ash_output
      artifact: ash-output
  • succeededOrFailed() runs the publishing steps after a failed scan, and skips them when the run is canceled.
  • workingDirectory runs ash dependencies install outside the checkout.
  • The JUnit file appears in the run's Tests tab.
  • The artifact named CodeAnalysisLogs is the one the free SARIF SAST Scans Tab extension from Microsoft DevLabs reads. With the extension installed in your organization, the run shows the SARIF findings in a tab of its own.
  • The apt-get line adds the Ruby headers and libyaml that building cfn-nag's gems needs.

docs.title: CircleCI
docs.text:
A .circleci/config.yml for CircleCI's Docker executor:

version: 2.1
jobs:
  ash-scan:
    docker:
      - image: cimg/python:3.12-node
    environment:
      INSTALL_SPEC: "automated-security-helper[cdk] @ git+https://github.com/awslabs/automated-security-helper.git@v3.7.0"
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run:
          name: Install ASH
          command: |
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ruby ruby-dev libyaml-dev
            python3 -m venv "$HOME/ash-venv"
            "$HOME/ash-venv/bin/pip" install --quiet "$INSTALL_SPEC"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/ash-venv/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
      - restore_cache:
          key: ash-tools-v3.7.0-{{ arch }}
      - run:
          name: Install scanner tools
          command: (cd "$(mktemp -d)" && ash dependencies install --tool grype --tool syft --tool opengrep --tool cfn-nag --tool actionlint --tool cfn-guard --tool gitleaks --tool trivy)
      - save_cache:
          key: ash-tools-v3.7.0-{{ arch }}
          paths:
            - ~/.ash/bin
      - run:
          name: Run ASH
          command: ash scan --mode local --no-progress --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db
      - run:
          name: Copy the JUnit file out of .ash
          when: always
          command: |
            mkdir -p /tmp/ash-test-results
            if [ -f .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml ]; then cp .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.junit.xml /tmp/ash-test-results/; fi
      - store_test_results:
          path: /tmp/ash-test-results
      - store_artifacts:
          path: .ash/ash_output/reports
          destination: ash-output/reports
      - store_artifacts:
          path: .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json
          destination: ash-output/ash_aggregated_results.json
workflows:
  ash:
    jobs:
      - ash-scan
  • cimg/python:3.12-node is CircleCI's Python image with Node.js added. The apt-get line adds Ruby, its headers, and libyaml, which building cfn-nag's gems needs. The image already has a C compiler.
  • Each run step starts a new shell. The line that appends to $BASH_ENV puts the virtual environment's bin on PATH for every later step. The virtual environment is in the home directory, outside the checkout in ~/project.
  • save_cache comes before the scan because, by default, it runs only when every step before it succeeded, and a scan with findings fails its step. CircleCI never overwrites a saved key, so key the cache on the ASH version, as above: each version pins its own tool versions.
  • Keep ash dependencies install after restore_cache. Pull requests from a fork share a cache with the repository's own builds, so a restored cache may have been written by another branch. ash dependencies install checks each binary against its pinned SHA256 and installs again any that does not match, so a restored cache cannot substitute a different tool. Because that check needs no install record, the cache holds ~/.ash/bin and nothing else: the records in ~/.ash/install-receipts hold the SHA256 each installed tool is checked against, so a cache a fork's pull request can write must not carry them. cfn-nag, and the cfn-guard rules in ~/.ash/share/cfn-guard-rules, are installed again on every run.
  • A non-zero exit from ash scan fails its step and the job. store_test_results and store_artifacts run after a failed step, so the JUnit file appears in the job's Tests tab, one failed test per actionable finding, and .ash/ash_output/reports/ and .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json are kept as the job's artifacts. Neither runs when the job is canceled or times out.
  • CircleCI's test results path must not be a hidden directory, and .ash is one, so the step before store_test_results copies the JUnit file out of it. Its when: always runs it after a failed scan.

docs.title: Generic shell
docs.text:
Any other CI service, or a cron job, runs the recipe as a shell step. Make the step that archives .ash/ash_output/ run after a failed scan, and pass the scan's exit code through to the build result:

ash_exit=0
ash scan --mode local --no-progress \
  --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db \
  || ash_exit=$?
tar -czf ash-output.tar.gz .ash/ash_output
exit "$ash_exit"

The same step with one scanner that needs no network runs anywhere. In a project whose app.py holds a hardcoded password, detect-secrets reports it, the archive is written, and the step exits 2:

ash_exit=0
ash scan --mode local --no-progress --offline --scanners detect-secrets \
  --fail-on-findings --fail-on-incomplete-scanners --no-allow-stale-content-db \
  || ash_exit=$?
tar -czf ash-output.tar.gz .ash/ash_output
exit "$ash_exit"

docs.title: Examples in the repository
docs.text:
• .github/workflows/ash-repo-scan.yml is how ASH scans itself with its reusable workflows, and uses their current inputs. Its sarif job's if: has no status function, so that job is skipped when the scan fails; Upload SARIF shows the condition to use instead.
  • examples/GitHubActions/ash-repo-scan.yml calls the reusable workflow at the floating v3 tag, with ash-version: v3, and uploads SARIF from the scan job on pull requests only. To pin a release, upload SARIF on every event, and install every default scanner's tool, follow Run ASH in GitHub Actions.
  • examples/AWSCodeBuild/ installs the ASH release it ships in and scans in container mode, which needs privileged mode on the CodeBuild project. The buildspec above scans in local mode instead.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: ASH's converters, scanners, and reporters are plugins, and so are event subscribers. Converters turn files that scanners cannot read, such as archives and notebooks, into files they can. Scanners run a security tool and return its findings as SARIF. Reporters turn the aggregated results into report files. Event subscribers are functions that ASH calls when something happens during a scan, such as a scanner finishing. How ASH works explains where each kind runs.

docs.title: Where plugins come from
docs.text:
Source Loaded What it provides Built in: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_builtin on every run the default scanners, reporters, and converters, and two event subscribers, listed in the scanner, reporter, and converter references Plugin modules that ship with ASH, under automated_security_helper.plugin_modules when a module list names them (for the MCP server, see What a plugin can do) the community plugins (ferret-scan, snyk-code, and trivy-repo) and the AWS reporters Third-party packages when a module list names them anything you or someone else writes, installed in the same Python environment as ASH

ASH has no automatic discovery. Installing a package does nothing until a module list names it, and ash scan imports none of the optional modules that ship with ASH unless a module list names them.

docs.title: Load a plugin module
docs.text:
Name the module in any of these:

  • the ash_plugin_modules list in an ASH config file (reference);
  • the --ash-plugin-modules option of ash scan and ash plugin list, repeated once per module or given names separated by commas;
  • the ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES environment variable, with module names separated by spaces or commas, which ash scan and ash plugin list read;
  • a config override, --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=[module.name]', which also works for ash dependencies install and ash report, the commands that have no --ash-plugin-modules option;
  • the ash_plugin_modules parameter of the Python API.

This config loads the ferret-scan plugin module:

project_name: my-service
ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

To check what a module provides before you scan with it, list the plugins with the module loaded. ferret-scan then appears in the scanners table:

ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins

The plugins in the modules that ship with ASH are enabled as soon as their module is loaded, so loading one adds its scanners to a default scan; set enabled: false for a plugin in your config to turn it off. The exceptions are the four AWS reporters, which stay off until the operator turns each one on (AWS reporters). A third-party plugin's config class sets its own default. ASH imports the names from every source together, in order, and a name given twice is imported once. Every source splits an entry on commas, so "a_ash_plugins, b_ash_plugins" names two modules. This lists the scanners of two community modules named in one value:

ash plugin list \
  --ash-plugin-modules "automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins, automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_trivy_plugins" \
  | grep -E -o "ferret-scan|trivy-repo" | sort -u

ferret-scan
trivy-repo

ash plugin list lists every plugin registered once the modules are imported, which is the set a scan selects from.

docs.title: Who may load a module
docs.text:
ASH sorts configuration by who controls it, as the Configuration trust model describes, and module loading follows the same tiers:

  • You, the operator, may name any plugin module, wherever it is installed: with --ash-plugin-modules, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES, --config-overrides, a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory, or the Python API.
  • A config file inside a git checkout or the scanned directory (a repository's own .ash/.ash.yaml, for example, or a config kept in an ops repository), or a file an MCP client delivered, may add only ASH's own plugin modules and modules installed outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. A third-party package in a virtual environment inside a checkout counts as inside it. Such a file may never add ash_aws_plugins or ash_snyk_plugins, or any module inside either, such as automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins.s3_reporter, because their plugins send findings or the scanned source to a remote service with your credentials.

Every source, yours included, is held to ASH's plugin namespace: a module path that starts with automated_security_helper. or ash_plugins, or whose top-level package ends in _ash_plugins. A name outside it, ASH's plugin root itself, a namespace package, or a name that is not a dotted path of Python identifiers stops the scan with exit code 3 before anything is scanned, whatever its source, and so does a module you name that fails to import. A scan uses only the modules it names.

From a repository's file, ASH drops every entry it cannot find or will not import, names them in one warning, and runs the scan without them. For a module installed inside a checkout, the warning says where Python found it and which checkout it is in. ASH checks where each module is without importing it, so a dropped entry runs no code. To load a dropped module anyway, name it from an operator source, or install it outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. Under its default policy, the MCP server refuses a delivered config whose ash_plugin_modules list has such an entry instead of dropping it (What a delivered config cannot set).

docs.title: What a plugin can do
docs.text:
A plugin is Python code that ASH imports into its own process. It runs as the same user as ASH, with the same files, environment variables, and credentials, and its import-time code runs as soon as a module list names it, before any scanner starts. The scanner sandbox (Enable the scanner sandbox) confines the tool processes that ASH starts on a scanner's behalf; it does not confine the plugin's own Python code, or a process the plugin starts by other means. Only install plugin packages you trust, and pin their versions as you would any other dependency of your build.

Plugins stay registered for the life of the process that loaded them. In a long-running process such as the MCP server that ash mcp starts, do not rely on module lists to keep out a plugin that ships with ASH or is installed in its environment. Give that process only the scanner tools and credentials you are willing to let every scan in it use, and start a new process when you change which plugin modules it loads.

docs.title: Package a third-party plugin
docs.text:
• Give the top-level package a name that ends in ash_plugins, such as acme_ash_plugins; ASH also accepts names under ash_plugins.. Other names are not supported, and ASH logs a warning for them.
  • Decorate each plugin class (@ash_scanner_plugin, @ash_reporter_plugin, or @ash_converter_plugin). The decorator registers the class when ASH imports the module, and ash plugin list shows every registered plugin. The module-level lists at the end of each how-to's module register nothing and are optional.

  • Give each plugin a config class whose name is a fixed string. That name is the key under scanners, reporters, or converters in an ASH config, and the name that --scanners and ash report --format select. Put the plugin's options in a class derived from the options base for its kind; ASH checks a config's section for the plugin with that class and refuses an option it does not declare (Write a scanner plugin). ASH finds the section by the name with case, punctuation, and the words Scanner, Reporter, and Converter ignored, so give the plugin a name of its own: two plugins of one type whose names read as one that way would read each other's section, and are refused with exit 3, naming both plugins and the modules that define them: a scan and a workspace scan refuse two such scanners, converters, or reporters, and ash report and ash merge refuse two such reporters. A reporter named csv_ is refused this way beside the built-in csv, and one named S3 when the AWS reporters, among them s3, are loaded. ash config validate imports no plugin module, so it does not see this. Two plugins of one type with the very same name, such as a subclass that keeps its base's config, are refused with exit 3 too, naming both classes and the modules that define them: a scan and a workspace scan refuse two such scanners, converters, or reporters, and ash report and ash merge refuse two such reporters. One class selected twice is one plugin. To run a subclass beside its base, give it a config class of its own with its own name, declare it as the subclass's config field, and build it in model_post_init when no config is given. A reporter subclass also needs its own extension; a different extension under the shared name is not enough. Two reporters with names of their own that write one report file are refused with exit 1 by a scan, a workspace scan, and ash merge, and without the model_post_init the subclass starts from its base's config and writes its base's file. This reporter runs beside the built-in csv and writes ash.copy.csv:

    from typing import Literal

from automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_builtin.reporters.csv_reporter import (
    CSVReporterConfig,
    CsvReporter,
)
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin


class CopyCsvConfig(CSVReporterConfig):
    name: Literal["csv-copy"] = "csv-copy"
    extension: str = "copy.csv"


@ash_reporter_plugin
class CopyCsvReporter(CsvReporter):
    config: CopyCsvConfig | None = None

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = CopyCsvConfig()
        super().model_post_init(context)

  • Install the package into the Python environment that runs ASH. In container mode ASH passes the module names into the container, but the image does not contain third-party packages, so a third-party plugin needs an image you build with it installed (Run ASH in a container).

docs.title: Write a plugin
docs.text:
• Write a scanner plugin wraps a command-line tool that writes SARIF.
  • Write a reporter plugin writes a report file from the aggregated results.
  • Write a converter plugin prepares files for the scanners.
  • Subscribe to scan events runs a function when a scanner or the whole scan finishes.

Each how-to builds a complete plugin in a package named acme_ash_plugins and runs it with ash scan.

docs.title: AWS reporters
docs.text:
The ash_aws_plugins package that ships with ASH has four reporters that send scan data to AWS services. Each one is off until an operator loads the package and turns that reporter on, and only an operator can choose where they send data and which credentials they use.

Reporter Sends to What leaves the machine s3 An S3 bucket The scan summary and the resolved ASH configuration cloudwatch-logs A CloudWatch Logs log group The same summary and configuration bedrock-summary-reporter Amazon Bedrock Finding messages, file paths, and severity counts aws-security-hub AWS Security Hub Nothing yet: the reporter checks its connection and writes a placeholder file (details)

The S3 and CloudWatch Logs reporters do not send individual findings. To collect findings centrally, copy a findings file such as reports/ash.ocsf.json or reports/ash.sarif to your storage yourself (Export reports).

docs.title: Load the package
docs.text:
Loading the package turns none of the reporters on: each one runs only when the operator sets enabled: true in its section. A section that sets a reporter's options but leaves enabled out, or sets it to anything but the boolean true, such as the string "true", leaves the reporter off, and ASH logs a warning that says so, unless --output-formats or output_formats leaves that reporter out anyway. Name the package in one of these places, all of which belong to the operator:

  • --ash-plugin-modules automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
  • ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES=automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
  • --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules=[automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins]'
  • ash_plugin_modules in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory (Configuration trust model)

When a config file inside any git checkout or the scanned directory names the package, or a module inside it, ASH drops that entry, logs a warning that says why, and runs the scan without it. Under its default policy, the MCP server refuses a config an MCP client delivered whose ash_plugin_modules list names it; in any other case it drops the entry the same way.

For ash scan, turn on the reporters you use in the same operator config. This one sends to S3 and CloudWatch Logs only:

ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
reporters:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: us-west-2
      bucket_name: example-security-scan-results
      key_prefix: ash-reports/
  cloudwatch-logs:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: us-west-2
      log_group_name: /security/ash

Only the operator can turn these reporters on or off, with --config-overrides, such as --config-overrides 'reporters.s3.enabled=true', or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. A config file inside any git checkout or the scanned directory, an ops repository of your own included, turns none of them on or off: each keeps the operator's enabled, or its own default where the operator sets none, and a different value in the file is ignored with a warning (Configuration trust model). For a repository's own config that sets reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled: true, the warning reads:

Ignoring reporters.aws-security-hub.enabled from /home/me/repo/.ash/.ash.yaml: that config is inside a git checkout or the scanned tree, or was delivered by an MCP client, and these options choose whether findings are sent, where they are sent or written, and which credentials send them. To keep a setting, move the file outside every git checkout, or pass the setting with --config-overrides. A file inside the scanned directory has to move out of it as well.

Under its default policy, the MCP server refuses a delivered config that turns one of these reporters on.

All of this is how ash scan reads the reporters' settings. ash report and ash merge take whether these reporters run, and where they send, from --config-overrides only, and ignore those settings in any config file (Rendering a reporter from saved results).

A repository's own config file can still set the reporters' options that are not operator-only (below) when a scan reads it. If you load the package with --ash-plugin-modules and let ASH read the repository's config, the repository can change those options of your reporters. Pass your config with --config to prevent that; in a scan of one directory, ASH then does not read the repository's config file.

In a scan, a reporter that has no credentials, or fails its pre-flight call, is dropped from the run without changing the exit code. An enabled reporter that is missing a setting it needs does not run either, and ASH logs an error that names the setting and how to set it, once per run for each reporter and setting: the bucket for S3, the log group for CloudWatch Logs, and the region (aws_region, else AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION) for S3, CloudWatch Logs, and Security Hub. A run is one ash scan, ash report, or ash merge, and a workspace run gives each error once for all its projects. Bedrock's region defaults to us-east-1, so it has no region only when a config sets aws_region to null. For S3 with no region set:

ERROR    Reporter 's3' is enabled but does not run: no aws_region is set. Set it with --config-overrides reporters.s3.options.aws_region=<value>, or set AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION in the environment, which is read only when no config sets aws_region.

The exit code does not change, so check after each run that reports/ash.s3.json and reports/ash.cwlog.json exist. A scan with --output-formats runs only the reporters it names, so name the AWS reporters in that list too, as in --output-formats sarif,s3.

docs.title: Destinations and credentials
docs.text:
These options choose where data goes, with which identity, what the Bedrock reporter sends. ASH takes them only from operator sources: the defaults below, an operator config file, or --config-overrides. ash report and ash merge take them from the defaults and --config-overrides only.

The operator-only options of s3:

Option Default aws_region from AWS_REGION, else from AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else null aws_profile from AWS_PROFILE, else null bucket_name from ASH_S3_BUCKET_NAME, else null key_prefix ash-reports/

Of cloudwatch-logs:

Option Default aws_region from AWS_REGION, else from AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else null log_group_name from ASH_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_NAME, else null log_stream_name ASHScanResults

Of bedrock-summary-reporter:

Option Default aws_region from AWS_REGION, else from AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else us-east-1 aws_profile from AWS_PROFILE, else null model_id from ASH_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, else us.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0 output_file ash.bedrock.summary.md output_executive_file bedrock-executive.md output_technical_file bedrock-technical.md include_code_snippets false custom_prompt null

Of aws-security-hub:

Option Default aws_region from AWS_REGION, else from AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, else null aws_profile from AWS_PROFILE, else null account_id null

With no account_id, the Security Hub reporter uses the account of its credentials. Turning a reporter on, enabled, is the operator's too (above).

When a config file inside any git checkout or the scanned directory sets one of these options, under any spelling of the reporter's section, ASH ignores it, logs a warning that names the option, and uses the operator's value. Under an MCP server's default policy, a delivered config that sets any option of these four reporters to a value other than the server's is refused.

Credentials come from the AWS SDK's default chain: environment variables, the shared config and credentials files (with aws_profile where the reporter has it), and the container or instance role. cloudwatch-logs has no profile option. Bedrock's region falls back to us-east-1, so with only ambient credentials and no region set, the Bedrock reporter still sends data.

In container mode, the scan runs inside the container, and the host's credential files and credential variables, such as AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, are not passed in (Run ASH in a container). AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, and AWS_PROFILE are passed in only when your own config file reads them and they are set (The config file). A role the container can reach through the instance metadata service may still be used; use --offline, or a network that blocks the metadata service, if that matters.

docs.title: What each reporter sends
docs.text: The S3, CloudWatch Logs, and Bedrock reporters first call sts:GetCallerIdentity, which needs no IAM permission. The Security Hub reporter calls it in its pre-flight check when account_id is not set.

docs.title: s3
docs.text:
Uploads one object per scan to <key_prefix>ash-report-<generated_at>.json (in workspace mode <key_prefix><project>/ash-report-<generated_at>.json), or .yaml with file_format: yaml. The object holds the scan summary: the report metadata and summary counts, each scanner's and converter's status and finding counts, and the resolved ASH configuration, which includes your suppressions and ignore paths. In the configuration and the metadata, a value or key a config file read from the environment is the reference the file wrote (Read values from the environment). It holds no individual findings.

Before the upload it calls HeadBucket. Locally it writes the uploaded content to reports/s3-report.json and a receipt with the object URL to reports/ash.s3.json. When ASH cannot write the local copy, the receipt's local_copy is null, ASH logs a warning, and the upload still counts.

IAM: s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/<key_prefix>*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket, which HeadBucket requires.

docs.title: cloudwatch-logs
docs.text:
Sends one log event per scan with the same summary and configuration as the S3 object, to the stream log_stream_name in log_group_name. It creates the stream if needed; the log group must already exist. Locally it writes the event and the API response to reports/ash.cwlog.json.

IAM: logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents on the log group.

docs.title: bedrock-summary-reporter
docs.text:
Asks a Bedrock model, through the Converse API, for an executive summary, a risk assessment, recommendations, and a technical analysis, and writes them to reports/ash.bedrock.summary.md, reports/bedrock-executive.md, and reports/bedrock-technical.md. output_file, output_executive_file, and output_technical_file change those names, and must be plain file names in reports/: ASH does not write a file whose name leads anywhere else, and logs a warning. A test scan of a small project with one finding made six Converse calls; more severity levels in the results mean more calls.

The prompts contain the names of every scanner in the results, severity counts, and, for each finding sent, its level, its message text, and its file paths. Line numbers are sent where a scanner's message includes them. With actionable_only (default true) the reporter sends only actionable findings: those that are not suppressed and whose severity is at or above the threshold of the scanner that reported them. In a scan of one directory those are the findings the exit code counts; a workspace verdict uses one threshold per project, so there the two can differ. With actionable_only: false it sends every finding, suppressed ones included. It sends a sample of them: up to max_findings_to_analyze (default 10) per request and up to max_findings_per_severity (default 5) per severity. With batch_processing: true and group_by_severity: false it sends every actionable finding, in batches. custom_prompt, custom_context, industry_context, and compliance_frameworks are added to the prompts. The Finding Details section at the end of the summary lists every finding; ASH writes it from the results, not from the model's answer.

Findings from secret scanners are sent with the others: the type of secret, the file and, in the message, the line. Source code is sent only with include_code_snippets: true; leave it off when the scanned code may hold credentials.

The reporter sends every request to model_id. Set it to a model or inference profile your role can invoke in that Region.

IAM: bedrock:ListFoundationModels and bedrock:ListInferenceProfiles, which it calls to check the model, and bedrock:InvokeModel, which the Converse API requires. The default model is a cross-Region inference profile, so allow bedrock:InvokeModel on the inference profile and on the foundation model in each Region the profile routes to, as the Bedrock inference profile prerequisites describe.

docs.title: aws-security-hub
docs.text:
The reporter is off until the operator turns it on. Security Hub must be enabled in the account and Region you name. In the operator's config file:

ash_plugin_modules:
  - automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins
reporters:
  aws-security-hub:
    enabled: true
    options:
      aws_region: us-east-1

This version of the reporter does not import findings yet. Its pre-flight check needs the Region, calls DescribeHub, and calls sts:GetCallerIdentity when account_id is not set; when one fails, ASH logs an error and the reporter does not run. When the checks pass, report() logs a warning that the Security Hub import is not implemented, sends nothing to Security Hub, and writes a placeholder file, reports/ash.aws-security-hub.asff.json, that holds a message and the number of findings in the results. In a workspace scan the reporter runs once per project.

IAM: securityhub:DescribeHub.

docs.title: Rendering a reporter from saved results
docs.text:
ash report --format s3, or the name of any of the other three, runs that reporter against the results of a previous scan, which sends the data again. Stored results do not record which tree was scanned, so a config file ash report reads could be the scanned repository's own, even one outside every git checkout. So ash report takes whether the reporter runs, and its destination options, from --config-overrides only:

ash report --format s3 \
  --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=[automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins]' \
  --config-overrides reporters.s3.enabled=true \
  --config-overrides reporters.s3.options.bucket_name=my-bucket

The config file that --config or ASH_CONFIG names still applies its other settings. Its enabled and destination options for these reporters are ignored with a warning, and a reporter that --config-overrides does not turn on is refused with exit code 1. With the same settings in a file, ash report --format s3 --config /etc/ash/ash.yaml sends nothing and prints:

WARNING  Ignoring reporters.s3.options.aws_region, reporters.s3.options.bucket_name, reporters.s3.enabled from /etc/ash/ash.yaml: ash report cannot tell that config from the scanned repository's own, since stored results do not record which tree was scanned, and these options choose whether findings are sent, where they are sent or written, and which credentials send them. To send findings off the host from ash report, pass each of these settings with --config-overrides instead.
Error: reporter 's3' sends findings off the host and is not enabled. ash report takes whether it runs, and where it sends, from --config-overrides: pass --config-overrides reporters.s3.enabled=true and its destination options.

ash merge holds its --config file to the same rule, since the shards do not record the tree either: the merged findings go off the host only with the reporter's enabled and destination options in ash merge's --config-overrides, and the file's values are ignored with the same warning, naming ash merge. A reporter a plugin module adds is held the same way for the options it declares as destinations. ash merge has these reporters only when the package is named for the merge itself, in its --config file's ash_plugin_modules or with --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=[automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins]': a package that only the shards' scan loaded is not loaded. It runs them only when --output-formats is not given.

ash report runs the reporter's pre-flight check first, as a scan does. When the check refuses, for a missing setting or for credentials it cannot find, the reporter sends nothing, and ash report logs the reason and exits 1. For S3 with no region set:

ERROR    Reporter 's3' is enabled but does not run: no aws_region is set. Set it with --config-overrides reporters.s3.options.aws_region=<value>, or set AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION in the environment, which is read only when no config sets aws_region.
Error: reporter 's3' cannot run: its dependency check refused. See the log above for the reason.

ash report has no --ash-plugin-modules option and does not read ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES, and without --config it reads the config file of the directory you run it from. Run it from outside the repository, and load the package with your config file (--config) or with --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=[automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_aws_plugins]'.

docs.title: Example IAM policy
docs.text:
A policy for the configuration above (S3 and CloudWatch Logs only), with your account, bucket, and log group:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "s3:PutObject",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-security-scan-results/ash-reports/*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "s3:ListBucket",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::example-security-scan-results"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["logs:CreateLogStream", "logs:PutLogEvents"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:logs:us-west-2:111122223333:log-group:/security/ash:*"
    }
  ]
}

Each reporter's full option list is in the reporters reference.

docs.title: Subscribe to scan events
docs.text:
An event subscriber is a function that ASH calls at a point in a scan: when a phase starts, when a scanner finishes, or when the whole scan ends. Use one to log progress somewhere ASH does not, to time scans, or to start work that depends on a scanner's result. This page builds a module with two subscribers, one that prints a line as each scanner finishes and one that prints the scan's duration at the end.

Prerequisites:

  • ASH installed (Install ASH);
  • a repository to scan, with your shell in its top directory. To keep the steps short, this page saves the module in an ash-plugins directory there; a module you keep belongs outside the repositories you scan (Package a third-party plugin).

Plugins explains how ASH loads plugin modules and what a loaded module can do.

docs.title: 1. Write the subscribers
docs.text:
Save this as ash-plugins/acme_ash_plugins/__init__.py:

from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import event_subscriber
from automated_security_helper.plugins.events import AshEventType


@event_subscriber(AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE)
def scanner_finished(**kwargs):
    print(f"acme: {kwargs['scanner']} finished, {kwargs['remaining_count']} left")


@event_subscriber(AshEventType.EXECUTION_COMPLETE)
def run_finished(**kwargs):
    print(f"acme: run finished in {kwargs['duration']:.1f} s")

docs.title: 2. Scan with them
docs.text:
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/ash-plugins"
ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners detect-secrets --offline

Among the scan's output are the two lines the subscribers print:

acme: detect-secrets finished, 0 left
acme: run finished in 0.9 s

ash plugin list does not show event subscribers.

docs.title: How subscribing works
docs.text:
@event_subscriber(event_type) subscribes the function when ASH imports the module, which happens when a module list names it (Load a plugin module). ASH calls each subscriber with keyword arguments only, so declare **kwargs and read the arguments you need; the table below lists them. Return values are ignored. Subscribing the same function to the same event twice has no effect.

A module can instead list its subscribers in a dict at module level, which ASH reads when it loads a module from a module list:

from automated_security_helper.plugins.events import AshEventType


def scanner_finished(**kwargs):
    print(kwargs["scanner"])


ASH_EVENT_HANDLERS = {AshEventType.SCAN_COMPLETE: [scanner_finished]}

Subscribers to one event run in the order they were subscribed. The order between modules is not fixed, so do not make one module's subscriber depend on another's.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
EXECUTION_START comes before the first phase and EXECUTION_COMPLETE after the last. Phases run in the order convert, scan, report, and inspect; each emits its _PHASE_START event, then its per-plugin events, then its _PHASE_COMPLETE event. Events emitted during a phase also receive phase and plugin_context.

Event When Keyword arguments EXECUTION_START once, before the first phase phases, plugin_context, source_dir, output_dir, enabled_scanners, excluded_scanners, python_based_plugins_only, strategy, message CONVERT_PHASE_START, SCAN_PHASE_START, REPORT_PHASE_START, INSPECT_PHASE_START when each phase starts; inspect runs only with --inspect the scan phase adds enabled_scanners, excluded_scanners, parallel, max_workers, global_ignore_paths, shard_index, and shard_count; the report phase adds report_dir and cli_output_formats CONVERT_START before each converter runs converter, converter_class, message CONVERT_COMPLETE after each converter that did not raise the same, plus converted_files and file_count SCAN_START before each scanner, when scanners run one at a time: with --strategy sequential, or when only one scanner runs scanner, scanner_class, scan_targets, message SCAN_COMPLETE after each scanner, including one that failed scanner, completed_count, total_count, remaining_count, remaining_scanners, message REPORT_START before each reporter reporter, reporter_class, message REPORT_COMPLETE after each reporter that returned a string; when the string was empty, no file was written, and output_file and output_filename are None the same, plus output_file and output_filename CONVERT_PHASE_COMPLETE, SCAN_PHASE_COMPLETE, REPORT_PHASE_COMPLETE, INSPECT_PHASE_COMPLETE when each phase ends the phase's start arguments, plus results EXECUTION_COMPLETE once, at the end, also when the scan failed phases, results, duration (seconds), completed_scanners, message ERROR, WARNING, INFO when ASH records a problem or a validation checkpoint message, and details that depend on the source

AshEventType also has EXECUTION_PROGRESS, CONVERT_PHASE_PROGRESS, SCAN_PHASE_PROGRESS, REPORT_PHASE_PROGRESS, INSPECT_PHASE_PROGRESS, INSPECT_START, and INSPECT_COMPLETE. ASH never emits them. When two or more scanners run under the default parallel strategy, SCAN_START is not emitted either; use SCAN_PHASE_START to learn which scanners will run.

docs.title: When a subscriber fails
docs.text:
A subscriber runs in ASH's own process, in the thread that emitted the event, and ASH waits for it before it continues. Keep subscribers fast: one that calls a network service delays the scan by that call.

If a subscriber raises an exception, the subscribers after it for that event do not run. What else happens depends on the event:

  • For a _PHASE_START or _PHASE_COMPLETE event, the scan stops. It exits with code 1 and writes no reports.
  • For any other event, ASH logs the error and the scan continues.

Catch exceptions inside your subscriber unless you mean it to stop the scan.

docs.title: Built-in subscribers
docs.text: ASH subscribes two functions of its own. At SCAN_COMPLETE one logs which scanners are still running, as in Scanner bandit completed. 2 remaining: semgrep, checkov, and All scanners completed! after the last one. At EXECUTION_START the other checks the expiration dates in the config (Expiration). It logs, in this order, one warning that names every suppression and ignore path that has already expired, one that expires today included; a warning for the ignore paths that expire within the next 30 days; and a warning for the suppressions that do. Under --ignore-suppressions it leaves the suppressions out of these warnings and still names the ignore paths.

docs.title: Write a converter plugin
docs.text:
A converter runs before the scanners and writes files they can read. ASH's own converters extract archives and turn Jupyter notebooks into Python. This page builds markdown-python, a converter that copies the Python code blocks out of Markdown files so that Python scanners check the code in your documentation too. It keeps each line at its original line number, so a finding in the converted file points at the same line of the Markdown file.

Prerequisites:

  • ASH installed (Install ASH);
  • a repository to scan, with your shell in its top directory. To keep the steps short, this page saves the plugin package in an ash-plugins directory there; a plugin you keep belongs outside the repositories you scan (Package a third-party plugin).

Plugins explains how ASH loads plugin packages and what a loaded plugin can do.

docs.title: 1. Write the plugin
docs.text:
Save this as ash-plugins/acme_ash_plugins/__init__.py:

import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Literal

from automated_security_helper.base.converter_plugin import (
    ConverterPluginBase,
    ConverterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.models.core import ignore_paths_that_skip_scanning
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_converter_plugin
from automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set import scan_set
from automated_security_helper.utils.scanned_tree import TreeInputRefused
from automated_security_helper.utils.suppression_matcher import file_path_matches

FENCE_OPEN = re.compile(r"^\s*```(python|py)\s*$")
FENCE_CLOSE = re.compile(r"^\s*```\s*$")


class MarkdownPythonConfig(ConverterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["markdown-python"] = "markdown-python"
    enabled: bool = True


@ash_converter_plugin
class MarkdownPythonConverter(ConverterPluginBase[MarkdownPythonConfig]):
    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = MarkdownPythonConfig()
        super().model_post_init(context)

    def _inputs(self) -> List[Path]:
        ignored = ignore_paths_that_skip_scanning(
            self.context.config.global_settings.ignore_paths,
            ignore_suppressions=self.context.ignore_suppressions,
        )
        inputs = []
        for name in scan_set(
            source=self.context.source_dir, output=self.context.output_dir
        ):
            path = Path(name.strip())
            relative = path.relative_to(self.context.source_dir).as_posix()
            if path.suffix == ".md" and not any(
                file_path_matches(relative, ignore.path) for ignore in ignored
            ):
                inputs.append(path)
        return inputs

    def convert(self) -> List[Path]:
        written = []
        for path in self._inputs():
            try:
                with self.open_source_file(path) as handle:
                    text = handle.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            except TreeInputRefused as refusal:
                self.record_refused_input(refusal)
                continue
            # Keep every line, blanking the ones outside python fences, so a
            # finding's line number is the same in the Markdown file.
            lines, inside, found = [], False, False
            for line in text.splitlines():
                if inside and FENCE_CLOSE.match(line):
                    inside = False
                    lines.append("")
                elif not inside and FENCE_OPEN.match(line):
                    inside = found = True
                    lines.append("")
                else:
                    lines.append(line if inside else "")
            if not found:
                continue
            relative = path.relative_to(self.context.source_dir)
            target = self.results_dir / relative.with_name(relative.name + ".py")
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            written.append(target)
        return written


ASH_CONVERTERS = [MarkdownPythonConverter]

docs.title: 2. Check that ASH finds it
docs.text:
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/ash-plugins"
ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins

The converters table has a row for the plugin:

│ markdown-python │ True    │ MarkdownPython… │ acme_ash_plug… │               │

docs.title: 3. Scan with it
docs.text:
Save this as docs/usage.md in the repository. It has a Python example at lines 5 to 8:

# Usage

Call it like this:

```python
import subprocess
subprocess.call(user_input, shell=True)
```

Run a scan with the module loaded:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners detect-secrets --offline

The scan exits with code 2 for the hardcoded password in app.py. List what the converter wrote:

ls .ash/ash_output/converted/markdown-python/docs

The converter wrote usage.md.py, which has the two lines of code at lines 6 and 7 and blank lines everywhere else. ASH passes the directory of converted files to every scanner as a second target, after the source directory. This scan ran only detect-secrets, which needs no download, so it shows the conversion but no finding in the converted file. A Python scanner, such as bandit or the ruff-security scanner from Write a scanner plugin, reports the shell=True call at .ash/ash_output/converted/markdown-python/docs/usage.md.py, line 7. bandit reports it once, from the converted target: on its run over the source directory, ASH tells it to skip ASH's output directory.

docs.title: How ASH runs a converter
docs.text:
ASH runs the converters in the convert phase, before any scanner. It constructs each enabled converter and calls its convert() with no arguments, once per scan. The converter finds its own inputs and returns the list of files it wrote.

The base class, ConverterPluginBase, declares the method as convert(self), as ASH's own converters define it. A convert() that requires one parameter, such as convert(self, target), still runs: ASH passes the source directory as that parameter and logs a warning that asks for convert(self). A convert() that requires more than one parameter, or is declared async, fails with an error that says to declare def convert(self), and the converter counts as failed.

Inside convert():

  • Find inputs with scan_set(source=..., output=...) from automated_security_helper.utils.get_scan_set. It returns the files ASH scans: the files under the source directory that the repository's .gitignore and .ignore files do not exclude. ASH's output directories are left out: the scan's output directory and .ash/ash_output under the source directory and under the working directory. In a git checkout, the files git tracks in those directories stay in the scan set.
  • Skip the inputs that global_settings.ignore_paths covers, as the example does with ignore_paths_that_skip_scanning and file_path_matches. ASH removes findings under an ignored path after the scan by matching the finding's path, and a converted file's path is under .ash/ash_output/converted/, so findings in a converted copy of an ignored file would otherwise be reported. ignore_paths_that_skip_scanning leaves out the ignore paths an MCP client supplied, which ASH reports as suppressed findings instead of skipping. An ignore path stops applying on its expiration date, and its files are scanned again; active_ignore_paths from automated_security_helper.utils.suppression_matcher returns the entries that still apply, and ASH's own converters skip only those.
  • Read each input through self.open_source_file(path), not open(). It refuses a symbolic link or a path outside the source directory by raising TreeInputRefused. Pass that to self.record_refused_input(), which logs a warning and lists the input in the converter's results.
  • Write output only under self.results_dir, which is .ash/ash_output/converted/<name>/. Every file you write there is scanned, whether or not you return it, as long as at least one name under .ash/ash_output/converted/ has an extension, such as .py; if none does, ASH does not scan the converted directory at all.
  • Return a list of the paths you wrote. An empty list means there was nothing to convert.

How a converter's problems affect the scan:

What happens Result convert(), or the constructor, raises an exception the converter is recorded as failed and the scan exits with code 1, because some files were not given to the scanners you call self.record_failed_input(path, reason) for an input you could not convert the input is listed in the results, the error is logged, and the scan exits with code 1 for the same reason an input is refused and recorded with record_refused_input() the input is listed in the results; the exit code is unaffected

The exit code 1 for lost coverage comes from fail_on_incomplete_scanners, which is on by default (Set the gate). The results row for each converter is under converter_results in .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json.

docs.title: A converter that needs a tool
docs.text: If your converter runs a program, override validate_plugin_dependencies() to return False when the program is not available; ASH then skips the converter. Also override candidate_input_count() to return how many inputs the converter would have converted, counted without the tool. When a converter that is skipped this way had inputs, ASH treats the scan as incomplete; when it had none, the skip costs nothing. A converter that does not override candidate_input_count() counts as having had inputs.

docs.title: Converted files in the results
docs.text: Findings in converted files point at the converted file under .ash/ash_output/converted/, not at the original. ASH drops the findings a scanner reports in its output directories, except those in the converted files and in files git tracks there, and it does not deduplicate findings. So a scanner that walks the whole source directory and does not skip ASH's output directory, which is inside the source directory by default, can report a converted file twice, once under each target.

docs.title: Write a reporter plugin
docs.text:
This page builds findings-list, a reporter plugin that writes ash.findings.txt: the number of actionable findings, then one line per finding with its scanner, rule, and location. A reporter receives the aggregated results after every scanner has run and returns the text of its report; ASH writes the file.

Prerequisites:

  • ASH installed (Install ASH);
  • a repository to scan, with your shell in its top directory. To keep the steps short, this page saves the plugin package in an ash-plugins directory there; a plugin you keep belongs outside the repositories you scan (Package a third-party plugin).

Plugins explains how ASH loads plugin packages and what a loaded plugin can do.

docs.title: 1. Write the plugin
docs.text:
Save this as ash-plugins/acme_ash_plugins/__init__.py:

from typing import Literal

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ReporterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin import (
    ReporterPluginBase,
    ReporterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin


class FindingsListOptions(ReporterOptionsBase):
    include_suppressed: bool = False


class FindingsListConfig(ReporterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["findings-list"] = "findings-list"
    extension: str = "findings.txt"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: FindingsListOptions = FindingsListOptions()


@ash_reporter_plugin
class FindingsListReporter(ReporterPluginBase[FindingsListConfig]):
    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = FindingsListConfig()
        super().model_post_init(context)

    def report(self, model: AshAggregatedResults) -> str:
        stats = model.metadata.summary_stats
        lines = [f"{stats.actionable} actionable, {stats.total} total"]
        for finding in model.to_flat_vulnerabilities():
            if finding.is_suppressed and not self.config.options.include_suppressed:
                continue
