            lines.append(
                f"{finding.scanner}\t{finding.rule_id}\t"
                f"{finding.file_path}:{finding.line_start}"
            )
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


ASH_REPORTERS = [FindingsListReporter]

docs.title: 2. Check that ASH finds it
docs.text:
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/ash-plugins"
ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins

The reporters table has a row for the plugin:

│ findings-list   │ True    │ FindingsListRe… │ acme_ash_plug… │               │

docs.title: 3. Scan with it
docs.text:
A loaded reporter runs in every scan, beside the built-in ones. This scan uses only detect-secrets, which needs no download:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners detect-secrets --offline

In a repository with one hardcoded password, the scan exits with code 2. Read the report:

cat .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.findings.txt

It reads:

1 actionable, 1 total
detect-secrets  SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD   app.py:3

To see the report again from the last scan's results without scanning, use ash report, which takes the module through a config override. It prints the report to the terminal and writes no file:

ash report --format findings-list --config-overrides 'ash_plugin_modules+=[acme_ash_plugins]'

ash scan --output-formats and the output_formats config key cannot select this reporter: they accept only the names of the reporters that ship with ASH, and when either names any, only the reporters it names run. --output-formats refuses the name of another reporter as a usage error, with exit code 5, and the config key refuses it as an invalid configuration, with exit code 3:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners detect-secrets --offline \
  --output-formats findings-list

The reporter's options go under its name, findings-list, in the reporters section of an ASH config, where enabled: false leaves it out of a scan:

project_name: my-service
ash_plugin_modules: [acme_ash_plugins]
reporters:
  findings-list:
    enabled: true
    options:
      include_suppressed: true

ASH checks that section with FindingsListOptions once it has loaded the module, before anything is scanned: an option the class does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the configuration with exit code 3, as for a scanner plugin (Write a scanner plugin).

docs.title: What ASH does with the return value
docs.text:
ASH calls report(model) once per scan, in the report phase, and handles what it returns:

report() Result returns a non-empty string ASH writes it to .ash/ash_output/reports/ash.<extension>, replacing any file there returns None an error is logged and no file is written returns an empty string a warning is logged and no file is written raises an exception the error is logged and the other reporters still run

None of these changes the scan's exit code, which is decided by the findings and by whether the scan was complete.

Set extension in the config class. It is the end of the file name, so it must be a plain suffix such as findings.txt: a value with /, \, or .., from any config, is replaced by the default with a warning, and a reporter with no extension writes ash.txt. To write a second file beside the report, call write_report_file(report_dir, filename, content) from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin with report_dir set to Path(self.context.output_dir) / "reports". It writes only inside that directory and does not follow a symbolic link at the file name.

docs.title: Read the results model
docs.text:
model is an AshAggregatedResults, the same data as .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json (Output files). The parts a reporter usually needs:

  • model.metadata.summary_stats: actionable, total (findings not suppressed), and severity_counts with critical, high, medium, low, info, and suppressed;
  • model.to_flat_vulnerabilities(): one flat record per finding, with scanner, rule_id, severity, file_path, line_start, line_end, description, and is_suppressed. The flat severity is the severity the summary and the gate use (Set the severity);
  • model.sarif: the aggregated SARIF, one run with every scanner's results;
  • model.scanner_results: the outcome of each scanner, with status (PASSED, FAILED, MISSING, SKIPPED, or ERROR) and finding_count.

docs.title: Test the reporter
docs.text:
A reporter is a class, so a test can build it, give it a results model, and check the text it returns. This test builds FindingsListReporter and gives it a model with no findings, so the report is the header line alone. The package from step 1 is not installed, so the test imports it by name. Run pytest with PYTHONPATH set as in step 2:

import importlib
from pathlib import Path

from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context import PluginContext
from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults


def test_findings_list_reporter():
    plugin = importlib.import_module("acme_ash_plugins")
    context = PluginContext(source_dir=Path("."), output_dir=Path("out"))
    reporter = plugin.FindingsListReporter(context=context)

    report = reporter.report(AshAggregatedResults())

    assert report == "0 actionable, 0 total\n"

docs.title: A reporter that sends findings somewhere
docs.text:
The plugin from step 1 writes a local report. A reporter can also send the results elsewhere. This one uploads them to an S3 bucket and returns the object's s3:// URL, which ASH writes as the report. Its region, profile, and bucket default to values from the environment of the process that runs ASH, and validate_plugin_dependencies() checks that it can reach the bucket before the scan uses it. Add it to the package from step 1, and list FindingsBucketReporter in the reporter list of __init__.py beside FindingsListReporter:

import json
import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import ClassVar, Literal, Optional, Tuple

import boto3

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ReporterOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.reporter_plugin import (
    ReporterPluginBase,
    ReporterPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.models.asharp_model import AshAggregatedResults
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_reporter_plugin
from automated_security_helper.utils.log import ASH_LOGGER


class FindingsBucketOptions(ReporterOptionsBase):
    aws_region: Optional[str] = os.environ.get("AWS_REGION")
    aws_profile: Optional[str] = os.environ.get("AWS_PROFILE")
    bucket_name: Optional[str] = os.environ.get("ACME_FINDINGS_BUCKET")
    key_prefix: str = "ash-reports/"


class FindingsBucketConfig(ReporterPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["findings-bucket"] = "findings-bucket"
    extension: str = "bucket.txt"
    enabled: bool = False
    options: FindingsBucketOptions = FindingsBucketOptions()


@ash_reporter_plugin
class FindingsBucketReporter(ReporterPluginBase[FindingsBucketConfig]):
    destination_options: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (
        "aws_region",
        "aws_profile",
        "bucket_name",
        "key_prefix",
    )

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = FindingsBucketConfig()
        super().model_post_init(context)

    def validate_plugin_dependencies(self) -> bool:
        options = self.config.options
        self.dependencies_satisfied = False
        if options.aws_region is None or options.bucket_name is None:
            return self.dependencies_satisfied
        try:
            session = boto3.Session(
                profile_name=options.aws_profile, region_name=options.aws_region
            )
            caller = session.client("sts").get_caller_identity()
            session.client("s3").head_bucket(Bucket=options.bucket_name)
            self.dependencies_satisfied = "Account" in caller
        except Exception as error:
            self._plugin_log(
                f"Cannot reach the bucket {options.bucket_name}: {error}",
                level=logging.WARNING,
                append_to_stream="stderr",
            )
        return self.dependencies_satisfied

    def report(self, model: AshAggregatedResults) -> str | None:
        options = self.config.options
        stamp = model.metadata.generated_at or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(
            timespec="seconds"
        )
        key = f"{options.key_prefix}ash-report-{stamp}.json"
        body = json.dumps(model.to_simple_dict(), default=str, indent=2)
        try:
            session = boto3.Session(
                profile_name=options.aws_profile, region_name=options.aws_region
            )
            session.client("s3").put_object(
                Bucket=options.bucket_name,
                Key=key,
                Body=body,
                ContentType="application/json",
            )
        except Exception as error:
            self._plugin_log(
                f"Error uploading to S3: {error}",
                level=logging.ERROR,
                append_to_stream="stderr",
            )
            return None
        url = f"s3://{options.bucket_name}/{key}"
        ASH_LOGGER.info(f"Uploaded the report to {url}")
        return url

validate_plugin_dependencies() returns False when the region or bucket is missing, or when an AWS call fails, and ASH skips the reporter. report() returns None when the upload fails, so ASH logs an error and writes no file (What ASH does with the return value). Each failure is also logged with _plugin_log, which takes a number from logging as its level, such as logging.ERROR. A string such as "ERROR" raises TypeError.

docs.title: Declare the destination options
docs.text:
A reporter that sends findings somewhere, or writes them to a path its options name, declares those options in destination_options, as FindingsBucketReporter does. List every option that chooses where findings are sent or written, or which credentials send them: an endpoint, a region, an account, a bucket, a profile, a token, an output path. Name each as its field in the options model. An alias of the field is covered as well. The default is ().

When the config was built from a file inside the scanned tree (a discovered .ash/.ash.yaml, a --config inside the tree, an extends base, or ASH_CONFIG), or from a file an MCP client delivered, ASH takes these options from the trusted base instead: the defaults, an operator config outside the tree, and --config-overrides. A value such a file set is replaced, under any spelling of the reporter's section that ASH reads as this reporter's, and one warning names each option it ignored. The reporter's other options still apply from the file. ASH does this once it has imported your plugin module and before it builds any reporter, in a scan and in ash report. The built-in AWS reporters declare theirs the same way (Configuration trust model).

A reporter that declares any destination option sends findings somewhere, so whether it runs is the operator's choice too, in both directions. Its enabled comes from the trusted base, or from the default of your config model's enabled when the trusted base sets none: such a file's enabled: true or enabled: false is replaced with a warning where it differs, and leaving the section out leaves the reporter as the trusted base has it. That is why FindingsBucketConfig sets enabled to False. A reporter that declares no destination options writes only local files, and its enabled applies from the file.

Under the MCP server, a delivered file that sets a declared option is scanned with the server's value rather than refused, because the server checks the file against denied_paths before it imports your plugin module. To have such a file refused, add the option to the profile's global_settings.mcp.runtime_overrides.denied_paths, for example /reporters/findings-bucket/options/bucket_name.

docs.title: A destination that is not an option
docs.text:
A destination the reporter reads itself, and not from its options, has to come from a source the scanned repository cannot write, such as an environment variable of the process that runs ASH:

import os


def endpoint_from_operator():
    """The endpoint the operator set for this run, or None when there is none."""
    return os.environ.get("ACME_FINDINGS_ENDPOINT") or None

A repository that names an endpoint in its .ash/.ash.yaml then changes nothing. A reporter that makes network calls also runs in the ASH process, outside the scanner sandbox, so it can reach any host ASH can.

docs.title: Workspace scans
docs.text: In a workspace scan (ash scan --workspace), ASH asks each reporter what to do with several projects through its workspace_behaviour class variable. The default, ReporterWorkspaceBehaviour.PER_PROJECT, writes the report once per project, under each project's own output directory, and no workspace-level file. Set MERGED only if your reporter handles results with one SARIF run per project. Scale to large repositories covers workspace scans.

docs.title: Write a scanner plugin
docs.text:
This page builds ruff-security, a scanner plugin that runs ruff's security rules (the S rules, ported from flake8-bandit) and gives ASH the SARIF file ruff writes. The same pattern fits any command-line tool that can write SARIF.

Prerequisites:

  • ASH installed (Install ASH);
  • ruff on your PATH (ruff --version prints a version);
  • a repository to scan, with your shell in its top directory. To keep the steps short, this page saves the plugin package in an ash-plugins directory there; a plugin you keep belongs outside the repositories you scan (Package a third-party plugin).

Plugins explains how ASH loads plugin packages and what a loaded plugin can do.

docs.title: 1. Write the plugin
docs.text:
Save this as ash-plugins/acme_ash_plugins/__init__.py:

from typing import Literal

from automated_security_helper.base.options import ScannerOptionsBase
from automated_security_helper.base.scanner_plugin import (
    ScannerPluginBase,
    ScannerPluginConfigBase,
)
from automated_security_helper.core.enums import ScannerToolType
from automated_security_helper.plugins.decorators import ash_scanner_plugin


class RuffSecurityOptions(ScannerOptionsBase):
    select: str = "S"


class RuffSecurityConfig(ScannerPluginConfigBase):
    name: Literal["ruff-security"] = "ruff-security"
    enabled: bool = True
    options: RuffSecurityOptions = RuffSecurityOptions()


@ash_scanner_plugin
class RuffSecurityScanner(ScannerPluginBase[RuffSecurityConfig]):
    command: str = "ruff"
    tool_type: ScannerToolType = ScannerToolType.SAST

    def model_post_init(self, context):
        if self.config is None:
            self.config = RuffSecurityConfig()
        super().model_post_init(context)

    def _execute_scan(self, target, target_type, global_ignore_paths):
        results_file = self.results_dir / target_type / "ruff.sarif"
        results_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args = [
            self.command,
            "check",
            "--isolated",
            "--no-cache",
            "--select",
            self.config.options.select,
            "--output-format",
            "sarif",
            "--output-file",
            results_file.as_posix(),
        ]
        for output_dir in self._ash_output_dirs_inside(target):
            args += ["--extend-exclude", (target / output_dir).as_posix()]
        args.append(target.as_posix())
        return args, results_file, None


ASH_SCANNERS = [RuffSecurityScanner]

docs.title: 2. Check that ASH finds it
docs.text:
Put ash-plugins on Python's import path, then list the plugins with the module loaded:

export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/ash-plugins"
ash plugin list --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins

The scanners table has a row for the plugin:

│ ruff-security  │ True    │ RuffSecuritySc… │ acme_ash_plugi… │               │

docs.title: 3. Scan with it
docs.text:
In the same shell:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners ruff-security

ASH runs ruff, reads its SARIF, and adds a row to the summary. In a repository with a hardcoded password and a subprocess call with shell=True, ruff reports both, the scanner is FAILED, and the scan exits with code 2:

┃ Scanner        ┃ S ┃ C ┃ H ┃ M ┃ L ┃ I ┃ Time ┃ Action ┃ Result  ┃ Thresh  ┃
│ ruff-security  │ 0 │ 2 │ 0 │ 0 │ 0 │ 0 │ 46ms │ 2      │ FAILED  │ MED (g) │

The findings are in the finding reports under .ash/ash_output/reports/, such as ash.sarif, ash.html, and ash.csv, and ruff's own SARIF file is in .ash/ash_output/scanners/ruff-security/source/. Read scan results explains the output directory.

To load the plugin on every scan instead of passing the option, add it to an ASH config file. A repository's own config may name it only while the package is installed outside every git checkout and the scanned directory (Configuration trust model), which ash-plugins inside the repository is not; until you install it elsewhere, use this in a config file outside every git checkout, passed with --config:

project_name: my-service
ash_plugin_modules: [acme_ash_plugins]
scanners:
  ruff-security:
    options:
      select: "S,B"

ASH checks the options of every section a loaded plugin reads with the plugin's own options model, once it has loaded the plugins and before it converts or scans anything. An option the model does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the configuration with exit code 3, and the message names the section and the key:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners ruff-security \
  --config-overrides 'scanners.ruff-security.options.selct=S,B'

ERROR (3) Invalid configuration: Configuration validation failed: scanners.ruff-security.options
(scanner 'ruff-security'): Value error, Unknown key 'selct' (did you mean 'select'?) in these plugin
options. Accepted keys: offline, scan_timeout, select, severity_threshold.

ash config validate and ash config lint do not import the modules in ash_plugin_modules, so they cannot check these options; ash config lint names each section it could not check.

docs.title: How ASH runs a scanner
docs.text:
Before the scan, ASH looks for command: on PATH, then in ASH's bin directory (~/.ash/bin, or the directory ASH_BIN_PATH names), then in the Python environment that runs ASH (its interpreter's directory and its scripts directory), then in /usr/local/bin, except on Windows. It refuses a copy inside the scanned tree unless the operator passed --allow-in-tree-tools. If the tool is not found, the scanner is MISSING, which fails the scan unless incomplete scans are allowed (Set the gate). A scanner that picks its own inputs out of the scan set, as cfn-nag picks CloudFormation templates, can override nothing_to_scan_reason() to return why it has nothing to scan in this run, from the same selection its scan makes; with a reason, a scanner whose tool is not found is SKIPPED instead of MISSING. The default, None, keeps MISSING.

ASH then calls _execute_scan(target, target_type, global_ignore_paths) once with the source directory (target_type is source) and, if converters produced files, once more with the directory that holds them (converted). Your method returns three things: the command line, the path of the SARIF file the tool will write, and the environment for the tool (None to inherit ASH's). For each call, ASH:

  1. runs the command in the source directory, with the scanner's scan_timeout (default 1800 seconds), and inside the scanner sandbox when one is enabled;
  2. reads the SARIF file. A missing file, or one with content that is not JSON, makes the scanner ERROR. An empty file is read as a report with no findings, and the scanner is PASSED, with a warning, whatever the tool's exit code, so do not let the tool create its output file before it has results. A JSON file that is not valid SARIF is logged as a warning, and the scanner is also recorded as PASSED with no findings, so check that your tool writes SARIF. The tool's exit code does not decide the outcome: it is recorded in the SARIF invocation, as successful when it is in success_exit_codes (0 and 1 by default);
  3. adds the command line and timing to the SARIF, makes paths relative to the source directory, drops the results located in ASH's output directories (apart from the converted files and the files git tracks there), applies ignore_paths and suppressions, and merges the results into the aggregated SARIF.

A scanner with findings at or above its threshold is FAILED; one without is PASSED.

Run the tool only by returning its command from _execute_scan. A process you start with subprocess yourself gets none of this: ASH does not check where its program is, does not time it out, and does not sandbox it.

docs.title: Parts of the plugin
docs.text: Part What it does The config class name is the scanner's name: the key under scanners in an ASH config, the value --scanners takes, and the directory under .ash/ash_output/scanners/. Options go in a subclass of ScannerOptionsBase, which already has severity_threshold, scan_timeout, and offline. An option the model does not declare refuses the configuration (above). model_post_init ASH constructs the scanner with no config when the ASH config has no section for it, and the base class refuses an empty config, so set the default before calling super(). command and tool_type command is the program the default dependency check looks for; tool_type labels the findings (SAST, SCA, SECRETS, IAC, and others). self.results_dir A directory for this scanner's files, .ash/ash_output/scanners/<name>/. Write the tool's output under it, one subdirectory per target_type. self._ash_output_dirs_inside(target) ASH writes its output under the source directory by default. ASH leaves its own files there out of the scan set and drops the results a scanner reports in them, but a tool that walks the whole directory still reads ASH's earlier reports and converted files, so pass each of these paths to the tool's exclude option. They are ASH's output directories inside target, relative to it: this run's output directory and an earlier run's .ash/ash_output, less those that hold files git tracks, which ASH scans. The list is empty for the converted target. ruff check --isolated ruff, like many tools, reads its configuration from files in the repository it checks, which would let the repository turn off the rules you selected, so pass the tool's option for ignoring those files. If your plugin takes an option that names a file the tool reads as configuration, use operator_path from automated_security_helper.utils.config_trust, the check ASH's own scanners use, which accepts the value only when the operator set it and the file is outside the scanned tree. The module-level list Optional. The decorator registers the class, and ash plugin list shows every registered plugin, listed or not.

docs.title: Declare what the scanner needs under the sandbox
docs.text:
Under --sandbox, a scanner gets the strictest policy unless it declares more: no network, no extra read paths, and no environment beyond the sandbox's allowlist (Scanner sandbox). ruff-security needs nothing more, so it declares nothing. A scanner whose tool downloads a rule pack into a cache would add a sandbox_requirements class attribute, or a property when the need depends on the scanner's options:

from typing import ClassVar

from automated_security_helper.utils.sandbox.policy import SandboxRequirements

sandbox_requirements: ClassVar[SandboxRequirements] = SandboxRequirements(
    network=True,
    cache_paths=("~/.cache/acme-rules",),
    cache_env=("ACME_CACHE_DIR",),
    env_prefixes=("ACME_",),
)

network asks for a network on online scans, read_paths for read-only host paths, and cache_paths for cache directories the tool keeps. Those are writable through a throwaway overlay under bwrap, where bwrap and the kernel support one, and read-only everywhere else, so a tool that has to write its cache also needs cache_env: variables that move the cache, which ASH points at a private, empty directory wherever cache_paths are read-only. env_prefixes and env_names are for environment variables. A variable whose name marks it as a credential passes only when env_names names it exactly.

If the read paths or environment variables come from the scanner's own options, which the scanned repository can write, also set read_paths_require_grant=True or env_requires_grant=True. The sandbox then mounts those paths only for a scanner named in sandbox.read_path_scanners, and only when a path resolves inside the source tree or an extra_read_paths entry and is a regular file or a directory. It passes those variables only to a scanner named in sandbox.env_scanners, and with read_paths_require_grant it never mounts the scanner's cache_paths. Only the operator can set those lists (Give a scanner more access).

docs.title: Declare whether the scanner is Python-only
docs.text:
ash scan --python-only runs only the scanners that need nothing but Python, and records every other scanner SKIPPED without looking for its tool. A scanner says which it is with the python_only class variable. True puts it in a --python-only run, False keeps it out, and a scanner that declares nothing (None) counts as Python-only only when it runs its tool through uv (use_uv_tool). ruff-security runs the ruff program from PATH and declares nothing, so a --python-only run leaves it out. With no other scanner selected, that scan ran no scanner, and it exits with code 1:

ash scan --ash-plugin-modules acme_ash_plugins --scanners ruff-security --python-only

A scanner that does its work in ASH's own process, such as the one in A scanner with no external tool, declares True in its class body; one that runs a binary, Node.js, or anything else that is not a Python package declares False:

from typing import ClassVar

python_only: ClassVar[bool] = True

docs.title: Set the severity
docs.text:
ASH takes a finding's severity from, in order: the result's properties.issue_severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or INFO); the security-severity score in its rule's properties; or its SARIF level, where error counts as critical, warning as medium, note as low, and none as info. A result with no level counts as medium: SARIF's default level is warning. The summary counts, the gate, and the finding reports read the severity this way. ruff marks every result error, so both findings above count as critical. To report them as HIGH, add this method to RuffSecurityScanner and import PropertyBag at the top of the module:

from automated_security_helper.schemas.sarif_schema_model import PropertyBag


def _post_process_sarif(self, sarif_report, final_args, target):
    for run in sarif_report.runs:
        for result in run.results or []:
            if result.properties is None:
                result.properties = PropertyBag()
            result.properties.issue_severity = "HIGH"
    return sarif_report

ASH calls _post_process_sarif after reading the SARIF file. The other hooks you can override are _process_config_options (turn options into arguments before the scan), _read_results_file (parse a file that is not SARIF JSON), and validate_plugin_dependencies (a different availability check; call super() from it to keep the in-tree tool refusal and its MISSING reason).

docs.title: Test the plugin
docs.text: ASH constructs a plugin with keyword arguments, context and config, so a unit test can do the same and call the method ASH calls. Build a PluginContext (from automated_security_helper.base.plugin_context) whose source_dir holds the files to scan, an output_dir, and a config such as AshConfig(project_name="scanner-test") (from automated_security_helper.config.ash_config). Then RuffSecurityScanner(context=context).scan(target=context.source_dir, target_type="source") runs ruff and returns the SarifReport read from its output, with one result per finding, before ASH makes paths relative and applies suppressions.

docs.title: Logging from threads your plugin starts
docs.text:
Each scan logs to its own ash.log. ASH knows which scan a line belongs to from the context the line is logged in, and ASH's own scanner threads carry that context. A thread your plugin starts with threading.Thread, or a task it submits to a ThreadPoolExecutor, starts in an empty context, so its lines belong to no scan. A CLI scan's ash.log still takes them, because that scan is the process's only one. The MCP server runs several sessions' scans in one process, so it puts such lines in no scan's ash.log, only in the server's own log (stderr, at the level the server was started with — its own log-level option, INFO when not given; quiet and simple name no logging level, so with either it is ASH_LOG_LEVEL, or WARNING when that is unset — when the server has no handler of its own on that logger). So start every thread your plugin makes with ash_thread: when the MCP server runs your plugin, a line from a thread without the scan's context never reaches the scan's ash.log.

Under ash scan, a line no handler takes reaches stderr at the scan's console level: its flags first, then ASH_DEBUG or ASH_VERBOSE, then INFO, and ERROR for --quiet and --simple unless --verbose or --debug is also given. --log-level INFO reads as the default, so it does not override ASH_DEBUG or ASH_VERBOSE; every other --log-level does. ASH_LOG_LEVEL does not change it there; under the MCP server it is the fallback for quiet and simple.

Start the thread with ash_thread, which runs the target in a copy of the scan's context, and submit to an executor through a copy the same way:

import contextvars
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from automated_security_helper.utils.log import ASH_LOGGER
from automated_security_helper.utils.threads import ash_thread


def check_one(path):
    ASH_LOGGER.info("checked %s", path)


worker = ash_thread(check_one, args=("app.py",), name="my-plugin-worker")
worker.start()
worker.join()

with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as pool:
    pool.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, check_one, "lib.py").result()

ash_thread takes the copy when it makes the thread, so make it in your scanner's own code (inside scan()), not at import time. It returns the thread unstarted, as threading.Thread does.

docs.title: A scanner with no external tool
docs.text: A scanner that does its work in Python overrides scan() instead of _execute_scan(), and must still define _execute_scan, which is abstract, as a stub that raises NotImplementedError. Declare python_only: ClassVar[bool] = True on it (above). ASH calls scan(target=..., target_type=...) once for the source directory and, when a converter wrote files, once more for the converted files, with target_type set to converted. scan() must return a SarifReport (from automated_security_helper.schemas.sarif_schema_model) for its findings to reach the reports. Return False if the scanner cannot run, which reports it MISSING; so does any other empty value, such as []. Returning None reports it ERROR. Any other value, including a dictionary of findings, is recorded as PASSED with no findings, so do not catch an exception and return something else: let it propagate, and ASH reports the scanner as ERROR. Read files from the scan set with open_in_scanned_tree from automated_security_helper.utils.scanned_tree, which refuses links and paths outside the source directory. The scanner of the example plugin package in the ASH repository, examples/ash_plugins_example/my_ash_plugins/scanner.py, overrides scan() and returns a SarifReport, and a test in the repository runs it through a scan.

docs.text:
These pages list every command, setting and plugin ASH has. Most are generated from the code by a script under scripts/, and CI fails when a generated page no longer matches the code, so they are current for the branch the site is built from. Each generated page names its generator at the top.

To regenerate a page after changing the code, run its script with uv run python, for example uv run python scripts/generate_cli_docs.py. The documentation guide explains how the generated pages and the docs checks fit together.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
This page is generated from the command definitions in the ASH source code by scripts/generate_cli_docs.py. Edits made to this file by hand are overwritten the next time it is generated.

The Environment variable column names the variable click reads for the option; an option given on the command line takes precedence over it. Some behavior is also controlled by variables read elsewhere in the code; see Environment variables.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description ash Automated Security Helper · one workflow for your security scanners. ash build-image Builds the ASH container image, then scans the current directory with it unless --no-run is given. ash config ASH configuration management ash config get Print the resolved configuration: the file's settings over the defaults. ash config init Create a configuration file with every setting at its default. ash config lint Lint an ASH configuration file for issues and optionally auto-fix them. ash config update Update an existing configuration file with the specified modifications. ash config validate Validate an ASH configuration file the way a scan loads it. ash config validate-plugin-dependencies Check that the configuration resolves and names a project. ash config wizard Interactive configuration wizard. ash dependencies Install dependencies for ASH plugins ash dependencies install Install dependencies for ASH plugins. ash get-genai-guide Write the ASH GenAI Integration Guide for AI assistants and LLMs to a file. ash inspect Inspect and analyze ASH outputs and reports ash inspect findings The inspect findings command provides an interactive TUI to explore the findings and identify actions to quickly take. ash inspect sarif-fields The inspect sarif-fields command analyzes SARIF reports to understand field usage across different scanners and ensure fields are preserved during aggregation. ash mcp Start the ASH MCP server (Model Context Protocol) ash merge Merges the results of a sharded scan into one unified report. ash plugin Manage ASH plugins ash plugin list The plugin list command lists all available plugins. ash report Generate a report from ASH scan results using the specified reporter plugin. ash scan Scan code, infrastructure, secrets, and dependencies.

docs.title: ash
docs.text:
Automated Security Helper · one workflow for your security scanners.

ash [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Run with no command, ash runs a scan. It accepts these options of ash scan, with the same types, defaults and environment variables: --source-dir, --output-dir, --scanners, --exclude-scanners, --ash-plugin-modules, --config-overrides, --offline, --sandbox, --offline-semgrep-rulesets, --strategy, --progress, --output-formats, --cleanup, --phases, --inspect, --use-existing, --version, --mode, --python-only, --show-summary, --quiet, --log-level, --config, --verbose, --debug, --color, --fail-on-findings, --fail-on-incomplete-scanners, --allow-stale-content-db, --simple, --ignore-suppressions, --honor-ignore-files, --min-severity, --compact-report, --changed-files-only, --base-ref, --allow-in-tree-tools, --shard-index, --shard-count, --config-from-scanned-repository, --config-file-from-scanned-repository, --config-file-from-another-checkout, --ash-config-from-host, --workspace, --workspace-config, --allow-missing-projects, --dry-run, --build, --run, --force, --oci-runner, --build-target, --container-uid, --container-gid, --ash-revision-to-install, --custom-containerfile, --custom-build-arg.

Options that only ash itself accepts:

Option Type Default Environment variable Description --install-completion flag off Install completion for the current shell. --show-completion flag off Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation.

docs.title: ash build-image
docs.text:
Builds the ASH container image, then scans the current directory with it unless --no-run is given.

It takes only the options below. To scan with scan options, run ash scan --mode container, which builds the image the same way and accepts every scan option.

ash build-image [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --no-build flag off Skip building the ASH container image; reuse an existing image if present --no-run flag off Build the ASH container image but do not run a scan --force, -f flag off Force rebuild of the ASH container image --oci-runner, --oci, --runner, -r text not set OCI_RUNNER Use the specified OCI runner instead of docker to run the containerized tools. To prefix every OCI command with a wrapper (e.g. sudo), set the OCI_RUNNER_WRAPPER environment variable instead of using this option (e.g. OCI_RUNNER_WRAPPER=sudo ash ...). --container-network text bridge Docker network mode for the container run (e.g. 'bridge', 'none', 'host'). Pass 'none' to force offline/airgapped network isolation independently of --offline. --build-target one of non-root, ci not set The ASH image stage to build: 'non-root' (an unprivileged user, the default) or 'ci' (root, the default on Windows). CI environment variables do not change it. --offline-semgrep-rulesets text p/ci Specify Semgrep rulesets for use in ASH offline mode --container-uid, -u text not set UID to use for the container user --container-gid, -g text not set GID to use for the container user --ash-revision-to-install text not set ASH branch, tag or full commit id to install in the container image for usage during containerized scans --custom-containerfile text not set Path to a custom container definition (e.g. Dockerfile) that you would like to build *after* the ASH container image builds. This is typically used when building a custom container image for ASH and including custom tooling that ASH does not come with by default. The fully qualified image name for the ASH image is passed in as the ASH_BASE_IMAGE build-arg so you can use it as a base. IMPORTANT: When a custom_containerfile path is provided, the build-target is set to ci so the container run-as configuration is not shifted to the non-root user. If you are using this parameter, you are responsible for securing your final container as appropriate. --custom-build-arg text, repeatable not set Custom build arguments to pass to the container build --config-overrides text, repeatable not set Configuration overrides specified as key-value pairs (e.g., 'reporters.cloudwatch-logs.options.aws_region=us-west-2') --offline / --no-offline flag off Run scan in offline/airgapped mode. npm-audit does not run offline, because npm, yarn and pnpm audit by asking the registry: a project with a lockfile reports it MISSING, and one without reports it SKIPPED. IMPORTANT: Online access is needed when building ASH to prepare it for usage during a scan! If selecting Offline while performing a build, the ASH container image will be built in offline mode and any typically online-only dependencies like downloadable tool vulnerability databases will be cached in the image itself before publishing for scan usage. --quiet / --no-quiet flag off Hide all log output --log-level one of QUIET, SIMPLE, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, TRACE INFO Set the log level. --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The path to the configuration file. By default, ASH looks for the following config file names in the source directory of a scan: ['.ash.yml', '.ash.yaml', '.ash.json', 'ash.yml', 'ash.yaml', 'ash.json'] (each at the root, then in .ash/), then ['.ashrc.toml', '.ashrc.yaml', '.ashrc.yml', '.ashrc.json', 'ashrc.toml', 'ashrc.yaml', 'ashrc.yml', 'ashrc.json'] at the root, then the tool.ash table of pyproject.toml at the root; the first found is used. Alternatively, the full path to a config file can be provided by setting the ASH_CONFIG environment variable before running ASH. --verbose, -v flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output --cli-json-input text not set Read parameter values from a JSON object: a path, a file:// URI, or '-' for stdin. Keys are parameter names (output_dir) or long flag spellings (--output-dir). Flags given on the command line override the file; the file overrides environment variables. Run with --generate-cli-skeleton for a template. --generate-cli-skeleton flag off Print a JSON template for --cli-json-input, listing every parameter of this command with its default, and exit.

docs.title: ash config get
docs.text:
Print the resolved configuration: the file's settings over the defaults.

Without --config, prints the config a scan of the current directory would use, or the defaults when there is none. Exit codes: 0 printed, 3 the named file does not exist, cannot be read or is not a valid configuration.

ash config get [OPTIONS] [config_path]
Argument Type Default Environment variable Description config_path text not set The configuration file, as a positional argument. Same as --config, which is preferred; when both are given they must name the same file. docs.title: ash config lint
docs.text:
Lint an ASH configuration file for issues and optionally auto-fix them.

This command performs all validation checks plus additional lint checks:

  • Internal-only fields in scanners/reporters/converters
  • Invalid or unknown top-level sections
  • Duplicate field definitions
  • Suppressions with line_start but missing line_end
  • Expired suppressions
  • Suppression reasons spanning multiple lines
  • Unused suppressions (from last scan report)

Use --fix to auto-fix common issues (removes internal fields, sets missing line_end, removes expired suppressions, collapses multi-line reasons).

Use --fix-unused to comment out suppressions that no longer match any finding (based on the unused suppressions report from the last scan).

Use --non-interactive (or --yes/-y) to skip confirmation prompts. This is useful for pre-commit hooks or CI/CD pipelines.

Exit codes: 0 a scan accepts the config (whatever else is reported is a warning); 1 no config file was found, or --fix or --fix-unused refused to rewrite it; 3 a scan would refuse the config, as 'ash config validate' reports it, the file does not parse, or the named file does not exist or cannot be read. The output marks each issue that makes a scan refuse the config with "blocks the scan".

Examples:

# Lint the default config
ash config lint

# Lint and auto-fix issues
ash config lint --fix

# Lint, fix, and remove unused suppressions
ash config lint --fix --fix-unused

# Non-interactive mode for pre-commit
ash config lint --fix --fix-unused --non-interactive

# Lint a specific config file
ash config lint --config path/to/config.yaml

ash config lint [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The path to the configuration file. By default, the config a scan of the current directory would use: ['.ash.yml', '.ash.yaml', '.ash.json', 'ash.yml', 'ash.yaml', 'ash.json'] (each at the root, then in .ash/), then ['.ashrc.toml', '.ashrc.yaml', '.ashrc.yml', '.ashrc.json', 'ashrc.toml', 'ashrc.yaml', 'ashrc.yml', 'ashrc.json'] at the root, then the tool.ash table of pyproject.toml at the root; the first found is used. --output-dir, -o text not set Path to the ASH output directory (for unused suppressions report). Defaults to .ash/ash_output --fix flag off Auto-fix fixable issues (internal fields, missing line_end, expired suppressions, multi-line suppression reasons). A TOML file, and a file that reads the environment (${VAR} or !ENV), are not rewritten: fix those by hand --fix-unused flag off Comment out unused suppressions based on the last scan's unused suppressions report. A TOML file, and a JSON file (which holds no comments), are not rewritten: remove those by hand --non-interactive, --yes, -y flag off Accept all changes without prompting. Useful for pre-commit hooks and CI/CD --source-dir text not set ASH_SOURCE_DIR The directory a scan would scan, as ash scan --source-dir: the config is discovered there unless --config names one, and a config inside it may only extend files inside it. Defaults to the current directory. --verbose, -v flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output

Same as --config, which is preferred; when both are given they must name the same file. Option Type Default Environment variable Description --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The path to the configuration file. By default, the config a scan of the current directory would use: ['.ash.yml', '.ash.yaml', '.ash.json', 'ash.yml', 'ash.yaml', 'ash.json'] (each at the root, then in .ash/), then ['.ashrc.toml', '.ashrc.yaml', '.ashrc.yml', '.ashrc.json', 'ashrc.toml', 'ashrc.yaml', 'ashrc.yml', 'ashrc.json'] at the root, then the tool.ash table of pyproject.toml at the root; the first found is used. --set text, repeatable not set Configuration modifications specified as key-value pairs (e.g., 'global_settings.severity_threshold=LOW'). Supports lists with [item1,item2], append mode with key+=[value], and JSON syntax. --verbose, -v / --no-verbose flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d / --no-debug flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output --dry-run / --no-dry-run flag off Show changes without writing to file

docs.title: ash config validate
docs.text:
Validate an ASH configuration file the way a scan loads it.

The file is loaded as a scan loads it: parsed (with ${VAR} and !ENV references resolved), its extends chain followed, and checked against the AshConfig model the JSON schema is generated from, with strict types. A config a scan would refuse is reported with every field it refuses, and the command exits 3, the exit code a scan gives for an invalid configuration.

It also warns about things a scan accepts but that are probably mistakes: internal-only fields in scanners/reporters/converters, unknown or internal top-level sections, duplicate top-level keys, a missing project_name, and directory paths without a '**' glob. Warnings do not change the exit code; 'ash config lint' reports the same checks and can fix some of them, with one exception: lint judges the file as written, so it reads neither --config-overrides nor ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES, and an input this command refuses for an environment-named module can still lint clean.

Exit codes: 0 valid (warnings may be printed), 1 no config file found and none of the scan's other inputs given (--config-overrides, ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES), 3 invalid, or the named config file does not exist or cannot be read. A file that does not parse is invalid too, and a scan refuses it as well. With --config-overrides or ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES and no config file, the default configuration with those scan inputs applied is validated -- the config a scan of the directory would run with, and the one ash config get prints or refuses for the same input, exiting 3 when the environment names a module the scan's plugin loader refuses.

Examples:

# Validate the config a scan of the current directory would use
ash config validate

# Validate specific config file
ash config validate --config path/to/config.yaml

# Validate with the overrides a scan will be given
ash config validate --config-overrides 'fail_on_findings=false'

ash config validate [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The path to the configuration file. Defaults to the current directory. --verbose, -v flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output

docs.title: ash inspect findings
docs.text:
The inspect findings command provides an interactive TUI to explore the findings and identify actions to quickly take.

A finding's code is the code snippet the results hold, wherever the results file is. For a finding with none, its lines are read from its file only when the results file sits in <root>/.ash/ash_output, and only from a regular file inside <root> (a hard link inside the tree counts as a file in it, as it does for the scanners); otherwise the detail view says "(source not shown)".

ash inspect findings [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --output-dir path not set Path to the output directory containing an ASH Aggregated Results JSON report file to analyze. --report-file text ash_aggregated_results.json Name of the report file to analyze. Defaults to 'ash_aggregated_results.json'. --config, -c path not set ASH_CONFIG Path to the configuration file where suppressions should be saved. By default, ASH searches for ['.ash.yml', '.ash.yaml', '.ash.json', 'ash.yml', 'ash.yaml', 'ash.json'] (each at the root, then in .ash/), then ['.ashrc.toml', '.ashrc.yaml', '.ashrc.yml', '.ashrc.json', 'ashrc.toml', 'ashrc.yaml', 'ashrc.yml', 'ashrc.json'] at the root, then the tool.ash table of pyproject.toml at the root; the first found is used. With none found, suppressions go to a new .ashrc.yaml in the current directory.

docs.title: ash inspect sarif-fields
docs.text:
The inspect sarif-fields command analyzes SARIF reports to understand field usage across different scanners and ensure fields are preserved during aggregation.

This command:

  1. Extracts field paths from the original SARIF reports
  2. Identifies which scanners populate which fields and their data types
  3. Compares fields between original scanner reports and the aggregated report
  4. Generates a comprehensive HTML report showing field presence and mapping information
  5. Outputs field data in both JSON and CSV formats for further analysis
ash inspect sarif-fields [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --sarif-dir text not set Directory containing SARIF files to analyze --output-dir text not set Directory to write output files

docs.title: ash mcp
docs.text:
Start the ASH MCP server (Model Context Protocol)

ash mcp [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --log-level one of QUIET, SIMPLE, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, TRACE INFO Set the log level. --verbose, -v / --no-verbose flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d / --no-debug flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output --quiet / --no-quiet flag off Hide all log output --transport text stdio Transport: 'stdio' (default), 'streamable-http', or 'sse'. --host text 127.0.0.1 Host to bind for HTTP transports. --port integer 8000 Port to bind for HTTP transports. --mount-path text /mcp HTTP path the transport listens on (default: /mcp for streamable-http, /sse for sse). --auth-header-name text not set Required HTTP header name for single-tenant auth (HTTP transports only). --auth-header-value text not set Expected value of --auth-header-name. Visible to other local users on the command line; prefer --auth-header-value-file or --auth-header-value-fd. --auth-header-value-file path not set Read the expected value of --auth-header-name from this file, once at startup: a regular file, not a symlink, readable by its owner only. One trailing newline is dropped. --auth-header-value-fd integer not set Read the expected value of --auth-header-name from this inherited file descriptor (3 or above), once at startup, then close it. --stateless-http / --no-stateless-http flag off Handle each streamable-HTTP request independently instead of binding it to a server-held session. Required behind a load balancer that may route consecutive requests to different replicas, and by managed runtimes that inject their own Mcp-Session-Id. Only valid with --transport streamable-http. --trust-upstream-session-id flag off Stateless streamable-HTTP only. Declare that a platform in front of ASH issues and authenticates the Mcp-Session-Id header, so it can name the caller's session. Without it a stateless server identifies no session, and tools that need one (source delivery, profiles, the scan registry) refuse. --allowed-host text, repeatable not set Host header value to accept, repeatable. Keeps DNS-rebinding protection enabled while allowing a known proxy or load balancer hostname. Required with a non-loopback --host unless --trust-upstream-host-check is given. --session-workspace-ttl integer not set HTTP transports only. Seconds a session workspace (delivered source, uploads, bound profile) may go unused before it is removed. Covers sessions whose end the server cannot see, such as every stateless one. Default: 86400 (24 hours). --trust-upstream-host-check flag off HTTP transports only. Declare that a proxy or platform in front of ASH checks the Host and Origin headers, so ASH serves any. Without it, a non-loopback --host needs --allowed-host or the server refuses to start. Cannot be combined with --allowed-host. --profile text, repeatable not set Register a named config profile as NAME=path/to/ash.yaml, repeatable. Clients list them with the list_profiles tool and bind one to their session with select_profile; a bound profile supplies the config for every later call in that session that names none. Each file is loaded and schema-validated now, so a typo fails startup rather than a scan.

docs.title: ash merge
docs.text:
Merges the results of a sharded scan into one unified report.

Pass one --results per shard. The command refuses to merge a set of shards that does not reconstruct exactly one whole scan, and its exit code is the verdict for the union — a shard that owned no failing scanner exits 0, so CI must gate on this command rather than on per-shard success.

ash merge [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --results text, repeatable required A shard's ash_aggregated_results.json, or a directory containing one. Repeat once per shard. --output-dir text required ASH_OUTPUT_DIR Directory to write the merged results and reports to. --output-formats text, repeatable not set Comma-separated report formats to generate. Defaults to the formats the scan's own configuration asks for. --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The operator's config file. Its values replace the shards' for the settings a shard's recorded config cannot choose, such as where reporters send findings and which off-host reporters run. Its ash_plugin_modules are the plugin modules the merge loads, with any --config-overrides adds; a module only the shards recorded is not loaded. It adds no reporter section the shards did not record; use --config-overrides for that. --config-overrides text, repeatable not set Configuration overrides as key-value pairs (e.g., 'reporters.s3.enabled=true'), applied over the shards' recorded config. --min-severity one of critical, high, medium, low, none low Minimum severity that counts as actionable for the exit code. --ignore-suppressions flag off Ignore all suppression rules and report every finding regardless of suppression status. Mirrors 'ash scan --ignore-suppressions', so the same tree gives the same verdict sharded or not. --fail-on-findings / --no-fail-on-findings flag not set Exit non-zero when the merged report has actionable findings. Defaults to the scan configuration's value, then to true. --fail-on-incomplete-scanners / --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners flag not set Refuse the merge when a shard completed none of the scanners it owned, and exit 1 when any scanner in the union is ERROR or MISSING, or when every one is SKIPPED, such as when no selected scanner had a file to scan. On by default: under --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners, a shard whose scanners never ran contributes no findings and the merged report reads as a complete, clean scan. Defaults to the scan configuration's value, then to true; pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners to merge a partial union anyway. --log-level one of QUIET, SIMPLE, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, TRACE INFO Set the log level. --verbose, -v flag off Enable verbose logging --debug, -d flag off Enable debug logging --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output --cli-json-input text not set Read parameter values from a JSON object: a path, a file:// URI, or '-' for stdin. Keys are parameter names (output_dir) or long flag spellings (--output-dir). Flags given on the command line override the file; the file overrides environment variables. Run with --generate-cli-skeleton for a template. --generate-cli-skeleton flag off Print a JSON template for --cli-json-input, listing every parameter of this command with its default, and exit.
