docs.title: ash scan
docs.text:
Scan code, infrastructure, secrets, and dependencies.

Start with: ash --mode container --source-dir .

Review the result with: ash inspect findings

Options are grouped by workflow below. Running ash without a subcommand starts a scan.

ash scan [OPTIONS]
Option Type Default Environment variable Description --source-dir text not set ASH_SOURCE_DIR The source directory to scan --output-dir text not set ASH_OUTPUT_DIR The directory to output results to --scanners text, repeatable not set ASH_SCANNERS Specific scanner names to run. Defaults to all scanners. --exclude-scanners text, repeatable not set ASH_EXCLUDED_SCANNERS Specific scanner names to exclude from running. Takes precedence over scanners parameter. --ash-plugin-modules text, repeatable not set ASH_PLUGIN_MODULES List of Python modules to import containing ASH plugins and/or event subscribers. These are loaded in addition to the default modules. --config-overrides text, repeatable not set Configuration overrides specified as key-value pairs (e.g., 'reporters.cloudwatch-logs.options.aws_region=us-west-2'). Supports lists with [item1,item2], append mode with key+=[value], and JSON syntax. See https://awslabs.github.io/automated-security-helper/latest/how-to/configure/ --offline / --no-offline flag off Run scan in offline/airgapped mode. npm-audit does not run offline, because npm, yarn and pnpm audit by asking the registry: a project with a lockfile reports it MISSING, and one without reports it SKIPPED. IMPORTANT: Online access is needed when building ASH to prepare it for usage during a scan! If selecting Offline while performing a build, the ASH container image will be built in offline mode and any typically online-only dependencies like downloadable tool vulnerability databases will be cached in the image itself before publishing for scan usage. --sandbox one of off, auto, bwrap, firejail, landlock, sandbox-exec not set Run every scanner subprocess in an OS-level sandbox: read-only source, writable results directory only, private home and temporary directory, no network unless the scanner needs one (never under --offline). 'auto' picks the best available (Linux: bwrap, firejail, landlock; macOS: sandbox-exec). A scanner that cannot be sandboxed as requested is reported MISSING. Overrides the config file's sandbox.mode; default off. Refused with --mode container (exit 5), which runs the scanners unsandboxed inside the container. See docs/content/docs/scanner-sandbox.md --offline-semgrep-rulesets text p/ci Specify Semgrep rulesets for use in ASH offline mode --strategy one of sequential, parallel parallel Whether to run scanners in parallel or sequential --progress, -p / --no-progress, -P flag on Show progress of each job live in the console. Defaults to True. --output-formats, --output-format, --formats, --format, -f text, repeatable not set The output formats to use (comma-separated). Available formats: text, flat-json, yaml, csv, html, junitxml, markdown, sarif, ocsf, cyclonedx, spdx, github-ghas, gitlab-sast, gitlab-cyclonedx, unused-suppressions. With the AWS plugin module (ash_aws_plugins) in ash_plugin_modules, also, once enabled: aws-security-hub, bedrock-summary-reporter, cloudwatch-logs, s3. Also accepted, though no reporter writes them: aggregated, dict, asff, custom. Values that write a report: text, flat-json, yaml, csv, html, junitxml, markdown, sarif, ocsf, cyclonedx, spdx, github-ghas, gitlab-sast, gitlab-cyclonedx, unused-suppressions. Values that name no reporter and write no report: aggregated, dict, asff, custom, aws-security-hub, bedrock-summary-reporter, cloudwatch-logs, s3. --cleanup / --no-cleanup flag off Clean up 'converted' directory and other temporary files after scan completes. Defaults to False. Note: Scans will always clean up existing files in the output directory before a new scan starts. This parameter only affects the cleanup of the temporary work directory after a scan has completed, typically for inspection of temporary artifacts. --phases one of convert, scan, report, inspect, repeatable not set The phases to run. Defaults to all phases except inspect. --inspect / --no-inspect flag off Enable inspection of SARIF fields after running. This adds the inspect phase to the execution. --use-existing / --no-use-existing flag off Use an existing ash_aggregated_results.json file in the output-dir. If True, the scan phase will be skipped and reports will be generated from this file. --version flag off Prints version number --mode one of precommit, container, local, nix local ASH_MODE Execution mode preset. 'local' (default) runs the scan in this process with the scanner tools installed on this machine. 'precommit' is a local scan that runs only bandit, detect-secrets, checkov, cdk-nag, npm-audit, plus any --scanners, with simplified output and no progress display; in workspace mode it changes only the output. 'container' builds the ASH container image and runs the scan inside it. 'nix' runs the scan inside nix develop, whose shell supplies pinned scanner versions, and always offline. --python-only, --python-based-scanners-only, --python-based-plugins-only / --full, --all-enabled-scanners, --all-enabled-plugins flag off Exclude execution of any plugins or tools that have depencies external to Python. --show-summary / --no-show-summary flag on Show metrics table and results summary --quiet / --no-quiet flag off Hide all log output --log-level one of QUIET, SIMPLE, ERROR, INFO, VERBOSE, DEBUG, TRACE INFO Set the log level. --config, -c text not set ASH_CONFIG The path to the configuration file. By default, ASH looks for the following config file names in the source directory of a scan: ['.ash.yml', '.ash.yaml', '.ash.json', 'ash.yml', 'ash.yaml', 'ash.json'] (each at the root, then in .ash/), then ['.ashrc.toml', '.ashrc.yaml', '.ashrc.yml', '.ashrc.json', 'ashrc.toml', 'ashrc.yaml', 'ashrc.yml', 'ashrc.json'] at the root, then the tool.ash table of pyproject.toml at the root; the first found is used. Alternatively, the full path to a config file can be provided by setting the ASH_CONFIG environment variable before running ASH. --verbose, -v flag off ASH_VERBOSE Enable verbose logging. Any log flag on the command line overrides ASH_VERBOSE. --debug, -d flag off ASH_DEBUG Enable debug logging. Any log flag on the command line overrides ASH_DEBUG. --color / --no-color flag on Enable/disable colorized output --fail-on-findings / --no-fail-on-findings flag not set Enable/disable throwing non-successful exit codes if any actionable findings are found. Defaults to unset, which prefers the configuration value. If this is set directly, it takes precedence over the configuration value. --fail-on-incomplete-scanners / --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners flag not set Exit 1 when a selected scanner did not complete -- ERROR (ran and failed) or MISSING (dependencies unavailable, so it never ran). On by default: under --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners, a run where nothing ran exits 0, the same code as a clean scan, because no scanner produced any finding. A SKIPPED scanner, one you did not select or one with nothing of its kind to scan, does not trip it by itself, so --scanners and --exclude-scanners both narrow what is gated; but a run in which every scanner is SKIPPED, such as one where no selected scanner had a file to scan, exits 1. Independent of --fail-on-findings, and takes precedence over it when both would fail: a partial scan's findings are real but its clean bill of health is not. Defaults to unset, which prefers the configuration value and then on. Pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners to accept a partial scan's exit code, or --exclude-scanners for a tool you do not have, which records it SKIPPED and says so in the report. --allow-stale-content-db / --no-allow-stale-content-db flag not set Let the scan pass when a scanner's content database (grype's or trivy's vulnerability database, the offline semgrep/opengrep rulesets) is older than its declared bound -- for grype, 120h after the database was built. Without it such a scan exits 1, except for trivy's database in an image built with OFFLINE=YES, which warns by default. With it the scan proceeds and the warning is recorded in the log and in the reports. --no-allow-stale-content-db forces the failure, for that database too. Defaults to unset, which prefers the content_db_staleness config value and then 'fail'; either form of the flag takes precedence over the config. --simple / --no-simple flag off Simplified output mode with minimal logging --ignore-suppressions / --no-ignore-suppressions flag off Ignore all suppression rules and report all findings regardless of suppression status. --honor-ignore-files / --no-honor-ignore-files flag not set Whether the .gitignore and .ignore files in the scanned tree decide which files are left out of ASH's scan set (the files detect-secrets, cfn-nag, cdk-nag, cfn-lint, cfn-guard, actionlint, zizmor, npm-audit and the converters read). --no-honor-ignore-files scans the files they match too; ASH's own exclusions such as .git still apply. Defaults to unset, which prefers the operator's honor_ignore_files config value and then honoring them. Either form takes precedence over the config. A config file inside the scanned tree cannot set it. The results and summaries record whether the ignore files were honored and how many files they excluded. --min-severity one of critical, high, medium, low, none low Minimum severity to trigger non-zero exit code (critical, high, medium, low, none). 'critical' and 'high' are equivalent because SARIF does not distinguish them. Findings below this threshold are still reported but don't affect the exit code. --compact-report flag off Produce a shorter markdown report suitable for PR comments. Omits the severity legend, scan metadata, footer, and rows for scanners that were skipped or had zero findings. --changed-files-only flag off ASH_CHANGED_FILES_ONLY Report only findings in files changed between --base-ref and HEAD, for example on a pull request. Scanners still scan every file; findings located in other files are dropped from every report, the summary counts and the exit code. Findings with no file location are kept. When git cannot list the changes, everything is reported; when nothing changed inside --source-dir, nothing is. Not supported with --mode container, which refuses it (exit 5). --base-ref text origin/main ASH_BASE_REF Git ref to diff against when --changed-files-only is set. --allow-in-tree-tools flag off Let ASH start scanners and other tools found inside the scanned directory, such as an activated in-repo .venv/bin or node_modules/.bin. Off by default: a tool inside the scanned directory is treated as missing. Only this flag (also the allow_in_tree_tools key of --cli-json-input) and the ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS environment variable (1, true, yes or on) turn it on, never a config file, and ash mcp never does. --shard-index integer not set ASH_SHARD_INDEX Zero-based index of this shard when one scan is split across several executors. Requires --shard-count. A 3-way split uses indices 0, 1 and 2. Each shard runs a disjoint subset of the scanners and records which ones in its results; recombine them with 'ash merge'. --shard-count integer not set ASH_SHARD_COUNT Total number of shards this scan is split across. Requires --shard-index. Balance is by scanner count rather than scanner cost, so counts above about four buy little: wall clock is bounded by the slowest single scanner. --config-from-scanned-repository flag off Apply the limits ASH puts on a repository-written config file to the --config file and every file it extends, wherever they are. Container mode passes this to the scan inside the container when the config is a file the scanned repository wrote (judged by its resolved path and by the name that reached it) but outside --source-dir, where that scan cannot see it. In a workspace scan it marks the --config file that is layered over every project's own config and used alone by a project without one, from planning on. This option is hidden from --help output. --config-file-from-scanned-repository text, repeatable not set Apply the limits ASH puts on a repository-written config file to this one file of the extends chain of the --config file or of the file ASH_CONFIG names. Container mode passes it, once per file, for each file of those chains the scanned repository wrote; the bases of a --config whose whole chain carries --config-from-scanned-repository are passed individually as well, so a mounted base judged on its own is still a marked file. Refused for a file that is in neither chain. This option is hidden from --help output. --config-file-from-another-checkout text, repeatable not set Apply the limits ASH puts on a config file inside a git checkout other than the scanned one to this one file of the extends chain of the --config file or of the file ASH_CONFIG names. The file cannot grant, and still sets what only restricts, as it does on the host: a lowered archive extraction limit, a scanner option that sends no usage data, and a network_scanners list as a limit. Container mode passes it, once per file, for each file of those chains that is in such a checkout, by its path inside the container, where the scan inside cannot see the checkout. Refused for a file that is in neither chain. This option is hidden from --help output. --ash-config-from-host text not set Read this file as the file ASH_CONFIG names, for the whole command. Container mode passes it to the scan inside the container, with the path there of the file the host's ASH_CONFIG names, which a local scan reads as its base whatever names the config. Not --config, whose environment variable ASH_CONFIG is. This option is hidden from --help output. --workspace text not set ASH_WORKSPACE Path to a '.code-workspace' file whose folders are scanned as separate, independently-scoped projects. Pass 'auto' to use the single '*.code-workspace' file in the current directory. Mutually exclusive with --source-dir. --workspace-config text not set ASH_WORKSPACE_CONFIG Path to the workspace policy file (severity ceiling, workspace-wide suppressions and ignore paths, additional scanners). Without this, ASH looks for 'ash-workspace.{yaml,yml,json}' in the workspace root or its '.ash' directory; finding none is not an error. Must not be any project's own ASH config: workspace policy governs every project, so reading one project's config as policy would apply its settings to its siblings. --allow-missing-projects flag off In workspace mode, skip project folders that are absent or unreadable instead of failing. Skipped projects are recorded in the plan. Without this, a missing project fails the whole workspace, so a typo or an un-cloned repository cannot pass as a clean scan. --dry-run flag off In workspace mode, print the resolved execution plan and exit without scanning anything. --build, -b / --no-build, -B flag on Whether to build the ASH container image --run, -r / --no-run, -R flag on Whether to run the ASH container image --force flag off Force rebuild of the ASH container image --oci-runner, --oci, --runner, -o text not set OCI_RUNNER Use the specified OCI runner instead of docker to run the containerized tools --build-target one of non-root, ci not set The ASH image stage to build and run: 'non-root' (an unprivileged user, the default) or 'ci' (root, the default on Windows). CI environment variables do not change it; --custom-containerfile builds on 'ci'. --container-uid, -u text not set UID to use for the container user --container-gid, -g text not set GID to use for the container user --ash-revision-to-install text not set ASH branch, tag or full commit id to install in the container image for usage during containerized scans --custom-containerfile text not set Path to a custom container definition (e.g. Dockerfile) that you would like to build *after* the ASH container image builds. This is typically used when building a custom container image for ASH and including custom tooling that ASH does not come with by default. The fully qualified image name for the ASH image is passed in as the ASH_BASE_IMAGE build-arg so you can use it as a base. IMPORTANT: When a custom_containerfile path is provided, the build-target is set to ci so the container run-as configuration is not shifted to the non-root user. If you are using this parameter, you are responsible for securing your final container as appropriate. --custom-build-arg text, repeatable not set Custom build arguments to pass to the container build --cli-json-input text not set Read parameter values from a JSON object: a path, a file:// URI, or '-' for stdin. Keys are parameter names (output_dir) or long flag spellings (--output-dir). Flags given on the command line override the file; the file overrides environment variables. Run with --generate-cli-skeleton for a template. --generate-cli-skeleton flag off Print a JSON template for --cli-json-input, listing every parameter of this command with its default, and exit.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
This page is generated from the configuration models in the ASH source code by scripts/generate_config_reference.py. Edits made to this file by hand are overwritten the next time it is generated.

Every key is listed with its type, default and the description the model carries. A key whose model has no description says so. Keys inside a list are written key[].field: global_settings.suppressions[].rule_id is the rule_id of one entry in the suppressions list. A default written as from NAME, else value is read from that environment variable when ASH starts; value applies when the variable is not set.

docs.title: Where ASH finds its configuration
docs.text:
A path given with --config, -c, or the ASH_CONFIG environment variable is used as is, and nothing is discovered.

Otherwise ASH looks in the scan's source directory and uses the first of these it finds. Sources are never merged: every other one that exists is ignored, with a warning naming it.

  1. .ash.yml
  2. .ash/.ash.yml
  3. .ash.yaml
  4. .ash/.ash.yaml
  5. .ash.json
  6. .ash/.ash.json
  7. ash.yml
  8. .ash/ash.yml
  9. ash.yaml
  10. .ash/ash.yaml
  11. ash.json
  12. .ash/ash.json
  13. .ashrc.toml
  14. .ashrc.yaml
  15. .ashrc.yml
  16. .ashrc.json
  17. ashrc.toml
  18. ashrc.yaml
  19. ashrc.yml
  20. ashrc.json
  21. pyproject.toml

pyproject.toml counts only when it has a [tool.ash] table; one without it is not a configuration source.

These are read from the source directory only, never from .ash/: .ashrc.toml, .ashrc.yaml, .ashrc.yml, .ashrc.json, ashrc.toml, ashrc.yaml, ashrc.yml, ashrc.json, pyproject.toml.

A config file can name base files with extends. A chain may be at most 10 levels deep and read at most 50 files.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
A key not listed here is ignored, without an error, when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description project_name string from ASH_PROJECT_NAME, else ash-scan Name of the project being scanned global_settings section see the section Global default settings for ASH shared across scanners. If the same setting exists at the scanner level and is set in both places, the scanner level settings take precedence. fail_on_findings boolean true Whether to exit with non-zero code if findings are detected fail_on_incomplete_scanners boolean true Whether to exit with a non-zero code when a selected scanner did not complete -- status ERROR (ran and failed) or MISSING (dependencies unavailable, never ran). A SKIPPED scanner, one not selected or one with nothing of its kind to scan, does not trip this by itself, but a run in which every scanner is SKIPPED, such as one where no selected scanner had a file to scan, exits 1 while this is on. Independent of fail_on_findings: one answers 'was anything found', this one answers 'did what I asked for actually run'. Selects on the scanner's status, so it covers only a failure that reached that status. Defaults to True, so a scanner recorded ERROR or MISSING does not report the exit code of a clean scan. Converters count too: one that crashed, one that could not convert some of its inputs, and one whose tool is missing while it had inputs make the scan exit non-zero the same way. Set it to False, or pass --no-fail-on-incomplete-scanners, to accept a partial scan's exit code; excluding the scanner whose tool is unavailable is usually better, because an excluded scanner is recorded SKIPPED and the report then says what was not measured. One ending overrides this setting: a run where ASH could not stop a scanner's tool exits 1 either way, because the tool may still be running and writing into the output directory. honor_ignore_files boolean true Whether the .gitignore and .ignore files in the scanned tree decide which files are left out of ASH's scan set, the file list detect-secrets, cfn-nag, cdk-nag, cfn-lint, cfn-guard, actionlint, zizmor, npm-audit and the converters read. True (the default) leaves out every file they match. False scans those files too; ASH's own exclusions (.git, CDK assets, its own output directory) still apply. An operator setting: a config file inside the scanned tree, or one an MCP client supplied, cannot change it, and its value there is ignored with a warning. Set it in a config file outside the tree, with --config-overrides, or with --no-honor-ignore-files / --honor-ignore-files. Every scan records the outcome in metadata.ignore_file_exclusions. sandbox section see the section OS-level sandboxing of scanner subprocesses. content_db_staleness one of fail, warn fail What a scan does when a scanner's content database (grype's or trivy's vulnerability database, the offline semgrep/opengrep rulesets) was built longer ago than the bound declared for it in automated_security_helper/utils/content_databases.py. 'fail' (the default) keeps the scanner's findings and exits 1, naming the database, its build time, its age and the bound. 'warn' lets the scan pass and records the same warning in the log and in the reports (summary, SARIF invocation notifications, flat JSON). The CLI flag --allow-stale-content-db sets 'warn' for one scan and takes precedence over this value; --no-allow-stale-content-db sets 'fail'. content_db_staleness_overrides list of section [] Per-database exceptions to content_db_staleness, each with a required expiration date and reason. An entry holds one named database to its own policy until 00:00 UTC on its expiration date, and every database not named keeps content_db_staleness. An expired entry is ignored with a warning. Empty by default. Either form of --allow-stale-content-db clears this list for that scan, so the flag still decides for every database. content_db_staleness_offline_image_default boolean true Whether an image built with OFFLINE=YES holds trivy-db to 'warn' rather than to content_db_staleness: fail. Such an image carries the trivy database it was built with, and trivy's own bound would fail every scan in it from a day after the build; with this, those scans pass and every report records the stale database. Only trivy-db: grype-db and the offline rulesets keep content_db_staleness. ASH_OFFLINE_AT_BUILD_TIME=YES in ASH's environment, which the image sets from its OFFLINE build argument, turns it on; without that variable this does nothing, whatever it says. Set false to hold trivy-db to content_db_staleness in the image too. A content_db_staleness_overrides entry for trivy-db outranks it, and either form of --allow-stale-content-db sets this to false for that scan. ash_plugin_modules list of string [] List of Python modules to import containing ASH plugins and/or event subscribers. These are loaded in addition to the default modules. external_reports_to_include list of string [] List of external reports to include in the final report. These can be paths to SARIF or CycloneDX reports produced by other tools. build section or null null Build-time configuration settings. ash config validate warns that this key is an internal field, and still passes the config; a scan accepts it. converters section see the section Converter configurations by name. scanners section see the section Scanner configurations by name. reporters section see the section Reporter configurations by name. output_formats list of one of aggregated, text, flat-json, yaml, csv, html, dict, junitxml, markdown, sarif, asff, ocsf, cyclonedx, spdx, custom, github-ghas, gitlab-sast, gitlab-cyclonedx, unused-suppressions, aws-security-hub, bedrock-summary-reporter, cloudwatch-logs, s3 [] Reports to write, by reporter name (for example sarif, markdown, github-ghas): a list, one name, or names separated by commas. Narrows the enabled reporters; it does not enable a disabled one. Empty or null writes every enabled reporter. A --output-formats list on the command line replaces this list. mcp-resource-management section see the section Configuration for MCP server resource management and limits. Also accepted as mcp_resource_management. workspace section see the section Workspace-mode execution settings. Read from the config resolved for the workspace root; a project's own copy of this block is ignored, because how many projects run at once is not a project's decision. extends string, list of string, or null null Base config file(s) this config extends: a path, or a list of paths applied in order, relative to this file. Mappings merge key by key; lists and scalars from this file replace the base's. Paths must stay inside the repository being scanned; URLs are refused. Read when the file is loaded and not written back when a config is saved. patch list of mapping of string to any or null null RFC 6902 JSON-Patch operations (add, remove, replace, test) applied after this file is merged over its bases. Use 'add' at '/global_settings/suppressions/-' to append to a base's list. Read when the file is loaded and not written back when a config is saved.

docs.title: global_settings
docs.text:
A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL from ASH_DEFAULT_SEVERITY_LEVEL, else MEDIUM Global minimum severity level to consider findings as failures across all scanners ignore_paths list of section [] Global list of IgnorePaths. Each path requires a reason for ignoring, e.g. 'Folder contains test data only and is not committed'. suppressions list of section [] Global list of suppression rules. Each rule specifies findings to suppress based on rule ID, file path, and optional line numbers. mcp section see the section MCP-server-specific configuration (runtime override allowlist, etc.).

docs.title: global_settings.ignore_paths[]
docs.text:
Represents a path exclusion entry.

Each entry in the list has these keys.

A key not listed here is accepted and kept, without validation.

Key Type Default Description path string required Path or pattern to exclude reason string required Reason for exclusion expiration string or null null (Optional) Expiration date (YYYY-MM-DD). The entry stops applying on this date, by the local clock of the host running the scan. client_supplied boolean false Set by ASH: True when a config or workspace policy file an MCP client delivered supplied this entry, so results show which suppressions and ignored paths came from the client. A value written in a config file is ignored.

docs.title: global_settings.suppressions[]
docs.text:
Represents a finding suppression rule.

Each entry in the list has these keys.

A key not listed here is accepted and kept, without validation.

Key Type Default Description path string required Path or pattern to exclude reason string required Reason for exclusion expiration string or null null (Optional) Expiration date (YYYY-MM-DD). The entry stops applying on this date, by the local clock of the host running the scan. client_supplied boolean false Set by ASH: True when a config or workspace policy file an MCP client delivered supplied this entry, so results show which suppressions and ignored paths came from the client. A value written in a config file is ignored. rule_id string or null null Rule ID to suppress line_start integer or null null (Optional) Starting line number line_end integer or null null (Optional) Ending line number package_name string or null null (Optional) Only suppress findings about this package (glob, case-insensitive). Findings that do not report a package name never match. package_version string or null null (Optional) Only suppress findings about this installed package version (glob, case-insensitive). Findings that do not report an installed version never match. package_path string or null null (Optional) Only suppress findings about the package copy installed at this path, relative to the scan root (glob, supports **), e.g. 'deploy/cdk/node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/node_modules/brace-expansion'. Separates two copies with the same name and version. Findings that do not report an install path never match. symbol string or null null (Optional) Only suppress findings whose lines lie inside the definition with this qualified name, e.g. 'MyClass.my_method', in the finding's file. Names are dotted from the top of the file, exact and case-sensitive. Resolved by parsing the file with tree-sitter (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java), which needs the 'symbols' extra; a finding whose file cannot be parsed never matches.

docs.title: global_settings.mcp
docs.text:
MCP-server-specific config bundle (transport-agnostic).

A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description runtime_overrides section see the section Allowlist for runtime JSON-Patch overrides.

docs.title: global_settings.mcp.runtime_overrides
docs.text:
Allowlist + denylist controlling which JSON-Patch ops the MCP server accepts.

A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description enabled boolean false Master switch — runtime patches are rejected unless True. allowed_paths list of string [] JSON-Pointer glob patterns the client may target. * matches one segment, ** matches any subtree. Example: '/scanners/*/options/severity_threshold'. denied_paths list of string ["/fail_on_findings", "/fail_on_incomplete_scanners", "/content_db_staleness", "/content_db_staleness_overrides", "/honor_ignore_files", "/content_db_staleness_offline_image_default", "/sandbox", "/sandbox/**", "/ash_plugin_modules", "/ash_plugin_modules/**", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/scan_settings/filters_used", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/scan_settings/filters_used/**", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/scan_settings/plugins_used", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/scan_settings/plugins_used/**", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/baseline_file", "/global_settings/ignore_paths", "/global_settings/suppressions", "/global_settings/mcp", "/global_settings/mcp/**", "/scanners/opengrep/options/exclude_rule", "/scanners/semgrep/options/exclude_rule", "/scanners/bandit/options/confidence_level", "/scanners/checkov/options/frameworks", "/scanners/checkov/options/skip_frameworks", "/scanners/opengrep/options/config", "/scanners/opengrep/options/patterns", "/scanners/opengrep/options/severity", "/scanners/semgrep/options/config", "/scanners/semgrep/options/severity", "/scanners/detect-secrets/options/scan_settings", "/scanners/cdk-nag/options/nag_packs/AwsSolutionsChecks", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/checks", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/confidence_levels", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/disable_ip_types", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/enable_preprocessors", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/finding_limit", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/profile", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/recursive", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/respect_gitignore", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/use_default_config", "/scanners/ferret-scan/options/validator_budget", "/scanners/trivy-repo/options/license_full", "/scanners/trivy-repo/options/scanners", Each entry starts with '/'. The defaults block the fields that decide whether a scan fails, what it runs and reports, where findings are sent, the scanner sandbox, and this policy. A list equal to a default ASH has shipped counts as the current default list. Any other list is added to the current defaults, unless replace_default_denied_paths is true. When it is added, a list that holds some default entries and leaves others out still gets them, and a warning names the ones it leaves out. Whatever the list, and with replace_default_denied_paths too, the entries ASH always denies (the scanner sandbox, ash_plugin_modules, the detect-secrets verification, plugin and baseline settings, the archive converter's extraction limits, and the sections of the plugins that send data off the host: the s3, aws-security-hub, cloudwatch-logs and bedrock-summary-reporter reporters and the detect-secrets, npm-audit, opengrep, semgrep, snyk-code and trivy-repo scanners) are added to it. denied_value_patterns mapping of string to string {} Map of JSON-Pointer pattern to regex. add/replace ops are rejected when any string leaf reachable from the op's value matches the regex; lists and dicts are walked recursively so a forbidden token cannot be hidden inside a nested structure. The test op is exempt because it is read-only. Each key starts with '/'. replace_default_denied_paths boolean false When true, denied_paths is used as written instead of being added to ASH's default list, and each default entry it leaves out is named in a warning. When false (the default), the entries listed are denied as well as the defaults. Either way, an unset list, or one equal to a default ASH has shipped, gets the current default list.

docs.title: sandbox
docs.text:
OS-level sandboxing of scanner subprocesses. Off by default.

A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description mode one of off, auto, bwrap, firejail, landlock, sandbox-exec "off" How scanner subprocesses are confined. 'off' runs them as plain subprocesses. 'auto' uses the best sandbox available (Linux: bwrap, then firejail, then landlock; macOS: sandbox-exec). Any other value requires that backend. A scanner that cannot be sandboxed as requested is recorded MISSING with the reason; it is never run unsandboxed. A mode that --sandbox, ASH_CONFIG or the operator's config file sets is a floor: a config file inside a git checkout or the scanned directory cannot turn it off or switch backends. Not applied in container mode, where the container is the boundary; ASH logs a warning when it is set there. network_scanners list of string or null null Scanners allowed a network when the scan is online. Null (the default) uses each scanner's declared need: semgrep, opengrep, grype, trivy, npm-audit and snyk-code fetch rules, databases or audit data. A list replaces those defaults. Under --offline no scanner gets a network. Honored only from --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory; set by any other config file, a list can only remove network. extra_read_paths list of string [] Additional host paths every sandboxed scanner may read, for example a corporate CA bundle or a shared rule directory. '~' and $VARS expand. Honored only from --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. read_path_scanners list of string [] Scanners allowed the extra host paths their own options ask for (a rules file or baseline outside the source tree, for example). Under a sandbox, without this, a scanner whose read paths come from its options gets only the default policy, and ASH does not read a detect-secrets baseline_file outside the source tree. With it, a granted path, that baseline included, is used only when it resolves inside the source tree or an extra_read_paths entry. Honored only from --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory. env_scanners list of string [] Scanners allowed the environment variables their own options ask for (a token for an online check, for example). Without this, such variables are not passed. Honored only from --config-overrides or a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory.

docs.title: Workspace policy file
docs.text:
In workspace mode, policy that applies to every project lives in its own file, separate from any project's configuration.

ASH looks for it at the workspace root and then in .ash/, under any of these names: .ash-workspace.yml, .ash-workspace.yaml, .ash-workspace.json, ash-workspace.yml, ash-workspace.yaml, ash-workspace.json.

Exactly one may exist: when ASH finds more than one, it refuses the workspace rather than choose.

docs.title: Workspace policy keys
docs.text:
A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description workspace section see the section Workspace-wide policy. Distinct from AshConfig.workspace, which holds execution scheduling knobs in a project config; nothing here can be set from a project's own file.

docs.title: Workspace policy workspace
docs.text:
Workspace-wide policy: the workspace block of the policy file.

A key not listed here is an error when the configuration is loaded.

Key Type Default Description max_severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null The LOOSEST severity threshold any project may use. A project configuring something stricter keeps it; a project configuring something looser is tightened to this value. 'max' refers to permissiveness, not to severity: the strictness order is ALL < LOW < MEDIUM < HIGH < CRITICAL, so raising this value LOOSENS the ceiling. Unset means no ceiling. Case-sensitive. suppressions list of section [] Suppressions that apply across the workspace. Paths are WORKSPACE-relative (e.g. 'api/src/legacy.py') and are rewritten into each project's own coordinates before being applied. A suppression that cannot match inside a project is not passed to it; one that cannot be rewritten soundly refuses the workspace. ignore_paths list of section [] Paths excluded across the workspace. Workspace-relative and pushed down per project, exactly as 'suppressions' are. additional_scanners list of string [] Scanners every project must run, in addition to whatever it enables itself. Additive only -- this cannot disable a scanner a project enabled. A scanner the project already declares runs under the project's own config and its findings are the project's; a scanner added only by this policy runs with default config and its findings are tagged 'origin: workspace-policy' and reported separately. policy_scanners_gate boolean false Whether findings from policy-added scanners affect a project's exit code. Default false: a workspace that adds a scanner to gather visibility should not thereby fail projects that never opted into it, and turning it on is the operator saying they have triaged what the new scanner reports.

The entry stops applying on this date, by the local clock of the host running the scan. client_supplied boolean false Set by ASH: True when a config or workspace policy file an MCP client delivered supplied this entry, so results show which suppressions and ignored paths came from the client. A value written in a config file is ignored. rule_id string or null null Rule ID to suppress line_start integer or null null (Optional) Starting line number line_end integer or null null (Optional) Ending line number package_name string or null null (Optional) Only suppress findings about this package (glob, case-insensitive). docs.title: Scanner coverage
docs.text:
Which scanners read which files. Every built-in scanner is on by default, and each one decides for itself what to read, so a scanner with nothing to read in your repository reports SKIPPED or PASSED with no findings. Scanners lists each scanner's tool, version, and options, and Choose scanners shows how to turn them on and off.

Community plugins run only when you load their module with ash_plugin_modules or --ash-plugin-modules; see Community plugins.

docs.title: By stack
docs.text:
What your repository has Built-in scanners Community plugins Python code bandit, semgrep, opengrep snyk-code JavaScript and TypeScript code semgrep, opengrep snyk-code Java, Go, Ruby, C#, PHP, and other languages semgrep, opengrep (as far as their rules cover the language) snyk-code Python dependencies (requirements.txt, lockfiles) grype, trivy, syft trivy-repo npm, Yarn, and pnpm dependencies npm-audit, grype, trivy, syft trivy-repo Other dependency manifests and lockfiles (go.mod, pom.xml, and the others grype and trivy recognize) grype, trivy, syft trivy-repo CloudFormation templates cfn-nag, cfn-lint, cfn-guard, cdk-nag, checkov trivy-repo AWS CDK apps cfn-nag, cfn-lint, cfn-guard, cdk-nag, checkov (on the templates cdk synth writes to cdk.out); bandit, semgrep, opengrep (on the app code; bandit reads only Python) trivy-repo Terraform checkov trivy-repo Kubernetes manifests and the other formats checkov supports checkov trivy-repo Dockerfiles checkov trivy-repo GitHub Actions workflows actionlint, zizmor, checkov Composite actions (action.yml) zizmor Secrets, in any file detect-secrets, gitleaks ferret-scan (sensitive data), trivy-repo A software bill of materials syft Jupyter notebooks bandit, detect-secrets, gitleaks (on the converted script, bandit only for a Python notebook; see Converted files) .zip, .tar, and .gz archives detect-secrets, gitleaks (on every extracted file; see Converted files)

The other scanners read converted scripts and extracted files of the kinds they cover, as they do in the source directory, except that semgrep and opengrep leave scripts converted from Python notebooks out by default.

For a CDK app, synthesize before you scan, so that cdk.out holds the templates. ASH keeps the synthesized templates in the scan set when your root .gitignore excludes cdk.out; see What decides the files.

docs.title: By scanner
docs.text:
"Whole directory" means the tool walks the source directory itself and applies its own rules for which files to read. "Selected files" means ASH picks the files and passes them to the tool.

Scanner Type What it reads --python-only --mode precommit actionlint IaC Selected files: GitHub Actions workflows no no bandit SAST Whole directory: Python files, skipping .venv/, venv/, and node_modules/ yes yes cdk-nag IaC Selected files: CloudFormation templates no yes cfn-guard IaC Selected files: CloudFormation templates, against the wa-Security-Pillar ruleset by default no no cfn-lint IaC Selected files: CloudFormation templates yes no cfn-nag IaC Selected files: CloudFormation templates no no checkov IaC Whole directory, every checkov framework (--framework all), skipping .venv/, venv/, and node_modules/ yes yes detect-secrets Secrets Selected files: every file in the scan set except generated lockfiles yes yes gitleaks Secrets Whole directory: the files on disk, not git history no no grype SCA Whole directory: the packages it catalogs from manifests and lockfiles no no npm-audit SCA Selected files: each package.json that has a lockfile beside it no yes opengrep SAST Whole directory, with ASH's bundled rules and the p/ci ruleset no no semgrep SAST Whole directory, with ASH's bundled rules and the p/ci ruleset yes no syft SBOM Whole directory: builds an SBOM and reports no findings no no trivy SCA Whole directory: trivy fs with the vulnerability scanner only, by default no no zizmor SAST Selected files: GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions yes no ferret-scan Secrets Whole directory, including files .gitignore excludes no no snyk-code SAST Whole directory, sent to Snyk's service no no trivy-repo SAST Whole directory: trivy repository with the vulnerability, secret, misconfiguration, and license scanners no no

--python-only runs only the scanners marked yes and reports the rest SKIPPED, whether or not their tools are installed.

--mode precommit runs the five scanners marked yes, plus any you name with --scanners.

docs.title: How each scanner picks its files
GitHub Actions
docs.text:
actionlint reads every *.yml and *.yaml file whose parent directory is workflows inside a .github directory, at any depth, so sub/.github/workflows/ci.yml counts and .github/workflows/nested/ci.yml does not. The directory names are case-sensitive; the extension is not.

zizmor reads the same workflows plus every action.yml and action.yaml, and skips paths under .venv, venv, or node_modules. zizmor itself rejects an upper-case extension such as CI.YML, and the scanner then reports ERROR.

With no workflows, both report SKIPPED. checkov also checks workflows, through its own GitHub Actions framework.

docs.title: CloudFormation
docs.text:
cfn-nag, cfn-lint, cfn-guard, and cdk-nag share one rule: a file in the scan set whose name ends in .json, .yaml, or .yml (lowercase) and that parses to a document with a top-level Resources mapping. AWSTemplateFormatVersion is not required. Files ending in .template are not read by these four; checkov reads them.

cfn-nag and cfn-guard run once per template; cfn-lint checks them all in one run. cdk-nag applies its AWS Solutions rule pack. With no templates, all four report SKIPPED.

cfn-nag reads a copy of each template that ASH writes in the scanner's results directory, named template.json, template.yaml, or template.yml after the template's extension, and removes it after the run. Findings name the original template. On Windows, where cfn_nag_scan is a batch file, the template's own name never reaches its command line, so characters such as & and | in it are not read as command syntax.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
npm-audit finds each package.json and audits the first lockfile beside it of yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, and package-lock.json, with yarn, pnpm, or npm. A package.json with no lockfile is not audited. If yarn or pnpm is not installed, that lockfile is not audited and counts as an input npm-audit could not read, so the scan is incomplete. With no lockfile beside any package.json, npm-audit reports SKIPPED, whether or not npm is installed. npm-audit does not run offline, because the package managers audit a lockfile by asking the registry: offline, a project with a lockfile reports npm-audit MISSING, and one without reports it SKIPPED.

grype and trivy read the source directory themselves, so they find every manifest and lockfile their own catalogers recognize. trivy runs only its vulnerability scanner unless you set scanners.trivy.options.scanners. syft builds the SBOM from the same kind of catalog and reports no findings.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: detect-secrets reads every file in the scan set except generated lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, npm-shrinkwrap.json, poetry.lock, uv.lock, pipenv.lock, Pipfile.lock, conda-lock.yml, conda-lock.yaml). gitleaks runs gitleaks dir on the source directory, so it reads the files on disk and not the git history.

docs.title: Source code
docs.text: bandit, semgrep, opengrep, checkov, and snyk-code read the source directory themselves. semgrep and opengrep always use ASH's bundled rules. Online they add the ruleset in their config option, p/ci by default (scanners.semgrep.options.config); offline they add the rules cached in the directory SEMGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR or OPENGREP_RULES_CACHE_DIR names. The languages they cover are the languages those rules cover.

docs.title: What decides the files
docs.text:
Before the scan, ASH lists the files to scan, the scan set, and writes it to ash-scan-set-files-list.txt in the output directory (see Output files):

  • It walks the source directory. It does not ask git, so untracked files are included and the directory does not have to be a repository.
  • Every .gitignore and .ignore file in the tree applies, with git's rules: a nested file applies to its own directory.
  • ASH always leaves out .git and cdk.out/asset.*, keeps *.template.json files that an ignore file would otherwise exclude, and drops every path containing /node_modules/aws-cdk (which also matches aws-cdk-lib). A directory the root .gitignore excludes is skipped whole, except a CDK cloud assembly: a directory named cdk.out, or one that holds a cdk.out file and a manifest.json. ASH still looks in it and keeps its *.template.json files, so the CloudFormation scanners read the synthesized templates.
  • ASH leaves out its own output directories: this scan's --output-dir, and .ash/ash_output under the source directory and under the working directory, when they are inside the source directory and not reached through a symbolic link. In a git repository, the files git tracks in them stay in the scan set, in this scan's own output directory too, and ASH logs a warning. Outside git, these directories are left out whole. Any other directory, such as another shard's output, is scanned like the rest of the tree; when it holds ASH's result files, ASH logs a warning.
  • node_modules, .venv, and venv stay in the scan set. bandit, checkov, and zizmor skip them on their own.

The scanners marked "Selected files" above read only the scan set. The scanners that walk the directory themselves do not use it, so they can report files your .gitignore excludes; bandit, checkov, gitleaks, grype, and trivy do. bandit, checkov, semgrep, opengrep, grype, syft, and ferret-scan skip ASH's output directories that hold no file git tracks. checkov gets each of them as a checkov --skip-path value, unless scanners.checkov.options.skip_ash_output_dir is false. On Windows, ASH passes none, and it leaves out a directory whose path holds ( or ) with a warning; there, add the directory to scanners.checkov.options.skip_path, or move --output-dir outside the source directory. ASH drops what checkov reports in those directories either way.

To drop findings from every scanner, add paths to global_settings.ignore_paths. ASH removes the findings under them after the scan, and actionlint, zizmor, detect-secrets, ferret-scan, snyk-code, and the converters also skip those files. bandit skips the ignore paths it can be given as exclude patterns, and ASH drops its findings under the others afterward. An ignore path stops applying on its expiration date. With --ignore-suppressions, ASH gives no scanner or converter the ignore paths and drops no finding under them. See Suppress findings.

ASH drops the findings scanners report in its output directories, even with --ignore-suppressions, except in files git tracks there and in this scan's converted/. A file a repository commits to one of those directories is scanned and reported like any other, in this scan's own output directory too:

mkdir -p .ash/ash_output/keep
printf 'DATABASE_PASSWORD = "correct-horse-battery-staple-1234"\n' > .ash/ash_output/keep/tracked.py
git add -f .ash/ash_output/keep/tracked.py
git commit -q -m "Commit a file under the default output directory"
ash scan --scanners detect-secrets

detect-secrets reports the password in .ash/ash_output/keep/tracked.py, and the scan exits 2. Outside a git repository, ASH cannot tell a committed file from its own, and drops every finding in those directories.

--changed-files-only drops the findings outside the changed files from every report after the scan; every scanner still reads its whole input.

docs.title: Converted files
docs.text:
Two converters run before the scanners, and every selected scanner then scans their output in converted/ as a second target:

  • archive extracts .zip, .tar, and .gz files from the scan set. It extracts only members with a file extension ASH knows how to scan, compared case-sensitively, so files such as Dockerfile or go.mod inside an archive, and archives inside archives, are not extracted. .tgz, .bz2, .xz, .jar, and .whl files are not opened. A .gz file whose name does not end in .tar.gz and that holds one compressed file rather than a tar archive, such as data.json.gz, is decompressed and scanned. It is a failed input only when it cannot be decompressed (a damaged stream or a bad CRC), and is refused when it exceeds an extraction limit or decompresses to an archive name. A .gz file that is neither gzip nor tar data is skipped. Any other file with one of the three extensions that Python cannot read as a zip or tar archive is a failed input.
  • jupyter converts each .ipynb notebook to a script with nbconvert. ASH runs nbconvert on a copy of the notebook named notebook.ipynb, in a temporary directory that holds nothing else, so nbconvert does not pick up a Python module or template directory from the repository through its working directory, and a notebook whose name contains characters such as [ or { still converts. The copy drops language_info.nbconvert_exporter, and keeps language_info.file_extension only when it is a plain extension such as .r. The converted file, in converted/jupyter/, is named after the notebook's path with characters other than letters, digits, and _ replaced, and ends in -converted.py, or in -converted plus the notebook's plain extension, such as -converted.r, for a notebook in another language.

semgrep and opengrep exclude *-converted.py by default (their exclude option), so they do not scan notebooks converted to Python. A notebook converted to another language, such as one ending in -converted.r, is not excluded. Findings in converted files point into the output directory, not into the original archive or notebook.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
This page is generated from the code that reads each variable by scripts/generate_env_var_reference.py. Edits made to this file by hand are overwritten the next time it is generated.

ASH reads 141 environment variables: 58 of its own (ASH_ prefix) and 83 set by other tools or the platform. The tables list every place each one is read. A variable that sets a CLI option links to that option; the option on the command line takes precedence over the variable.

Columns:

  • Default: the value the code uses when the variable is unset, as written in the code, at each read that supplies one. Where none does, or the only one is an empty string, it is the default of the CLI option the variable sets, or of the configuration key it is the default of. Blank means none of these supplies one (the code checks whether the variable is set, or treats unset as empty).
  • Container image: the value the ASH container image sets, from an ENV line in the Dockerfile, and the build stage that sets it.
  • Read at: the file of each read and the function, method or script function it is in, or module level or top level when it is in none. ash and utils/ are the shell and PowerShell entry scripts; everything else is the Python package.
  • Purpose: the option's help text, or the code comment or docstring at the read, quoted with the file and function it is in. "Purpose not documented in code." means the code around the read does not say.

docs.title: Variables a configuration file can read
docs.text: A value in a configuration file that begins with ${NAME} or ${NAME:default} has the reference replaced by that environment variable. Only names that start with ASH_ and these names are substituted: AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, AWS_PROFILE, AWS_REGION. Any other reference is left as written, with a warning. The prefix and the list are defined in automated_security_helper/core/constants.py.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The exit code of every ash command, with the conditions that produce it. For how to change the scan verdict, see Set the gate.

On every command, a command-line usage error exits 5: an unknown option, subcommand, or argument; a value outside the choices an option takes (such as --mode or --min-severity) or a number that is not one; a missing required option; or a --cli-json-input document that ASH cannot read or use. ash scan, ash build-image, and ash with no subcommand reject an option or argument they do not define. An option given to ash before a subcommand is passed to the command named right after ash, and is a usage error when that command does not take it: ash --source-dir . config get exits 5, because ash config has no --source-dir, while ash config get --source-dir . works. Some names and paths that ASH cannot use are usage errors too, such as a --scanners list that names no scanner, a --source-dir that does not exist, or an --output-dir that ASH cannot create, while ash report exits 1 when it finds no results to report on. The tables below list both. Two ash dependencies install selections exit 2 instead: a --tool name that it has no plugin for, or whose plugin type --plugin-type leaves out, and a --plugin-type other than converter, scanner, or reporter. Usage errors have a code of their own so that a CI gate does not read a mistyped flag as a scan with findings.

docs.title: ash scan
docs.text:
ash with no subcommand runs a scan and exits the same way.

Code Condition 0 No actionable findings; or findings, with fail_on_findings off. With fail_on_incomplete_scanners off, also an incomplete scan, including one in which no selected scanner had a file to scan. Also --version, and --workspace with --dry-run. 1 The scan is incomplete: a selected scanner ended ERROR or MISSING or lost some of its targets, no scanner ran (every selected scanner was SKIPPED, also when none of them had a file to scan), or a converter failed (with fail_on_incomplete_scanners on, the default) 1 A rule could not be evaluated 1 A content database is past its age bound, with content_db_staleness: fail (the default). A scanner that passed against that database is recorded ERROR, and one that failed its threshold stays FAILED. This row sets the code for both, also with fail_on_incomplete_scanners off. 1 A report file a reporter is about to write, such as reports/ash.sarif, is a link (Output files) 1 Any other error during the scan 2 Actionable findings: an unsuppressed finding at or above its scanner's severity threshold, with fail_on_findings on and --min-severity met 3 The configuration cannot be used: the config file that --config or ASH_CONFIG names, or that discovery finds, does not exist, is not a regular file, cannot be read, is not UTF-8, or does not parse; it does not validate (an unknown key in a suppression, an ignore path, or a plugin's options makes it invalid, and so does one plugin's section written under two spellings, such as detect-secrets and DETECT_SECRETS); an override does not parse or does not validate; a config file an MCP client delivered sets a field the server's policy denies; or two plugins of one type that the scan loads have the same name or names that read as one (Package a third-party plugin) 3 Refused before writing: the output directory, a directory on the way to it, or a directory or fixed-name file ASH writes in it, such as reports or ash.log, is a link (Output files). An output directory that is a symlink, or that a symlink below the source directory leads to, is refused this way in every mode, --mode container (also with --no-run) and --mode nix included, and before the check that the directory can be written, so nothing is made and the link's target keeps its entries. 4 A workspace error (see Workspace mode), or --dry-run, --allow-missing-projects, or --workspace-config given without --workspace 5 A usage error. For a scan that includes: the source directory (--source-dir or ASH_SOURCE_DIR) does not exist, is not a directory, cannot be entered, or is not a valid path because it holds a NUL character; the output directory is not a directory, cannot be created, cannot be entered, or cannot be written, or it is not a valid path because it holds a NUL character, which a --cli-json-input document can carry and a command line cannot; --use-existing finds no results; with --changed-files-only, a --base-ref that git would read as something other than a revision, such as one that starts with -; --changed-files-only, or ASH_CHANGED_FILES_ONLY, with --mode container, which is refused before anything is built or run; the shard options are invalid or combined with --workspace; an --output-formats value is not a format name ASH accepts; no name in --scanners (or ASH_SCANNERS) matches a scanner; every scanner --scanners names is also excluded. ASH checks the --scanners names when the scan phase starts, after the converters have run and the output directory has been written. 130 Interrupted with Ctrl-C, in every mode, container and Nix mode included. ASH prints ASH scan interrupted before it finished: there is no verdict, and the output directory may hold partial results. on stderr, and no results table and no line saying the scan completed, in the console or in the scan's log file. Container and Nix mode first give the runtime or the Nix shell time to stop (Container and Nix mode).

A source or output directory that ASH refuses stops the scan before anything is created, with one of these lines on stderr, each naming the path as it was given:

  • Source directory does not exist: <path>
  • Source directory is not a directory: <path>
  • Source directory cannot be entered: <path>
  • Source directory is not a valid path: <path>
  • Output directory is not a directory: <path>
  • Output directory is not a valid path: <path>
  • Output directory cannot be created: <path> (<reason>)
  • Output directory cannot be entered: <path>
  • Output directory cannot be written: <path> (<reason>)

The reason is the system's text for the error, such as Not a directory when a file is on the way to the output directory, or Permission denied. A NUL character in the path is shown as \x00, as in Output directory is not a valid path: out\x00dir. An output directory that does not exist is created. --mode container refuses the same directories, also with --no-run. So does ./ash, which prints the same line after ERROR: and exits 5, and so does Invoke-ASH, which sets $LASTEXITCODE to 5 and stops with the same line after ERROR:.

Only a scan with no config file at all uses the default configuration. A config file that is named or found and cannot be used, in any format, is exit 3, and so is an extends base that is missing or does not parse.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
In a repository where detect-secrets reports one finding, SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD in app.py, a scan with only that scanner fails on it, with 2:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress

With fail_on_findings off, the same scan exits 0:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --no-fail-on-findings

--use-existing with an output directory that holds no results is a usage error, 5:

ash --source-dir . --use-existing --output-dir no-scan-here

So is a --source-dir that does not exist:

ash --source-dir no-such-dir --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress

Source directory does not exist: no-such-dir

A threshold in lowercase does not validate, so the config is invalid, 3:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress \
  --config-overrides global_settings.severity_threshold=high

A --config that names no file exits 3 too:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --config no-such-config.yaml

--dry-run without --workspace exits 4:

ash --source-dir . --dry-run

A mistyped --min-severity value is a usage error, 5, and nothing is scanned:

ash --source-dir . --scanners detect-secrets --offline --no-progress --min-severity hihg

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
ASH stops at the first of these that applies:

  1. A usage error in the command line itself, such as an unknown option, an invalid value, or a missing required option: 5.
  2. A check before scanning: the shard and workspace options, workspace resolution, the source directory, an output directory that is a link or is reached through one, then an output directory that is not a directory, cannot be entered or written, or has a file on the way to it, --use-existing, --output-formats, an output directory that cannot be created for another reason, such as a parent directory that cannot be written, the config, then the scanner selection, which ASH checks when the scan phase starts. Each exits as the table above says (3, 4, or 5).
  3. With fail_on_incomplete_scanners on: a selected scanner ERROR, MISSING, or with lost targets; then no scanner ran; then a failed converter: 1.
  4. A rule could not be evaluated: 1.
  5. A stale content database under content_db_staleness: fail: 1.
  6. fail_on_findings off: 0.
  7. Actionable findings, counted against each scanner's own threshold, and at least one unsuppressed finding at or above --min-severity: 2.
  8. Otherwise: 0.

fail_on_findings and fail_on_incomplete_scanners each come from the command-line flag, then the config, then their default (on). --allow-stale-content-db and --no-allow-stale-content-db replace the config's content_db_staleness.

docs.title: Container and Nix mode
docs.text:
In --mode container (and ash build-image) and --mode nix, ASH reads the results back on the host and computes the code by the rules above, applying --min-severity there. --ignore-suppressions reaches the scan inside the container and works there as in a local scan.

Code Condition 0, 1, 2 The verdict, from the results 1, or the container runtime's code Refused before a container started: no container runtime found, a non-numeric UID or GID, an invalid revision, no Dockerfile, or a failed image build 3 Refused before a container started: a path ASH would mount is not UTF-8 (Mounts and network); a config file cannot be used, or would be mounted from a place the scanned repository chooses (The config file); a config file reads a variable a container scan does not pass in; or, through OCI_RUNNER_WRAPPER, the variables a config reads cannot be passed in an env file; or the output directory is a symlink, or a symlink below the source directory leads to it (such as a committed .ash link, for the default .ash/ash_output), as in every mode (ash scan). Nothing is created or mounted, also with --no-run. ./ash and Invoke-ASH refuse the same output directory with exit 3 1 The results file is missing or does not parse 0, or the build's code --no-run 130 Interrupted with Ctrl-C. Outside Windows, ASH passes the interrupt to the container runtime or the Nix shell, unless the terminal already delivered it there, waits up to 5 seconds for it to stop, and then kills it; a second Ctrl-C during the wait kills it at once. On Windows, a Ctrl-C typed in the console reaches the container runtime as well, and ASH waits up to 5 seconds for it to stop, as above; without a console, ASH ends the runtime at once. A scan prints the interrupted-scan message above. ash build-image prints ASH build-image interrupted before it finished., and, without --no-run, adds : there is no verdict, and the output directory may hold partial results before the period. any other The container exited with a code other than 0, 1, or 2 (for example 3, 4, 5, 125, 126, 127, or 137); ASH exits with the same code 1 Nix mode: nix is not installed 3, 4, or 5 Nix mode: the Nix shell wrote no results and exited with 3, 4, or 5, which means the ASH inside it refused the run before scanning; ASH exits with the same code. Any other code without results exits 1.

docs.title: Sharded scans
docs.text: Each shard computes the verdict for its own scanners, so a shard with findings exits 2 and a shard with a MISSING scanner exits 1. The one difference is that a shard that ran no scanner does not fail for that reason. Gate the pipeline on ash merge, not on the shards.

docs.title: Workspace mode
docs.text:
With --workspace, ASH scans each project and combines their verdicts. The highest of these wins: 3 (a project's config is invalid), then 2 (a project has actionable findings at or above its threshold), then 1 (a project failed, is incomplete, or has a stale database), then 0. Codes 4 and 5 are not part of that ranking: ASH gives them when it refuses the workspace before any project runs.

Code Condition 3 A project's config, or the --config file, cannot be used or is invalid, as for a scan; or two plugins of one type that the scan loads have the same name or names that read as one, as for a scan. ASH detects this before it scans anything, also with --dry-run. 4 The workspace file is missing or ambiguous (--workspace auto finds more than one); --source-dir is also given; the workspace policy file is not valid, including an unknown key in one of its suppressions or ignore paths; a project directory is missing and --allow-missing-projects is not set; or no project could be scanned 5 A usage error, including a --scanners selection that matches no scanner or that --exclude-scanners cancels. ASH refuses it once, before it scans any project. 0 --dry-run; or nothing was scanned because every project was skipped as unchanged

Because the combination puts 2 above 1, a project with findings and a MISSING scanner makes the workspace exit 2, where the same project scanned alone exits 1. Workspace mode does not check for rules that could not be evaluated.

docs.title: ash merge
docs.text:
Code Condition 0, 1, 2 The verdict over all shards, by the same rules as ash scan, including incompleteness, stale databases, and --min-severity 1 Refused: no shard index; results from a scan that was not sharded; a --results directory with no ash_aggregated_results.json at its top, in ash_output/, or in .ash/ash_output/, and none or more than one below it; a duplicated or mismatched shard; a results file that does not parse; a shard that completed none of its scanners; a report file it is about to write, such as reports/ash.sarif, is a link (Output files) 3 The output directory, a directory on the way to it, or a directory ASH writes in it, such as reports, is a link (Output files) 3 The configuration recorded in the shards reads a field that takes a fixed choice, a boolean, or a number from the environment, and neither --config-overrides nor the file --config names supplies the field (Read values from the environment) 3 Two reporters that the merge loads have the same name or names that read as one, as for a scan 5 A usage error, including a missing --results or --output-dir, a --results path that does not exist or is neither a file nor a directory, and an invalid --output-formats or --min-severity value 5 An output directory it cannot use, refused as a scan refuses it (ash scan): it is not a directory, it cannot be created, entered, or written, or it is not a valid path because it holds a NUL character, which a --cli-json-input document can carry. The merge prints the scan's Output directory line for it, with the path as given, on standard output, where it prints its log, and creates nothing. An output directory that does not exist is created

A shard whose scanner is ERROR only because its content database is stale counts as having completed that scanner: ash merge merges the shard and then exits 1 for the stale database.

A --results path that does not exist is a usage error:

ash merge --results no-such-shard --output-dir merged

docs.title: ash report
docs.text:
ash report never fails on findings.

Code Condition 0 The report was printed 1 Results that cannot be read; the reporter failed; an AWS reporter's pre-flight check refused, for a missing setting or for credentials it cannot find (AWS reporters) 3 The output directory, a directory on the way to it, or reports in it is a link (Output files) 3 The --config file cannot be used or is invalid, as for a scan, including an option that a plugin loaded from ash_plugin_modules does not accept; an override is invalid; or the configuration recorded in the results reads a field that takes a fixed choice, a boolean, or a number from the environment, and neither --config-overrides nor --config supplies the field; or two reporters that the command loads have the same name or names that read as one, as for a scan 5 No results to report on, or a results file in more than one of the places an output directory is searched (nothing is created, and an output directory under a directory ASH cannot search counts as one with no results); an output directory that is a file (Output directory is not a directory:), or a path the system cannot look up, such as one holding a NUL character (Output directory is not a valid path:), each with the path as given; an unknown --format, also when there are no results; an output directory that exists but cannot be entered (Output directory cannot be entered: and the path as given); any other usage error

ASH checks the config first, then --format, then the results:

ash report --output-dir no-scan-here --format bogus

docs.title: ash mcp
docs.text:
Code Condition 0 The stdio transport's input closed, also while the server was writing to it; or the server was stopped with SIGTERM or SIGHUP: a stdio server on Linux and macOS, or an HTTP server with SIGHUP 1 The MCP dependencies are not installed, or an error stopped the server while it started or ran, on any transport, other than an HTTP server that fails to start (3). The error is printed on stderr, also with --quiet. 3 A --profile that cannot be registered: no =, a file that does not exist or does not load, an unknown top-level key, or a name given twice. An ASH_CONFIG that names a path that is not a file, a file the server cannot read, or a config that does not load or validate, on every transport; an empty ASH_CONFIG counts as unset. Also when an HTTP server fails to start, for example because it cannot bind its port: the HTTP server exits 3 for that. 5 A usage error, such as an unknown option, a --port that is not a number, an invalid --transport or ASH_MCP_TRANSPORT, --quiet with --verbose or --debug, only one of --auth-header-name and --auth-header-value, or --stateless-http without the streamable-http transport. Also these refusals at startup: --trust-upstream-session-id anywhere other than --transport streamable-http --stateless-http; --trust-upstream-host-check on stdio, with a loopback --host, or with --allowed-host; a non-loopback --host with neither --allowed-host nor --trust-upstream-host-check; and a --session-workspace-ttl that is not a positive number of seconds, or is given on stdio 130 The server was stopped with Ctrl-C, on any transport 143 An HTTP server was stopped with SIGTERM: the HTTP server ends the process with the signal, which a shell reports as 128 + 15

A scan's own errors end that scan as failed, not the server. On Windows a stdio server has no SIGTERM handling: the process that ends it sets its exit code. Ctrl-C there ends a stdio server with 130 only once the client has closed the connection.

ash mcp --transport bogus

docs.title: ash config
docs.text:
Command Code Condition ash config init 0 The file was written 1 The file exists and --force is not given. When neither --config nor ASH_CONFIG names the file, also when the directory already has another config source, which --force does not override. ash config get 0 The resolved config was printed (the defaults, when no config file is found) 3 The named config path does not exist, is a directory, or cannot be read; the config does not parse or does not validate; or an override does not validate ash config update 0 The file was updated, no --set was given, or --dry-run was given with --set values it can apply 1 No config file is found; the file is TOML, uses extends or patch, or reads values from the environment; it cannot be written 3 The named config path does not exist, is a directory, or cannot be read; the file is not UTF-8, does not load, or does not validate; a --set value does not parse (no =, or nothing before it), starts with a top-level key the configuration does not have, or leaves a config a scan would refuse. update prints Not updating <file>: ... and leaves the file unchanged, also with --dry-run, and applies no other --set given with it. ash config validate 0 A scan accepts the config, apart from the options of plugins loaded from ash_plugin_modules, which only a scan checks. Warnings may be printed, for example for a missing project_name, which a scan does not need, or for an ignore or suppression path that names an existing directory and matches no file in it (Check a config). 1 No config file is found in the source directory and none is named: validate says so, and that a scan of that directory uses the default configuration. Also when an error occurred. 3 The named config path does not exist, is a directory, or cannot be read. A scan refuses the config: it does not parse, it or an override does not validate (one plugin's section written under two spellings included), its extends chain does not resolve, or ash_plugin_modules names a module a scan refuses. validate imports no plugin module, so two plugins whose names read as one pass it. 5 The source directory (--source-dir or ASH_SOURCE_DIR) does not exist, is not a directory, or cannot be entered, refused with the line a scan prints ash config lint 0 A scan accepts the config (warnings and notes are allowed), apart from the options of plugins loaded from ash_plugin_modules. Also when a fix prompt was declined, if a scan accepts the file. 1 No config file is found; --fix or --fix-unused refused to rewrite the file (a TOML file, --fix-unused on a JSON file, or --fix with something to fix on a file that reads values from the environment); an error that a scan accepts remains 3 As for validate, also after a declined fix prompt. With --fix, the code describes the file after the fixes. ash config validate-plugin-dependencies 0 The config resolves (project_name has a default, so the file does not need to set it) 1 No config file is found 3 The named config path does not exist, is a directory, or cannot be read, or the config does not resolve ash config wizard 0 The file was written 1 The file is TOML, uses extends or patch, or reads values from the environment; a prompt was aborted 3 The file cannot be loaded

The named config path is the one --config, ASH_CONFIG, or the path argument of get, update, and validate-plugin-dependencies gives. An ASH_CONFIG that names a file that does not exist exits 3 from get, validate, lint, and validate-plugin-dependencies even when --config or the path argument names a file that loads, since a scan refuses that pair too. Configure ASH explains what validate, lint, and get check.

ash config init refuses to add a second config source:

mkdir -p .ash && printf 'project_name: payments-api\n' > .ash/.ash.yaml
ash config init

A named config path that does not exist or is a directory exits 3 from every ash config command that reads a config:

ash config get --config no-such-config.yaml

ash config validate --config .ash

ash config lint --config no-such-config.yaml

ash config validate-plugin-dependencies --config no-such-config.yaml

So does an ASH_CONFIG that names one, beside a --config file that loads:

printf 'project_name: payments-api\n' > named.yaml
ASH_CONFIG=no-such-config.yaml ash config lint --config named.yaml

ash config update refuses a file that is not UTF-8 the same way, and leaves it unchanged:

printf '\377\376' > not-utf8.yaml
ash config update --config not-utf8.yaml --set fail_on_findings=false

A config without project_name is valid, with a warning:

printf 'global_settings:\n  severity_threshold: HIGH\n' > no-name.yaml
ash config validate --config no-name.yaml

A --set without = leaves the file unchanged and exits 3:

ash config update --set fail_on_findings

So does a --set whose top-level key the configuration does not have, such as the misspelled fail_on_finding. A top-level key may be written with - for _, as in a config file, so --set fail-on-findings=false sets fail_on_findings:

ash config update --set fail_on_finding=false
