A config that a scan refuses exits 3 from ash config validate, here for the misspelled rule_id:

cat > misspelled.yaml <<'EOF'
project_name: payments-api
global_settings:
  suppressions:
    - path: app.py
      ruleId: SECRET-SECRET-KEYWORD
      reason: Fixture value, not a real password
EOF
ash config validate --config misspelled.yaml

docs.title: Other commands
docs.text:
Command Code Condition ash dependencies install 0 Without --tool: every tool that a scan with the same configuration on this platform would run is present after the install. With --tool: every named plugin's tool is present; the other plugins are not installed and do not count. 1 For a plugin that counts (one such a scan would run, or with --tool one it names): an install command failed, the plugin raised an error, or its tool is still absent. Without --tool, a plugin the scan skips (disabled in the config, or not available on this platform) does not count. 2 A --tool name matches no plugin, or names a plugin of a type that --plugin-type leaves out; or a --plugin-type is not converter, scanner, or reporter. ASH names the tool or the type, installs nothing, and starts no program. 3 The config cannot be used or is invalid, as for a scan, or an override does not validate; or there is no usable home directory, so nowhere to keep install receipts, whatever --bin-path says: HOME is empty or relative, or unset with no absolute home in the passwd entry. Nothing is installed ash plugin list 0 The lists were printed, also when a plugin module is skipped 1 Any other error 3 The config cannot be used or is invalid, as for a scan, or an override does not validate ash get-genai-guide 0 The guide was written 1 The installation has no readable copy of the guide; with --from-github, the download failed; or the output directory does not exist ash inspect findings 0 Always, also when there are no results to show ash inspect sarif-fields 0 The analysis was written 1 No SARIF files were found, or a scanner's field is missing from the aggregated SARIF 
tool=not-a-tool
ash dependencies install --tool "${tool}"

docs.title: MCP tools reference
docs.text:
This page is generated from the tools and resources the ASH MCP server registers, with editorial notes kept in the generator by scripts/generate_mcp_tool_reference.py. Edits made to this file by hand are overwritten the next time it is generated.

The ASH MCP server exposes twenty-two tools and five resources.

docs.title: run_ash_scan
docs.text:
Starts a scan in the server process and returns a scan_id at once. The scan stops if the server process exits; over stdio, that is when the client disconnects.

Param Type Default Notes source_dir string | null not set Absolute path to scan. When not set: the tree this session delivered with set_source_git or set_source_zip_finalize. With none delivered, a call with no session id (stdio) scans the server's working directory, and a call with a session id is refused severity_threshold string | null not set Least severe finding that counts as actionable, any case; it can make the config's global_settings.severity_threshold stricter for this scan, never looser config_path string | null not set Custom config path. When not set: the profile this session bound with select_profile, else the config ASH discovers in the source directory, else the file ASH_CONFIG names in the server's environment, else the built-in defaults clean_output boolean true Set the previous scan's results in the output directory aside as soon as the scan is registered; with false, the scan's own set-up does it a moment later. Either way they are deleted once the scan has results of its own, and put back if it fails or is canceled. A refused call leaves the previous results as they were

Output reports are written to <source_dir>/.ash/ash_output/ — there is no parameter to override this. Scanner selection, mode, and other tuning live in the project's ASH config, not in tool arguments.

Returns:

{
  "success": true,
  "status": "running",
  "scan_id": "<uuid>",
  "progress": 0.0,
  "message": "Scan started, initializing scanners. Use get_scan_progress to track progress.",
  "directory_path": "<absolute path scanned>",
  "important": {
    "connection_management": "<server's polling guidance>",
    "next_steps": ["..."]
  }
}

The directory_path field tells you the resolved absolute path the server is scanning — derive output_dir for get_scan_results from this value (<directory_path>/.ash/ash_output) rather than constructing it independently.

Poll get_scan_progress until is_complete is true, then read status. is_complete is true for every ending, including failed and cancelled. (See get_scan_progress below.)

A refused config keeps its own error_type. The scan does not start, and the response is success: false with one of these error_type values and the reason in error:

  • config_input_not_permitted: config_path, or a base its extends chain names, is outside the directories this session may read a config from.
  • config_check_failed: the check of the config sources in the scan target could not finish (an unreadable entry, a link loop), so the scan was not started. The config was not found to be outside the permitted roots -- that case is config_input_not_permitted -- so check the config files in the target for unreadable entries and link loops.
  • config_field_denied: a config file an MCP client delivered or named sets a field the session's runtime-override policy denies. error names each field and why.
  • config_policy_unreadable: that policy cannot be established, for example because the profile the session bound is no longer registered. error starts with A config an MCP client delivered cannot be checked:.
  • config_env_not_resolved: a file of the config uses an !ENV tag, or a plain value that starts with a ${VAR} or ${VAR:default} reference, where none is resolved. For a remote caller that is any file the operator did not set aside (outside the directories ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_CONFIG_ROOTS names, other than the profile files the server writes in the calling session's config/ directory), the scan target's own config included, and every base such a file extends; for a stdio caller, a file a client delivered. The server's own config, the file ASH_CONFIG names outside the MCP workspace root and each registered profile, is not refused. error names the file and the line or key.

The target and source checks have their own error_type values too (scan_target_not_permitted, output_dir_not_permitted, no_source_delivered, session_source_mismatch, delivered_source_missing, invalid_session_id). A directory that already has a scan is refused with error_type: MCPResourceError and error_category: resource_exhausted; error says the directory already has an active scan, or, for a scan that was cancelled or stopped at its timeout and has not finished stopping, has a scan that is still stopping. That error_type is the exception's class name, and an unexpected error while the scan is being started arrives as MCPResourceError too, with error_category: unexpected_error, so MCPResourceError alone does not prove a deliberate refusal: branch on error_category. The server's max_concurrent_scans limit is refused the same way (resource_exhausted); its context holds max_concurrent_scans: wait for a running scan to finish, then retry. The busy-directory refusal's context names the running scan's scan_id only when the scan is this session's: poll get_scan_progress with it, or cancel_scan it if it is no longer needed (list_active_scans lists this session's scans). Without a scan_id, another session's scan holds the directory and the server does not name it: wait and retry, or scan another directory. After a cancel_scan of that directory the refusal repeats until the scan has stopped (see cancel_scan): retry after a few seconds. Any other reason the scan could not be started returns error_type: scan_start_failure, and an unexpected error returns the exception's class name. Branch on error_type and error_category, never on the text of error.

On failure, error_type is one of committed_output_files, config_env_not_resolved, config_field_denied, config_input_not_permitted, config_policy_unreadable, delivered_source_missing, invalid_session_id, no_source_delivered, output_dir_not_permitted, output_dir_not_usable, scan_start_failure, scan_target_not_permitted, session_identity_required, session_scan_limit, session_source_mismatch, source_delivery_busy and source_dir_not_usable, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: get_scan_progress
docs.text:
Poll progress every 5 seconds until is_complete is true, then read status: completed, incomplete, failed, or cancelled. The scan continues server-side independently of polling.

Param Type Notes scan_id string From run_ash_scan

Returns:

{
  "scan_id": "...",
  "directory_path": "/path/to/scanned/project",
  "output_directory": "/path/to/.ash/ash_output",
  "start_time": "<iso8601>",
  "end_time": "<iso8601 | null>",
  "status": "pending | running | completed | incomplete | failed | cancelled",
  "severity_threshold": "<the threshold the scan was judged by; null until it finishes when none was named>",
  "config_path": "<path | null>",
  "warnings": [...],
  "error_message": "<str | null>",
  "is_complete": bool,
  "results_available": bool,
  "output_holds_previous_results": bool,
  "coverage_complete": "bool | null",
  "incomplete_scanners": [
    { "scanner": "grype", "status": "MISSING", "reason": "missing_dependencies", "detail": "MISSING" }
  ],
  "no_scanner_ran": bool,
  "incomplete_converters": [{ "converter": "...", "reason": "...", "failed_input_kinds": ["..."] }],
  "unevaluated_rules": ["..."],
  "stale_content_databases": [{ "name": "grype-db", "scanner": "grype", "built": "<iso8601 | null>", "age": "...", "max_age": "...", "refresh": "..." }],
  "completed_scanners": int,
  "finished_scanners": int,
  "total_scanners": int,
  "scanner_status_counts": { "passed": int, "failed": int, "skipped": int, "running": int, "pending": int },
  "total_findings": int,
  "severity_counts": { "critical": int, "high": int, "medium": int, "low": int, "info": int, "suppressed": int },
  "scanners": {
    "<scanner_name>": {
      "<target_type>": { ... per-scanner-target progress ... }
    }
  }
}

There is no overall percentage field. To compute progress, use finished_scanners / total_scanners: finished_scanners counts every scanner that has ended, whatever its status, and completed_scanners only the ones that PASSED. scanner_status_counts splits them into passed, failed (FAILED or ERROR), skipped (MISSING or SKIPPED), running, and pending. Guard against total_scanners == 0 during the pre-flight phase (before any scanner has registered). Show "initializing" or 0% when total_scanners is zero.

There is no top-level duration field; derive elapsed time from start_time and end_time (or from current time while running).

is_complete is true once the scan has ended, whatever the ending: completed, incomplete, failed or cancelled. It is decided by the scan's state alone, never by a results file on disk, which can be a previous scan's. results_available is true for completed and incomplete, the scans whose results get_scan_results can read.

A failed or cancelled scan leaves the previous scan's results in place. ASH puts them back in output_directory, and output_holds_previous_results is then true and the scanner fields are empty, because those files are not this scan's. get_scan_results on that directory reads the previous scan's results.

incomplete is terminal, with partial coverage. The run finished and its results are readable, but a selected scanner was MISSING or ERROR (or lost targets), no scanner reached a verdict, a converter did not run or could not convert some of its inputs, a rule could not be evaluated, or a content database was past its declared age bound. incomplete_scanners names each scanner and why, and stale_content_databases each stale database. The findings are real but partial, so read them, and do not report the target as clean. failed means the run crashed, left no readable results, or ran past the server's scan_timeout_seconds. coverage_complete is null while running and for failed or cancelled; with fail_on_incomplete_scanners: false a scan is completed with coverage_complete: false when scanners did not run.

Status enum: the documented values are pending | running | completed | incomplete | failed | cancelled. The registry uses pending briefly while a scan is queued, transitions to running once execution begins, and may also expose the legacy in_progress string from older ScanProgress instances. Treat pending, running, and in_progress as equivalent "not done yet" states.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id, scan_not_found and session_identity_required, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: get_scan_results
docs.text:
Fetch finalized results with filtering. Run only after get_scan_progress reports complete.

Param Type Default Notes output_dir string ".ash/ash_output" Absolute path strongly recommended; the server resolves relative paths against its own cwd, which usually isn't your project root filter_level string "full" full, summary, minimal scanners string not set Comma-separated subset; not set means every scanner severities string not set Comma-separated subset of critical,high,medium,low,info,suppressed; not set means every severity actionable_only boolean false Keep only the actionable findings, the ones behind exit code 2: unsuppressed and at or above the severity threshold the scan was judged by (a scanner's own where its config sets one). Drop the rest and add findings, a flat list of them that honors scanners and severities (full level only)

With filter_level full, raw_results is the aggregated results document without its sarif, cyclonedx, and ash_config sections; summary returns the metadata and the counts by severity and by scanner, and minimal the status. Individual findings are in the report files: get_scan_result_paths lists them, and the flat-json reporter, which is enabled by default, writes reports/ash.flat.json under output_dir.

status is completed or incomplete, decided by the same rule as the scan's exit code, with coverage_complete and incomplete_scanners as in get_scan_progress. An incomplete scan's findings are returned in full.

On failure, error_type is invalid_session_id, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: get_scan_summary
docs.text:
Metadata and counts only — no individual findings. Cheap for quick health checks.

Param Type Default Notes output_dir string ".ash/ash_output" Absolute path

Returns total count, severity breakdown, scanner statuses.

On failure, error_type is invalid_session_id, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: get_scan_result_paths
docs.text:
Returns file paths to all generated reports. Useful when you want to read HTML, SARIF, CSV, or markdown directly with file tools instead of pulling JSON over MCP.

Param Type Default Notes output_dir string ".ash/ash_output" Absolute path

Returns a dict mapping format names to absolute paths.

On failure, error_type is one of DirectoryNotFound, invalid_session_id and scan_target_not_permitted, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: list_active_scans
docs.text:
All scans the server tracks (active + recently completed).

No parameters. Returns a list of scan summaries.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id and session_identity_required, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: cancel_scan
docs.text:
Stops a running scan. The scanner tool running at the time is stopped with every process it started (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 10 seconds). The scan halts at its next cancel check, and no further scanner, phase, or reporter starts, so a scan canceled before its report phase writes no reports. Work that is not waiting on a child process, such as a scanner parsing its tool's output, can still finish and write under scanners/ or converted/, but ash_aggregated_results.json is not written after the cancel. When the output directory held a previous scan's results, they are put back in place of every result the canceled scan wrote; its log, ash.log, stays, and an ash.log.jsonl already there is left as it was. With no previous results, what the scan wrote before it stopped stays, except that a cancel during the report phase removes the reports that phase wrote. reports/ash.unused-suppressions.md, which its reporter writes on its own, stays even then.

Param Type Notes scan_id string The scan to cancel

Returns success, status, and message. The status is cancelled at once. A running scan stops within about 10 seconds; one still waiting for another scan of its session stops when that scan ends. Until it has stopped, run_ash_scan refuses another scan of the same directory as still stopping, and the scan counts against max_concurrent_scans. A scan that has already ended is not changed, and the response has success: false and the scan's status. For a run_ash_workspace_scan, cancel_scan takes one project's scan id and stops that project, which ends failed; the other projects carry on.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id and session_identity_required, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: check_installation
docs.text:
Reports whether ASH can scan: its version and, for each built-in scanner, whether its tool can run. Enabled means enabled in ASH's defaults: the call reads no project's config and checks no plugin scanner. It runs each scanner's dependency check, which can start the tool, so it takes several seconds, and it installs and downloads nothing. The tool of a scanner that ASH installs with uv is installed when uv tool list lists it, or when its executable is on PATH or in a directory ASH also searches, such as ~/.ash/bin. A scanner whose tool is not, when the server is online and has uv, is listed in installs_on_first_scan, because the first scan installs it with uv, which needs network access. Offline, or without uv, it is listed in missing_dependencies. Offline, semgrep is also missing when it has no rules cache.

No parameters. Returns installed (at least one enabled scanner can run, or will once the first scan installs its tool), ready (every enabled scanner can run or will), version, scanners (each scanner's name, enabled, dependencies_satisfied, installs_on_first_scan, and version), installs_on_first_scan, missing_dependencies and undetermined_dependencies (the enabled scanners whose tool is missing and that a scan cannot install, or whose check could not run), and ash_command_available (whether an ash executable is on PATH, which the server does not need).

On failure, error_type is invalid_session_id, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: clear_source
docs.text:
Delete this session's delivered source tree and workspace.

No parameters. Deletes this session's delivered source tree and workspace.

Refused while a scan of this session is running: success: false, error_type: source_delivery_busy. Clear again once the scan ends. Entries the server cannot delete (files another account owns) stay on disk; the session's delivered source is forgotten either way.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id, session_identity_required and source_delivery_busy, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: diff_scan_results
docs.text:
Compare two ash_aggregated_results.json files and return a structured diff.

Param Type Notes before_path string Path to the baseline ash_aggregated_results.json file. after_path string Path to the comparison ash_aggregated_results.json file.

On failure, error_type is invalid_session_id, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: explain_finding
docs.text:
Return structured details for a single finding by ID.

Param Type Default Notes finding_id string required The FlatVulnerability ID to look up (e.g. "bandit-B601-880359fd90e1"). results_path string | null not set Optional path to the output directory containing ash_aggregated_results.json. Defaults to <cwd>/.ash/ash_output.

On failure, error_type is invalid_session_id, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: get_config
docs.text:
Get the resolved ASH config (defaults + user overrides merged).

Param Type Default Notes config_path string | null not set Optional explicit path to config file. If None, auto-discovers. raw boolean false If True, returns the file's contents as written, without merging defaults or reading the environment. A value the config's loader would read from the environment (an !ENV value, or an unquoted ${VAR:default}) comes back as !ENV and the reference, never as its value; a quoted string that only looks like a reference comes back as written. search_dir string | null not set The directory the caller's scan will target (scan_directory's directory_path). With config_path None it is where the config is discovered; with a named config_path it is the target the file is judged for, so the answer refuses exactly what a scan of that target refuses -- an entry such a scan drops with a warning never refuses the answer. Without it, a named file is judged for this session's delivered source, or else the server's working directory.

A config this session may not read, or one a client delivered that the server refuses, returns success: false with error_type config_input_not_permitted, config_field_denied, config_policy_unreadable or config_env_not_resolved, as run_ash_scan does for the same file.

On failure, error_type is one of config_env_not_resolved, config_field_denied, config_input_not_permitted, config_policy_unreadable, invalid_session_id, plugin_module_refused, scan_target_not_permitted and source_dir_not_usable, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: list_profiles
docs.text:
List the config profiles the operator registered at server startup.

No parameters. Returns the config profiles the operator registered at server startup, each with ash mcp --profile NAME=path/to/ash.yaml (repeatable). A client cannot register one; an empty list means the operator registered none.

On failure, error_type is the class name of an exception.

docs.title: list_scanners
docs.text:
List all registered ASH scanners with their metadata.

No parameters. Returns one entry per registered scanner with its config name, detected version, and whether it is enabled.

docs.title: resolve_ash_workspace
docs.text:
Resolve a VS Code workspace file into a scan plan without scanning anything.

Param Type Default Notes workspace_file string required Absolute path to the .code-workspace file. workspace_config string | null not set Optional path to a workspace policy file. Must exist if given; ASH will not fall back to searching for one. allow_missing_projects boolean false Mark project directories that are absent or unreadable as skipped instead of refusing the workspace. config_overrides array | null not set Optional list of key=value config overrides, applied to each project's config so the reported threshold is the enforced one. profile string | null not set Name of a registered config profile to resolve under for this one call, instead of whatever select_profile bound to this session. Call list_profiles to see what the operator registered. The fields the profile sets are final for every project, and a project's own config fills the rest.

A workspace policy file, named or found in the workspace file's directory or its .ash directory, is used only when it is in a directory ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_CONFIG_ROOTS names; any other refuses the workspace with exit code 4, or with exit code 3 when a client delivered it and it sets a field the server's policy denies.

On failure, error_type is one of config_env_not_resolved, config_input_not_permitted, environment_value_in_longer_string, invalid_session_id and output_dir_not_usable, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: run_ash_workspace_scan
docs.text:
Scan every project in a VS Code workspace and return the per-project verdict.

Param Type Default Notes workspace_file string required Absolute path to the .code-workspace file. workspace_config string | null not set Optional path to a workspace policy file. allow_missing_projects boolean false Skip absent or unreadable project directories rather than refusing the workspace. config_overrides array | null not set Optional list of key=value config overrides. output_dir string | null not set Where to write the workspace output tree. Defaults to <workspace root>/.ash/ash_output. Refused when it, a directory or file ASH writes in it, or a project's projects/<key> is a symlink. scanners array | null not set Restrict every project to these scanner names. excluded_scanners array | null not set Exclude these scanners from every project. Takes precedence over scanners. offline boolean false Run without network access. clean_output boolean true Hide each project's previous results once the scan has its directory. Either way they are put back for a project whose scan does not finish. A scan refused because a project already has a scan touches nothing in any project's output. profile string | null not set Name of a registered config profile to scan under for this one call, instead of whatever select_profile bound to this session. An unknown name refuses the whole scan; running N repository scans under the default config because a profile name was misspelled, and reporting success, is exactly what the confinement refusal above exists to prevent. The fields the profile sets are final for every project, and a project's own config fills the rest.

A workspace policy file, named or found in the workspace file's directory or its .ash directory, is used only when it is in a directory ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_CONFIG_ROOTS names; any other refuses the workspace with exit code 4, or with exit code 3 when a client delivered it and it sets a field the server's policy denies.

On failure, error_type is one of config_env_not_resolved, config_input_not_permitted, environment_value_in_longer_string, invalid_session_id, output_dir_not_usable, session_scan_limit and source_delivery_busy, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: select_profile
docs.text:
Bind one of the operator's registered config profiles to this session.

Param Type Default Notes profile_name string required Name the operator registered the profile under. patch_ops array | null not set JSON-Patch operations to apply to the profile's config. override_yaml string | null not set Complete ASH config YAML replacing the profile's.

On failure, error_type is one of environment_value_in_longer_string, invalid_session_id, session_identity_required and session_workspace_busy, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: set_source_git
docs.text:
Clone a repository into this session's workspace and make it the scan target.

Param Type Default Notes url string required Repository URL ref string | null not set Branch, tag, or commit; not set means the remote's default branch ssh_key_id string | null not set Leave it out: the server registers no SSH keys, so any value is refused depth integer 1 Clone depth, a whole number of commits from 1 to 1000

Refused while a scan of this session is running, because the clone would replace the tree and config files that scan is reading. The response is success: false, error_type: source_delivery_busy, and error set to a scan of this session is running; change the delivered source after it finishes. Deliver the source again once get_scan_progress reports a terminal status.

A refusal or a git failure returns success: false with an error_type: clone_url_not_permitted (a url beginning with - or using the ext:: transport, a url holding a control character or a lone surrogate, or a url whose host cannot be read), clone_ref_not_permitted (a ref beginning with - or holding a control character or a lone surrogate), invalid_clone_depth (below 1 or above 1000; the limit is on how much history is fetched), invalid_session_id, local_clone_source_refused (a local path or file:// url, which would read the server's own filesystem), clone_host_not_permitted (the host is not in ASH_MCP_GIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS), ssh_key_not_registered (an ssh_key_id was named), clone_timed_out (git ran past its time limit and was stopped), git_clone_failed or git_checkout_failed (git's own message is in error; git_clone_failed also covers a git that is not on PATH or cannot be started), or session_workspace_unavailable (the session's workspace could not take the clone: a directory of it could not be created, the previously delivered source could not be moved aside for it, or the clone could not be moved into place; each move is tried a few times before it fails). The clone is made beside the delivered source and replaces it only once it has worked, so a delivery that fails for any of these reasons, or is refused, leaves the previously delivered source in place, and run_ash_scan with no source_dir scans it. A partial clone that cannot be fully deleted stays beside the source, logged, for the next delivery to delete, and the error returned is still git's own. The one exception is a clone that could not be moved into place after the previous source had been moved aside and could not be put back: the recorded source then names a path that is gone, and run_ash_scan with no source_dir answers delivered_source_missing until a source is delivered again; that next delivery puts the previous source back first. A session_workspace_unavailable that names a refused rename can be retried with the same call: the refusal is usually a program holding a handle inside a tree (a virus scanner, a file indexer), and it passes.

A re-delivery needs room for both trees at once, because the new clone is made beside the delivered source, which is deleted only after it. When the disk is short, call clear_source first to free the delivered one. A clone, fetch or checkout that fails for want of space returns git_clone_failed or git_checkout_failed with git's own message, and that advice added when the session has a delivered source to free.

On failure, error_type is one of clone_host_not_permitted, clone_ref_not_permitted, clone_timed_out, clone_too_large, clone_tree_unreadable, clone_url_not_permitted, git_checkout_failed, git_clone_failed, invalid_clone_depth, invalid_session_id, local_clone_source_refused, session_identity_required, session_workspace_unavailable, source_delivery_busy and ssh_key_not_registered, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: set_source_zip_chunk
docs.text:
Upload one base64 chunk of a zipped source tree.

Param Type Notes upload_id string Caller-chosen id tying the chunks of one upload together sequence integer Zero-based chunk index; chunks must arrive in order data_b64 string Base64 of this chunk's bytes last boolean true on the final chunk

Pair with set_source_zip_finalize, which verifies the reassembled archive against expected_sha256 before extracting it. A chunked upload that is never finalized is not a scan target.

When the session's workspace directory cannot be created, both upload tools return success: false with error_type session_workspace_unavailable.

While the server removes the session's workspace for being unused longer than its time to live, set_source_zip_chunk returns success: false with error_type session_workspace_busy. Send the upload again from its first chunk.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id, session_identity_required, session_workspace_busy and session_workspace_unavailable, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: set_source_zip_finalize
docs.text:
Verify an uploaded zip and extract it as this session's scan target.

Param Type Notes upload_id string The identifier used for the preceding chunk calls. expected_sha256 string Hex sha256 of the complete zip.

Refused while a scan of this session is running, for the same reason as set_source_git: success: false, error_type: source_delivery_busy, and error set to a scan of this session is running; change the delivered source after it finishes. set_source_zip_chunk is not refused, so the chunks can be sent while the scan runs and the upload finalized after it ends.

A finalize that cannot deliver returns success: false with an error. Its error_type is session_workspace_unavailable when the session's workspace could not take the tree: a directory of it could not be created, the previous tree could not be renamed aside (nothing is deleted where it stands), or the extracted one could not be moved into place, whatever the operating system error was. The previous tree stays delivered and the uploaded zip is kept, so the same call can be sent again; when the previous tree could not be put back either, run_ash_scan with no source_dir answers delivered_source_missing. A checksum mismatch, an upload that never received its last chunk, or an archive the limits refuse returns error with no error_type. An archive that is not a zip returns error_type BadZipFile, and a failure on disk while the archive is read or extracted (no space, no permission, a file that vanished) returns the class name of the exception, OSError or one of its subclasses; both carry an error that starts Error finalizing source upload:.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id, session_identity_required, session_workspace_unavailable and source_delivery_busy, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: suggest_suppression
docs.text:
Build a paste-ready AshSuppression entry for a specific finding.

Param Type Default Notes finding_id string required Stable hash ID of the finding (from get_scan_results or explain_finding). results_path string | null not set Path to ash_aggregated_results.json. Defaults to .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json in cwd. expiration string | null not set Expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to 90 days from today. justification string | null not set Human-readable reason for the suppression.

On failure, error_type is one of invalid_session_id and path_not_expressible, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: validate_config
docs.text:
Validate an ASH configuration file or content string.

Param Type Default Notes config_content string | null not set YAML/JSON string to validate. config_path string | null not set Path to the config file to validate.

config_content counts as the client's config, and so does a config_path that a client delivered or that is outside the directories ASH_MCP_ALLOWED_CONFIG_ROOTS names and its session's config/ directory. Each field such a config may not set under the server's runtime-override policy is an error of type denied_by_runtime_policy, and a policy the server cannot read is one error of type config_policy_unreadable; for config_content, both only when a remote client calls. A ${VAR} or ${VAR:default} reference at the start of a plain value, or an !ENV tag, in such a config is an error of type config_env_not_resolved.

Each entry of errors has a type that is one of config_env_not_resolved, config_input_not_permitted, config_policy_unreadable, denied_by_runtime_policy, duplicate_field, extends_error, file_not_found, internal_field, invalid_field, invalid_session_id, json_parse_error, missing_input, missing_required_field, toml_parse_error, unknown_field, validation_error and yaml_parse_error, or the class name of an exception.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• ash://exit-codes — Return the meaning of each ASH exit code as JSON
  • ash://help — Get help information about ASH usage
  • ash://schema/config — Return the AshConfig JSON schema
  • ash://schema/suppression — Return the AshSuppression JSON schema
  • ash://status — Get the current status of ASH installation

Read these via the standard MCP resource read mechanism for context-free help.

docs.title: Severity levels
docs.text:
CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW > INFO > SUPPRESSED

actionable_only=True drops SUPPRESSED findings (false positives, accepted risks) and findings below the scan's severity threshold, which are reported but do not fail the scan.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: What a scan writes to its output directory. The output directory is <source-dir>/.ash/ash_output unless you pass --output-dir; see Read scan results for which file to open for what.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
A scan of a project with Python, a CloudFormation template, and a GitHub Actions workflow, with every built-in scanner installed:

.ash/ash_output/
├── ash.log
├── ash_aggregated_results.json
├── ash-ignore-report.txt
├── ash-scan-set-files-list.txt
├── analysis/
├── converted/
├── reports/
│   ├── ash.cdx.json
│   ├── ash.csv
│   ├── ash.flat.json
│   ├── ash.ghas.sarif
│   ├── ash.gl-dependency-scanning-report.cdx.json
│   ├── ash.gl-sast-report.json
│   ├── ash.html
│   ├── ash.junit.xml
│   ├── ash.ocsf.json
│   ├── ash.sarif
│   ├── ash.summary.md
│   ├── ash.summary.txt
│   ├── ash.unused-suppressions.json
│   └── ash.unused-suppressions.md
└── scanners/
    ├── bandit/
    │   └── source/
    │       ├── ASH.ScanResults.json
    │       ├── BanditScanner.stderr.log
    │       └── bandit.sarif
    ├── checkov/
    │   └── source/
    │       ├── ASH.ScanResults.json
    │       ├── CheckovScanner.stdout.log
    │       ├── results_cyclonedx.json
    │       └── results_sarif.sarif
    └── ...one directory for every scanner
Path Written by Contents ash.log ASH's logger The run's log, INFO and above by default, one tab-separated line per record: time, level, source location, and message. Lines from a scanner have a field before the message naming the scanner and target, such as ([yellow]bandit[/yellow] @ [magenta]source[/magenta]), and messages can contain the same Rich markup. ash_aggregated_results.json the scan engine Every result of the scan in one document. See below. ash-ignore-report.txt the scan set step The ignore rules that shaped the scan set: the text of each .gitignore and .ignore ASH found, and ASH's built-in rules (.git and **/cdk.out/asset.* left out, **/*.template.json kept). ash-scan-set-files-list.txt the scan set step The files ASH selected, one absolute path per line. Scanners that walk the source directory themselves can read more; see Coverage. analysis/ ash scan --inspect The SARIF field analysis. Empty otherwise. converted/ the converters archive/ holds a directory per .zip, .tar, or .gz file with the members ASH extracted; jupyter/ holds each notebook converted to a script, named after the notebook's path and ending in -converted.py for a Python notebook (see Converted files). Empty when there was nothing to convert. reports/ the reporters One file per enabled reporter, named ash.<extension>. See below. scanners/<name>/<target>/ each scanner ASH.ScanResults.json and the tool's own output for one target: source for the source directory, converted for converted/. See below.

In workspace mode the workspace's output directory holds the combined ash_aggregated_results.json, and each project's own output tree is under projects/<project>/. The workspace's reports/ holds the reports that combine every project, and workspace-reports.json, which lists where each project's own reports are. The reporters that write one file per project, cyclonedx, spdx, github-ghas, gitlab-sast, and gitlab-cyclonedx, write nothing at the workspace level; their files are in each project's reports/. See Scale to large repositories.

docs.title: Each scan replaces the last
docs.text:
Before a scan writes anything, ASH removes and recreates analysis/, reports/, scanners/, and converted/, and deletes ash_aggregated_results.json, ash-ignore-report.txt, and ash-scan-set-files-list.txt. ash.log is truncated when the logger opens it.

So a scan that fails leaves only what it wrote before it failed: gate CI on ASH's exit code, not on whether reports/ exists. Container mode and Nix mode delete the same entries before they start the scan.

In local mode, ASH clears the output directory only after it has accepted the command line and the configuration. A scan refused before that leaves the earlier results in place: an unknown option or scanner name, or a selection that excludes every scanner it names (exit 5), or a configuration that does not validate (exit 3). Only ash.log is rewritten. For example, after a scan of the sample project:

ash scan --scanners detect-secrets

a scan that names a scanner ASH does not have is refused:

ash scan --scanners not-a-scanner

and the first scan's results are still there:

test -f .ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json

A scan started over MCP keeps the previous results until it has its own. When it starts, the server moves the previous reports/, scanners/, analysis/, converted/, ash_aggregated_results.json, ash-ignore-report.txt, and ash-scan-set-files-list.txt into .ash_previous_results/ in the output directory. When the scan finishes with results, they are deleted. When it fails or is canceled, the server removes what the scan wrote, puts them back, and writes .ash_previous_results_restored beside them. The next scan removes that file, and the next ash scan also deletes a held .ash_previous_results/. For a scan whose previous results were put back, get_scan_progress returns output_holds_previous_results: true, and the tools that read results from the directory, such as get_scan_results, answer that the scan is not complete.

ash scan --use-existing runs only the report phase: it writes reports/ again from the ash_aggregated_results.json already in the output directory, rewrites metadata.summary_stats in that file, leaves scanners/ and the other files in place, and exits with the verdict of the stored results.

docs.title: Links are refused
docs.text:
ASH refuses to write through a symbolic link or a Windows directory junction at any of these:

  • the output directory itself, or a directory on the way to it below the source directory (the default .ash/ash_output is below it, so a repository can commit such a link);
  • analysis, reports, scanners, or converted in the output directory;
  • the files ASH writes there by a fixed name: ash_aggregated_results.json, ash-ignore-report.txt, ash-scan-set-files-list.txt, ash.log, and ash.log.jsonl;
  • in workspace mode, projects and .workspace-spool in the workspace's output directory, and each project's projects/<project> directory.

It also refuses an output directory below the source directory whose real path, with every link resolved, is outside the source directory.

The check runs before anything is written or deleted, in every run mode and whatever the sandbox mode, and also in ash report and ash merge. The command exits 3:

ERROR (3) The output directory /work/out-link is a symlink. ASH does not write to, clear or
mount its output directory through a link, whatever the sandbox mode. Pass --output-dir with
a directory that is not a link, or replace the link with a directory.

In an ash --workspace scan, a link at projects or .workspace-spool stops the whole run this way before any project starts. A link at projects/<project> fails only that project, logged as Project '<project>' was not scanned: and the same refusal. The other projects still run, and the run exits 1, or 2 when another project has actionable findings (see Workspace mode). Over MCP, run_ash_workspace_scan refuses the whole call when any of these is a link.

Directories above an output directory that is outside the source directory are not examined, so --output-dir /tmp/ash works on a system where /tmp is a link.

Reports are checked again before any reporter writes. If reports/, or a file that one of the reporters about to run writes there, such as reports/ash.sarif, is a link, the run stops with exit 1:

ERROR (1) /work/out/reports/ash.sarif is a symlink. ASH does not write a report through a link.
Remove the link and run ASH again.

This applies to scans in every run mode, including --use-existing and workspace scans, and to ash merge. ash merge prints the same text after Refusing to write reports:. ash report prints its report instead of writing it, and refuses a link only at a file the reporter writes beside it.

docs.title: ash_aggregated_results.json
docs.text:
The scan engine writes this file, not a reporter, and every reporter and ash report reads it. Its JSON schema is AshAggregatedResults.json.

Top-level name Contents name, description A label with the scan's start time, and a fixed description. metadata About the run. See below. ash_config The configuration the scan resolved, after overrides and trust rules. A value or key a config file read from the environment is recorded as the reference the file wrote, here and in metadata.expected_scanners (Read values from the environment). scanner_results One row per scanner, keyed by scanner name. See below. converter_results One row per converter, keyed by converter name. See below. sarif The aggregated SARIF report. See SARIF. cyclonedx The CycloneDX software bill of materials syft produced; with no components when syft did not run. additional_reports Each scanner's per-target record, keyed by scanner and then target (source, converted). The same records as scanners/<name>/<target>/ASH.ScanResults.json. validation_checkpoints The checks ASH ran on its own execution (were all selected scanners queued, did each finish), and configuration warnings, which have type set to config_warning. used_suppressions The ids of the global_settings.suppressions entries that matched a finding (format below). Inline ash-ignore comments are not listed. workspace The workspace plan and per-project outcomes in workspace mode; null otherwise.

A suppression's ID is its path, rule ID, first line, and last line joined with |, with * for a part the entry does not set, so an entry for rule B602 in app.py with no lines is app.py|B602|*|*. Entries that set package or symbol fields have more parts.

metadata holds report_id, generated_at, project_name (the config's project_name, else the ASH_PROJECT_NAME environment variable, else ash-scan), tool_version (the ASH version), summary_stats, validation_summary, execution_discrepancy_report, shard (set by --shard-index), expected_scanners, requested_scanners_not_run (the names in --scanners or ASH_SCANNERS that matched no scanner, or null when every name matched or no list was given; ash merge records the names of all the shards), plugin_load_errors (plugin groups that failed to import), and changed_files_only (true when --changed-files-only filtered the findings, false on a full scan, including one that fell back to a full scan).

report_id is unique to each scan: ASH-, the scan's start as a UTC date and time, and 12 random hexadecimal digits, such as ASH-20261011180835-deff7bedfe39. Reports rendered again from saved results, by ash report or --use-existing, keep it. ash merge gives the merged results an id of the same shape, computed from the shards' ids, so merging the same shards again gives the same id. A workspace scan's combined results have an id of the form ASH-WORKSPACE-<workspace file name>-<date and time>-<hex digits>.

summary_stats totals the scan: severity_counts (suppressed, critical, high, medium, low, info), total (unsuppressed findings), actionable, the count of scanners in each status (passed, failed, missing, skipped, error), and start, end, and duration.

docs.title: Scanner rows
docs.text:
Each scanner_results row has:

Name Meaning status PASSED, FAILED, ERROR, MISSING, or SKIPPED; see the summary table. severity_counts, finding_count, actionable_finding_count, suppressed_finding_count The counts the summary table shows. duration How long the scanner ran, in seconds. dependencies_satisfied false on a MISSING row. excluded true when the run left the scanner out: --scanners, --exclude-scanners, enabled: false, --python-only, the shard split, or a platform it does not support. exit_code The tool's exit code, the highest over the targets it ran on, or null when no tool ran: a MISSING or excluded scanner, one that had nothing to scan, or one that started no tool for its targets. missing_reason On a MISSING row, why: the tool that was not found and where ASH looked, what the scanner's own dependency check reported, that the tool was found only inside the scanned directory, which ASH does not run unless you allow it (see Tools inside the scanned directory), or that the scanner could not be sandboxed. null otherwise. skipped_reason On a SKIPPED row, why: the option that left it out, such as not named by --scanners, or what it had nothing to scan, such as no CloudFormation template in the scanned files. null otherwise. 
{
  "grype": {
    "status": "MISSING",
    "dependencies_satisfied": false,
    "excluded": false,
    "severity_counts": {"suppressed": 0, "critical": 0, "high": 0, "medium": 0, "low": 0, "info": 0},
    "finding_count": 0,
    "actionable_finding_count": 0,
    "suppressed_finding_count": 0,
    "exit_code": null,
    "duration": 0.0,
    "missing_reason": "its tool grype was not found on PATH or in /home/me/.ash/bin, /home/me/.local/share/uv/tools/automated-security-helper/bin, /usr/local/bin; install it with `ash dependencies install` or exclude grype with --exclude-scanners",
    "skipped_reason": null
  }
}

docs.title: Converter rows
docs.text:
Each converter_results row (archive, jupyter) has:

Name Meaning dependencies_satisfied false when the converter's tool was missing. excluded true when the converter was turned off. failure The error, as <Type>: <message>, when the converter itself crashed or could not be created, or a note that it was dropped although its dependency check passed. candidate_inputs How many inputs it set out to convert, when it counts them. refused_inputs Inputs it declined to read, each with path, member (for an archive member) and reason, such as links, special files, and archive members with absolute names or names that would land outside the extraction directory. These never fail the scan. failed_inputs Inputs it tried and could not convert, each with path and reason, such as a corrupt archive or a notebook nbconvert could not read. A reason that comes from an unexpected error is the error's type and message, such as BadZipFile: Bad CRC-32 for file 'app.py'. converted_paths The files it wrote under converted/.

A converter with a failure, any failed_inputs, or a missing tool while it had inputs makes the conversion incomplete. Under the default fail_on_incomplete_scanners the scan then exits 1, because the scanners were given fewer files than the repository has. The console line for each such converter, and its entry in incomplete_converters in the MCP scan results, give its failure, the number of failed inputs and up to five of their paths, or dependencies unavailable, so it never ran.

{
  "archive": {
    "dependencies_satisfied": true,
    "excluded": false,
    "failure": null,
    "candidate_inputs": null,
    "refused_inputs": [],
    "failed_inputs": [
      {"path": "bundle.zip", "reason": "it is not a zip or tar archive Python can read"}
    ],
    "converted_paths": []
  }
}

docs.title: Suppressions and ignore paths in ash_config
docs.text: Each entry under ash_config.global_settings.suppressions and ash_config.global_settings.ignore_paths has a client_supplied flag. ASH sets it to true on entries that came from the config file of a tree an MCP client delivered, and marks the findings they hide in the SARIF (below). Treat the flag as a label for reading results, not as an access control. See Configuration trust model.

docs.title: SARIF
docs.text:
reports/ash.sarif and the sarif member of ash_aggregated_results.json hold the same SARIF 2.1.0 run, written two ways. The member writes every field of every result, defaults included, so its results show "ruleIndex": -1, and "rule": null unless the scanner gave one. reports/ash.sarif leaves out the fields ASH did not set, ruleIndex among them, and the empty ones, and adds each result's rule reference (below). After a scan of the sample project:

ash --scanners detect-secrets --no-progress

import json

with open(".ash/ash_output/ash_aggregated_results.json", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    member = json.load(f)["sarif"]["runs"][0]["results"][0]
with open(".ash/ash_output/reports/ash.sarif", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    report = json.load(f)["runs"][0]["results"][0]
for name, result in (("sarif member", member), ("reports/ash.sarif", report)):
    print(name, result.get("ruleIndex", "no ruleIndex"), result.get("rule", "no rule"))

sarif member -1 None
reports/ash.sarif no ruleIndex no rule

The run:

  • tool.driver is ASH itself (AWS Labs - Automated Security Helper, with ASH's version).
  • tool.extensions has one entry per scanner that produced SARIF, named after the scanner, carrying that scanner's rules and, as version, the version the scanner's own run reported. Some extensions also carry semanticVersion. When ASH does not know a scanner's version, version is left out. A scanner that produces only an SBOM, such as syft, has no entry.
  • results holds every scanner's results, appended without merging duplicates. Every result has a level; ASH fills in the level of a result that stated none, as How ASH counts findings describes.
  • In reports/ash.sarif, a result whose rule its scanner's extension defines carries rule, as SARIF asks for rules defined in an extension: rule.toolComponent gives the extension's name and its index in tool.extensions, and rule.index is the rule's position in that extension's rules. A result whose rule no extension defines, such as a detect-secrets result, has no rule.
  • invocations has one entry per scanner run, with its command line, working directory, exit code, and times. The command lines contain absolute paths from the machine that ran the scan.

Each result's properties carries scanner_name, tags, scanner_details (tool_name, tool_version, and the run's start and end times), and issue_severity when the scanner integration assigned one. scanner_version and scanner_details.tool_version hold the scanner's own version, and are left out when ASH does not know it. Locations in the source directory are relative to it, wherever ASH runs from. Findings in converted/ point into the output directory.

{
  "ruleId": "B602",
  "rule": {"id": "B602", "index": 2, "toolComponent": {"name": "bandit", "index": 0}},
  "level": "error",
  "message": {"text": "subprocess call with shell=True identified, security issue."},
  "locations": [
    {"physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": "app.py"}, "region": {"startLine": 7, "endLine": 7}}}
  ],
  "suppressions": [
    {
      "kind": "inSource",
      "justification": "(ASH) Suppressing finding for rule 'B602' in 'app.py' with reason: Commands come from a fixed allowlist in this demo"
    }
  ],
  "properties": {
    "tags": ["bandit"],
    "issue_confidence": "HIGH",
    "issue_severity": "HIGH",
    "scanner_name": "bandit",
    "scanner_version": "bandit 1.9.4",
    "scanner_details": {
      "tool_name": "bandit",
      "tool_version": "bandit 1.9.4",
      "tool_invocation": {
        "start_time": "2026-10-11T18:11:00.025599+00:00",
        "end_time": "2026-10-11T18:11:00.954843+00:00"
      }
    }
  }
}

A suppressed finding stays in results with a suppressions entry:

Source of the suppression kind justification starts with A global_settings.suppressions entry inSource (ASH) Suppressing finding for rule ... An inline ash-ignore comment inSource (ASH inline) An entry from the config of a tree an MCP client delivered inSource (ASH, client-supplied config) An ignore path or scanner exclusion from such a config external (ASH, client-supplied config)

Client-supplied entries also carry properties.clientSupplied: true. A finding under one of your own global_settings.ignore_paths is removed from the results, not suppressed. See Suppressions, ignore paths, and scanner exclusions.

In workspace mode the document has one run per project. Each run declares its project's root in originalUriBaseIds, keeps its URIs relative to that root, and gives the workspace-relative path in properties.workspace_uri.

reports/ash.ghas.sarif is a smaller variant for GitHub code scanning; see github-ghas.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
reports/ holds one file per enabled reporter, named ash.<extension>, or ash.txt for a reporter that declares no extension. The table lists the reporters ASH ships and whether each is enabled by default; Reporters gives each one's format and options.

A reporter's extension must be a file name suffix. A configured extension that contains /, \, .., or a NUL character is ignored with a warning, and the reporter's default is used. If a reporter's report file name is still not a single file name, one that is not empty, ., or .. and contains no /, \, or NUL, the run stops with exit 1 before any reporter writes.

File Reporter Enabled ash.cdx.json cyclonedx yes ash.csv csv yes ash.flat.json flat-json yes ash.ghas.sarif github-ghas yes ash.gl-dependency-scanning-report.cdx.json gitlab-cyclonedx yes ash.gl-sast-report.json gitlab-sast yes ash.html html yes ash.junit.xml junitxml yes ash.ocsf.json ocsf yes ash.sarif sarif yes ash.summary.md markdown yes ash.summary.txt text yes ash.unused-suppressions.json, ash.unused-suppressions.md unused-suppressions yes ash.spdx.json spdx no ash.yaml yaml no

Reporters from plugin modules, such as the AWS reporters, write their files here too. A reporter that fails logs an error and leaves its file out; it does not change the exit code.

ash.flat.json holds metadata (the project name, the scan and report times, and ASH's version), scanner_metrics (one row per scanner with its counts, status, excluded, dependencies_missing, missing_reason, and skipped_reason), content_databases, top_hotspots, and findings, one record per finding. A finding's id is <scanner>-<rule>-<12 hex digits>, such as bandit-B602-426afbe0ae52, and no two findings in a scan share one. The digits are a hash of what identifies the finding: the SARIF fingerprints its scanner gives, when they tell findings apart, or else its file and its start and end lines, plus the package for a dependency finding and the project in a workspace scan. A file a converter wrote is identified by its path under converted/. Findings that share all of that, such as two secrets on one line, are told apart by their column and message. So a finding keeps its id from one scan to the next, unless it has no fingerprints and an edit above it moves it to other lines.

docs.title: Per-scanner results
docs.text:
scanners/<name>/ is where each scanner writes, and under the sandbox it is the only directory a scanner can write to. Each target's directory below it holds the tool's raw output (SARIF, JSON, <Class>.stdout.log, and <Class>.stderr.log), the configuration files ASH generated for the tool, and ASH.ScanResults.json, ASH's record of that run. Some scanners keep the files ASH generated in scanners/<name>/ itself. Every scanner gets a directory; one that did not run holds only a short ASH.ScanResults.json with its status.

ASH.ScanResults.json has:

Name Meaning scanner_name, target, target_type Which scanner ran, on which directory, and whether it was source or converted. exit_code The tool's exit code. start_time, end_time, duration When it ran. finding_count, severity_counts How many results the run produced, suppressed ones included, and their split by severity, with suppressed results under suppressed. status The status of this run. It can differ from the scanner's row in scanner_results, which is the verdict the summary table shows. targets_attempted, targets_failed For scanners that count their inputs, how many they tried and how many they could not evaluate. raw_results For a failed run, errors, exception, and stack_trace.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: run_ash_scan runs an ASH scan from Python. It is the function that ash scan and the MCP server's scan tool call, so a scan started from Python behaves like one started from the command line, with one difference that matters: it ends a non-zero result by raising SystemExit.

docs.title: Programmatic usage
docs.text:
from automated_security_helper.interactions.run_ash_scan import run_ash_scan

results = run_ash_scan(
    source_dir=".",
    scanners=["detect-secrets"],
    offline=True,
    fail_on_findings=False,
    progress=False,
    show_summary=False,
    quiet=True,
)
stats = results.metadata.summary_stats
print(f"Found {stats.total} findings, {stats.actionable} actionable")
for name, row in results.scanner_results.items():
    if row.status != "SKIPPED":
        print(name, row.status.value, row.finding_count)

Run in a repository with one hardcoded password, this prints:

Found 1 findings, 1 actionable
detect-secrets FAILED 1

The scan also writes its usual output directory, here .ash/ash_output under the working directory.

docs.title: Return value and exit behavior
docs.text:
Outcome What run_ash_scan does exit code 0 returns an AshAggregatedResults, the model that ash_aggregated_results.json holds (Output files) actionable findings (exit code 2) raises SystemExit(2), with no results attached incomplete scan: a scanner MISSING, ERROR, or with lost targets, no scanner ran, a converter that lost inputs, a rule that could not be evaluated, or a stale content database raises ScanIncompleteExit, a SystemExit with code 1 whose incompleteness says why and whose results holds the model other errors (exit code 1) raises SystemExit(1) a configuration that cannot be used or is invalid, as for ash scan: a config path or an ASH_CONFIG that names no readable file, a config file that does not parse or does not validate, or an override that does not validate (exit code 3) raises SystemExit(3) a scanner selection that selects nothing: no name in scanners matches a scanner, or every name in scanners is also in exclude_scanners (exit code 5) raises SystemExit(5) before any scanner runs an output directory ASH refuses because it, a directory on the way to it, or one of its reports, scanners, converted, or analysis directories is a symbolic link raises OutputDirRefusedExit, a SystemExit with code 1 whose found names the link and whose reason says what to do interrupted with Ctrl-C lets KeyboardInterrupt propagate; ash scan turns it into exit code 130

The exit codes are those of the CLI (Exit codes). To get the results of a scan that has findings, pass fail_on_findings=False, as the example does. To get them from an incomplete scan, catch ScanIncompleteExit:

from automated_security_helper.interactions.run_ash_scan import (
    ScanIncompleteExit,
    run_ash_scan,
)

try:
    results = run_ash_scan(
        source_dir=".",
        scanners=["detect-secrets", "bandit"],
        offline=True,
        progress=False,
        show_summary=False,
        quiet=True,
    )
except ScanIncompleteExit as incomplete:
    print("incomplete:", incomplete.incompleteness.scanners)
    results = incomplete.results
except SystemExit as stopped:
    print("exit code", stopped.code)
    results = None

When bandit is not installed, this prints incomplete: (('bandit', 'MISSING'),). incompleteness.scanners lists (name, status) pairs; incompleteness.converters lists (name, reason) pairs; incompleteness.stale_content_databases lists the databases past their age bound; incompleteness.unevaluated_rules lists the rules that could not be evaluated; and incompleteness.no_scanner_ran is True when no scanner reached a verdict, as when every scanner was skipped. ASH also prints its incomplete-scan message, even with quiet=True.

A scanner name that matches no scanner stops the call before any scanner runs, so a misspelled name is never reported as a clean scan:

from automated_security_helper.interactions.run_ash_scan import run_ash_scan

run_ash_scan(
    source_dir=".",
    scanners=["detect_secrets"],
    offline=True,
    progress=False,
    show_summary=False,
    quiet=True,
)

ASH prints ERROR (5) None of the requested scanners exist: detect_secrets. and the names it has, and the uncaught SystemExit(5) ends the script with exit code 5. Scanner names use hyphens: detect-secrets. When only some of the names match, the scan runs the scanners they name and logs a warning about the rest.

A config that names no file stops the call the same way, with SystemExit(3), instead of scanning with the default configuration:

from automated_security_helper.interactions.run_ash_scan import run_ash_scan

run_ash_scan(
    source_dir=".",
    config="no-such-config.yaml",
    scanners=["detect-secrets"],
    offline=True,
    progress=False,
    show_summary=False,
    quiet=True,
)

With a workspace_plan, run_ash_scan returns the workspace result instead of AshAggregatedResults, and raises SystemExit with the workspace exit code when it is not 0.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Every parameter is optional and can be passed by keyword. Unless the table says otherwise, a parameter means what the ash scan option of the same name means. An unknown keyword argument raises TypeError, so a misspelled parameter name stops the call before anything runs, and so does a positional argument past the last parameter.

Parameter Default Notes source_dir None The directory to scan. None scans the working directory. output_dir None None writes to .ash/ash_output under the working directory, not under source_dir as the CLI does. Pass it whenever source_dir is not the working directory. config None Path to a config file. None discovers one in source_dir. config_overrides None List of key=value strings, as --config-overrides takes. offline False strategy ExecutionStrategy.PARALLEL An ExecutionStrategy from automated_security_helper.core.enums. scanners None List of scanner names. exclude_scanners None List of scanner names. progress True Set False outside a terminal. output_formats None List of ExportFormat members from automated_security_helper.core.enums. cleanup False phases None List of ExecutionPhase members. None runs every phase but inspect. inspect False existing_results None Path to an ash_aggregated_results.json to report from, as --use-existing sets it. python_based_plugins_only False As --python-only. quiet False simple False verbose False debug False color True fail_on_findings None None takes the value from the config, else True. fail_on_incomplete_scanners None None takes the value from the config, else True. ignore_suppressions False min_severity 'low' changed_files_only False base_ref 'origin/main' shard_index None shard_count None mode RunMode.local RunMode.container, RunMode.nix, or RunMode.precommit for the other run modes. show_summary True Prints the results table. log_level AshLogLevel.INFO build True Container mode only. run True Container mode only. force False Container mode only. oci_runner None Container mode only. build_target None Container mode only. offline_semgrep_rulesets 'p/ci' Container mode only. container_uid None Container mode only. container_gid None Container mode only. ash_revision_to_install None Container mode only. custom_containerfile None Container mode only. custom_build_arg None Container mode only. ash_plugin_modules None Plugin modules to load. This is an operator source: ASH imports every module it names (Who may load a module). container_network 'bridge' Container mode only: the network the scan container uses when the scan is online. workspace_plan None A workspace scan, which --workspace builds the plan for. allow_missing_projects False For a workspace scan. config_base_gate None Used by the MCP server; see below. untrusted_config False Used by the MCP server; see below. trusted_config_path None Used by the MCP server; see below. client_config_policy None Used by the MCP server; see below.

config_base_gate, untrusted_config, trusted_config_path, and client_config_policy let the MCP server apply the MCP-client limits of the Configuration trust model to the scans it runs; leave them at their defaults. untrusted_config raises ValueError in container or nix mode and with a workspace_plan, and client_config_policy raises it in container or nix mode.

Some ash scan options have no parameter. They become config overrides or an environment variable:

ash scan option Python equivalent --sandbox auto config_overrides=["sandbox.mode=auto"] --compact-report config_overrides=["reporters.markdown.options.compact=true"] --allow-stale-content-db config_overrides=["content_db_staleness=warn", "content_db_staleness_overrides=[]"] --allow-in-tree-tools set ASH_ALLOW_IN_TREE_TOOLS=1 in os.environ before the call

docs.title: Side effects
docs.text: run_ash_scan runs in your process. It sets environment variables while it runs (offline=True sets ASH_OFFLINE, and restores the previous value when the scan ends), configures ASH's logger, and registers plugins in a process-wide registry. A plugin module loaded by one call stays loaded for every later call in the same process. To change which plugin modules a scan loads, run it in a new process.

Unset, a model call is retried 3 times and a model listing makes 3 attempts. base_delay number, at most 60 1.0 Base delay in seconds between retries (will be increased exponentially). max_delay number, at most 60 60.0 Maximum delay in seconds between retries. enable_fallback_models boolean true Whether to try fallback models if the primary model fails. output_executive_file string bedrock-executive.md Filename for the executive summary markdown report, a file name in the reports directory. output_technical_file string bedrock-technical.md Filename for the technical analysis markdown report, a file name in the reports directory. include_code_snippets boolean false Whether to include code snippets in the report. summary_style one of executive, technical, detailed executive Style of summary to generate: executive (high-level), technical (detailed), or detailed (comprehensive). custom_prompt string or null null Custom prompt to prepend to all Bedrock requests for more tailored analysis. exclude_scanner_types list of string ["SECRET"] Scanner tool types whose findings are counted but not sent to the model (e.g., 'SECRETS'). A finding's type is its scanner's tool type, looked up from the scanner's name, or a tool_type:: tag on the finding; 'SECRET' and 'SECRETS' both name the secrets type. A finding whose type cannot be determined is sent without its code snippets. actionable_only boolean true Whether to include only actionable findings (not suppressed, above severity threshold). include_sections list of string ["executive_summary", "risk_assessment", "technical_analysis", "remediation_guide", "compliance_impact"] List of sections to include in the report. exclude_sections list of string [] List of sections to exclude from the report. industry_context string or null null Industry context to provide to the model for more relevant analysis. compliance_frameworks list of string [] List of compliance frameworks to consider in the analysis. custom_context string or null null Custom context information to provide to the model. summarize_findings boolean false Whether to summarize findings to reduce token usage. batch_processing boolean false Whether to process findings in batches for better performance with large datasets.

docs.title: Scanners reference
docs.text:
This page is generated from the scanner plugins in the ASH source code by scripts/generate_scanner_reference.py. Edits made to this file by hand are overwritten the next time it is generated.

ASH ships 19 scanners. The built-in ones are loaded on every scan. The others are community scanners, each in a plugin module that ash scan loads only when the configuration's ash_plugin_modules (or --ash-plugin-modules) names the module; for the MCP server, see What a plugin can do.

Scanner Tool type Enabled by default Provided by Command Runs with --python-only actionlint IAC yes built in actionlint no bandit SAST yes built in bandit yes cdk-nag IAC yes built in python no cfn-guard IAC yes built in cfn-guard no cfn-lint IAC yes built in cfn-lint yes cfn-nag IAC yes built in cfn_nag_scan no checkov IAC yes built in checkov yes detect-secrets SECRETS yes built in detect-secrets yes gitleaks SECRETS yes built in gitleaks no grype SCA yes built in grype no npm-audit SCA yes built in npm no opengrep SAST yes on Linux and macOS; no on Windows built in opengrep no semgrep SAST yes on Linux and macOS; no on Windows built in semgrep yes syft SBOM yes built in syft no trivy SCA yes built in trivy no zizmor SAST yes built in zizmor yes ferret-scan SECRETS yes community module ash_ferret_plugins ferret-scan no snyk-code SAST yes community module ash_snyk_plugins snyk no trivy-repo SAST yes community module ash_trivy_plugins trivy no

Tool type is the scanner's own ScannerToolType. --python-only keeps a scanner when its is_python_only() is true: the scanner class's own python_only when it states one; otherwise only when the scanner runs its tool through uv, declares no install commands, and has only pip dependencies. A scanner it does not keep is SKIPPED.

docs.title: Environment in the sandbox
docs.text:
When sandbox.mode confines scanners, a scanner process receives only an allowlist of the environment ASH was started with. Every sandboxed scanner gets these names: COLUMNS, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, FORCE_COLOR, GEM_HOME, GEM_PATH, JAVA_HOME, LANG, LANGUAGE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, NO_COLOR, PATH, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, SSL_CERT_DIR, SSL_CERT_FILE, SYSTEMROOT, TERM, TZ, VIRTUAL_ENV; and names starting with LC_, ASH_, UV_, PYTHON. A scanner's own prefixes and names, listed with each scanner below, are added to that. A name containing TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSWD, SECRET, CREDENTIAL, AUTH, APIKEY, API_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, SESSION is dropped even under an allowed prefix, unless the scanner names it exactly. The proxy variables HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY, http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy are passed only to a scanner that has a network. The lists are in automated_security_helper/utils/sandbox/policy.py.

The network entry of each scanner below is its default. sandbox.network_scanners, when it is set, replaces every scanner's declared need: only the scanners it names get a network. A config file inside a git checkout or the scanned directory can only take network away, and an offline scan gives no scanner a network.

Options, under scanners.cfn-lint.options. An option not listed here refuses the configuration.

Option Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null Minimum severity level to consider findings as failures. This is a scanner-level override of the default severity-level within ASH of MEDIUM. scan_timeout integer or null, at least 1 1800 Maximum time in seconds to allow this scanner's tool invocation to run before it is killed. Set to null to leave the scanner unbounded, which risks a scan that never completes. offline boolean false Run this scanner offline even when ASH runs online. False follows ASH's own mode; it never puts a scanner online under --offline. config_file path, string, or null null Path to a cfn-lint configuration file (.cfnlintrc). A relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides, not from the source directory. When unset, ASH gives cfn-lint an empty configuration, so a .cfnlintrc in the scanned repository or the home directory is NOT read: such a file can load Python rules (append_rules) and switch checks off. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; otherwise it is ignored with a warning. regions list of string [] AWS regions to validate templates against, e.g. ['us-east-1', 'eu-west-1'], or ['ALL_REGIONS']. Empty validates against us-east-1, or the regions a template names in its own cfn-lint metadata or config_file names; AWS_REGION and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION are not read. ignore_checks list of string [] cfn-lint rule ids or prefixes to skip, e.g. ['W2001', 'W3']. Prefer ASH suppressions for individual findings; this removes the rule from every template. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. Set by such a config, it is ignored with a warning. include_checks list of string [] cfn-lint rule ids or prefixes to enable in addition to the defaults, e.g. ['I'] for informational rules. honor_inline_ignores boolean false Honor the ignore_checks and configure_rules a template sets for itself in Metadata: cfn-lint: config (ignore_checks also at the resource level). Off by default: every rule outside ignore_checks and the config_file's ignore_checks is passed to cfn-lint as mandatory, and the config_file's configure_rules are passed on the command line, which cfn-lint takes instead of a template's, so a template cannot hide its own findings or the next template's parse errors, which reach ASH, where suppressions are reported and counted. A config_file setting the command line cannot carry (a list of more than one item, or a value with a comma, colon or equals sign) is then left out with a warning, and a config_file that sets merge_configs fails the scan. On, each template is linted by a cfn-lint run of its own, so its settings reach no other template; that adds a cfn-lint start-up per template. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. Set by such a config, it is ignored with a warning. tool_version string or null ">=1.43.3,<2.0.0" Version constraint for the cfn-lint installation, in pip requirement syntax. The default is the range the scanner's SARIF handling was verified against. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. Set by such a config, it is ignored with a warning. install_timeout integer 300 Timeout in seconds for tool installation

By default, all plugins will be used and no filters are configured. scan_settings takes precedence over baseline_file skip_generated_lockfiles boolean true Skip machine-generated dependency lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, poetry.lock, and similar) before scanning. These are dense with integrity hashes and are regenerated rather than hand-edited, so findings in them are usually noise. Hand-authored dependency declarations such as requirements.txt, Pipfile and environment.yml are always scanned and are not affected by this option. Set to false to scan generated lockfiles as well. max_worker_output_mib integer, greater than 0, at most 4,096 256 The most of the detect-secrets worker's output read back, in MiB, at most 4096. A finding is about 300 bytes of output, so the default of 256 holds about 900,000 findings. Reading the output costs about three times its size in memory (1024 MiB of output needs about 3 GiB). A scan whose output is larger fails and records no findings, with an error that names this option. Honored only from --config-overrides or a config file outside the scanned tree.
