Options, under scanners.trivy.options. An option not listed here refuses the configuration.

Option Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null Minimum severity level to consider findings as failures. This is a scanner-level override of the default severity-level within ASH of MEDIUM. scan_timeout integer or null, at least 1 1800 Maximum time in seconds to allow this scanner's tool invocation to run before it is killed. Set to null to leave the scanner unbounded, which risks a scan that never completes. offline boolean false Run in offline mode: skip database and check updates and use the vulnerability database already in trivy's cache. ASH still fails the scan when that database is past its 24h bound. When true, this scanner runs offline even if ASH does not. ASH's own offline mode (--offline or ASH_OFFLINE) applies whatever this is set to; false follows it. scanners list of one of vuln, misconfig, secret, license, length at least 1 ["vuln"] Which trivy scanners to run. Defaults to vuln only: ASH's default scanners already cover secrets (detect-secrets) and IaC misconfigurations (checkov, cfn-nag, cdk-nag), and license findings are a compliance question. Add secret, misconfig or license to run trivy's checks for them as well. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. Set by such a config, any set but the default is ignored with a warning. license_full boolean false Look for licenses in source file headers and license files too (trivy --license-full). Only used when scanners includes license. ignore_unfixed boolean false Report only vulnerabilities that have a fixed version (trivy --ignore-unfixed). Off by default: an unfixed vulnerability is still one, and turning this on withholds it from the report. disable_telemetry boolean true Disable sending anonymous usage data to Aqua (--disable-telemetry). Only the operator sets it to false, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, may set it to true but not to false. Offline, trivy sends none whatever this says. As for trivy-repo. config_file path, string, or null null A trivy config file (trivy.yaml), passed as --config. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; otherwise it is ignored with a warning. A relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides, not from the source directory. Unset or ignored, ASH passes TRIVY_CONFIG when that names a file outside the scanned tree (a relative path in it is taken from the working directory), and otherwise an empty config of its own, so a trivy.yaml in the scanned repository is not read: its settings (severity, scan.skip-files, db.repository, ...) can drop findings with nothing in the report saying so, and module.dir can load WASM modules. A path that does not exist fails the scan. ignore_file path, string, or null null A trivy ignore file, passed as --ignorefile. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; a relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides and the environment variable. Unset, TRIVY_IGNOREFILE is used the same way, and otherwise trivy gets an empty one, so a .trivyignore in the scanned repository does not remove findings. As for trivy-repo. secret_config_file path, string, or null null A trivy secret scanning config (trivy-secret.yaml), passed as --secret-config. Only read when scanners includes secret. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree, and a relative path is taken as for ignore_file. Unset, TRIVY_SECRET_CONFIG is used the same way, and otherwise trivy gets an empty one, so a trivy-secret.yaml in the scanned repository does not disable secret rules. As for trivy-repo.

docs.title: ferret-scan
docs.text:
Ferret Scan is a sensitive data detection tool that scans files for potential sensitive information such as credit card numbers, passport numbers, SSNs, API keys, and other secrets.

  • Scanner page: ferret-scan scanner page
  • Class: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins.ferret_scanner.FerretScanScanner
  • Provided by: community module ash_ferret_plugins, which ash scan loads when ash_plugin_modules names automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_ferret_plugins
  • Enabled by default: yes
  • Tool type: SECRETS
  • Command: ferret-scan
  • Install: none declared
  • Offline strategy: bundled
  • Network in the sandbox, by default: no
  • Environment passed into the sandbox: FERRET_*
  • Environment set under sandbox-exec: none

Options, under scanners.ferret-scan.options. An option not listed here refuses the configuration.

Option Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null Minimum severity level to consider findings as failures. This is a scanner-level override of the default severity-level within ASH of MEDIUM. scan_timeout integer or null, at least 1 1800 Maximum time in seconds to allow this scanner's tool invocation to run before it is killed. Set to null to leave the scanner unbounded, which risks a scan that never completes. offline boolean false Run this scanner offline even when ASH runs online. False follows ASH's own mode; it never puts a scanner online under --offline. confidence_levels one of all, high, medium, low, high,medium, high,low, medium,low all Confidence levels to display: 'high', 'medium', 'low', or combinations checks string all Specific checks to run, comma-separated. As of ferret-scan v2.4.5 through v2.5.2: BANK_ACCOUNT, CLOUD_RESOURCES, CREDIT_CARD, DATE_OF_BIRTH, DRIVERS_LICENSE, EMAIL, INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY, IP_ADDRESS, MEDICAL_ID, METADATA, OTP, PASSPORT, PERSON_NAME, PHONE, PHYSICAL_ADDRESS, SECRETS, SOCIAL_MEDIA, SSN, VIN, or 'all'. The authoritative list for the installed version is 'ferret-scan --help checks'. recursive boolean true Recursively scan directories config_file path, string, or null null Path to Ferret configuration file (YAML). If not specified, uses the default config bundled with this plugin. Set to a custom path to override the default configuration. use_default_config boolean true Use the default ferret-config.yaml bundled with this plugin. Set to False to disable the default config and rely only on ferret-scan's built-in defaults. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. profile string or null null Profile name to use from config file (e.g., 'quick', 'ci', 'security-audit', 'comprehensive'). A profile can run fewer checks and report only higher-confidence findings. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. exclude_patterns list of string [] File patterns to exclude from scanning (glob patterns) show_match boolean false Display the actual matched text in findings. Note: This affects ferret-scan output, not ASH logging. enable_preprocessors boolean true Enable text extraction from documents (PDF, Office files). This allows scanning content within binary document formats. finding_limit integer, at least 0 0 Maximum number of findings ferret-scan will emit, passed as '--limit'. ferret-scan defaults to 200, which silently truncates results on large scans; ASH defaults this to 0 (unlimited) so no findings are dropped from the SARIF report. Set a positive integer to cap output. fail_on_incomplete boolean false Pass '--fail-on-incomplete' so ferret-scan exits 3 when a file could not be fully scanned (coverage cut short by a timeout/budget, or the file could not be opened). Findings may be missing in that case. The plugin still reports the (partial) findings, and counts the target as failed, so the scanner's row is ERROR and the completeness gate fails the scan. Off by default to match ferret-scan, which otherwise only warns on stderr. respect_gitignore boolean false Pass '--respect-gitignore' so ferret-scan honours .gitignore when scanning. Off by default: .gitignore commonly hides files with high secret-scanning value (.env, *.pem, credentials/), so honouring it can suppress exactly what a sensitive-data scan should see. disable_ip_types string or null null Comma-separated INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY sub-types to skip, passed as '--disable-ip-types': copyright, patent, trademark, trade_secret, internal_url. Useful for codebases with a standard copyright header on every file. Only affects the INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY check. explain boolean false Pass '--explain' so ferret-scan annotates each finding with a plain-language rationale, a verdict (likely real/test/uncertain), and a drafted suppression reason. Fully offline — no data leaves the host. validator_budget string or null null Per-validator time budget passed as '--validator-budget', e.g. 'SSN=500ms,IP_ADDRESS=2m' or 'all=2m'. Over-budget validators are stopped and the scan is marked incomplete (see fail_on_incomplete). Default: no budget. max_live_bytes string or null null Cap on total extracted content held in memory across concurrently scanned files, passed as '--max-live-bytes', e.g. '256MB' or '1GB' (units: B, KB, MB, GB; bare number = bytes). Bounds peak memory on constrained hosts. Default: no cap. ferret_debug boolean false Enable ferret-scan's debug logging (shows preprocessing and validation flow). This controls ferret-scan's own output, not ASH logging. ferret_verbose boolean false Enable ferret-scan's verbose output (detailed finding info). This controls ferret-scan's own output, not ASH logging. tool_version string or null null Version constraint for ferret-scan installation (e.g., '>=1.0.0,<2.0.0', '==1.2.0'). If not specified, uses the plugin's default compatible version range: >=2.4.5,<2.6.0. Supported versions: 2.4.5 to 2.6.0 (exclusive). skip_version_check boolean false Skip version compatibility check. Use with caution - incompatible versions may cause unexpected behavior or errors.

docs.title: snyk-code
docs.text:
• Scanner page: snyk-code scanner page
  • Class: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins.snyk_code_scanner.SnykCodeScanner
  • Provided by: community module ash_snyk_plugins, which ash scan loads when ash_plugin_modules names automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_snyk_plugins
  • Enabled by default: yes
  • Tool type: SAST
  • Command: snyk
  • Install: none declared
  • Offline strategy: skip_offline
  • Network in the sandbox, by default: yes, unless the scan is offline
  • Environment passed into the sandbox: SNYK_*, SNYK_TOKEN
  • Environment set under sandbox-exec: none

Options, under scanners.snyk-code.options. An option not listed here refuses the configuration.

Option Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null Minimum severity level to consider findings as failures. This is a scanner-level override of the default severity-level within ASH of MEDIUM. scan_timeout integer or null, at least 1 1800 Maximum time in seconds to allow this scanner's tool invocation to run before it is killed. Set to null to leave the scanner unbounded, which risks a scan that never completes. offline boolean false Run this scanner offline even when ASH runs online. False follows ASH's own mode; it never puts a scanner online under --offline. honor_tree_exclusions boolean false Let snyk code test apply the exclusion files it finds in the scanned tree: the exclude.code and exclude.global entries of a .snyk file and the rules of a .dcignore file, which leave the files they name out of the analysis. snyk has no option that stops it reading them, so while this is false and the tree has one, snyk-code does not run and its error names the files. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it.

docs.title: trivy-repo
docs.text:
• Scanner page: trivy-repo scanner page
  • Class: automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_trivy_plugins.trivy_repo_scanner.TrivyRepoScanner
  • Provided by: community module ash_trivy_plugins, which ash scan loads when ash_plugin_modules names automated_security_helper.plugin_modules.ash_trivy_plugins
  • Enabled by default: yes
  • Tool type: SAST
  • Command: trivy
  • Install: pinned, checksum-verified release of trivy by ash dependencies install, for darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64
  • Offline strategy: cache_flags
  • Network in the sandbox, by default: yes, unless the scan is offline
  • Environment passed into the sandbox: TRIVY_*
  • Environment set under sandbox-exec: none

Options, under scanners.trivy-repo.options. An option not listed here refuses the configuration.

Option Type Default Description severity_threshold one of ALL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL, or null null Minimum severity level to consider findings as failures. This is a scanner-level override of the default severity-level within ASH of MEDIUM. scan_timeout integer or null, at least 1 1800 Maximum time in seconds to allow this scanner's tool invocation to run before it is killed. Set to null to leave the scanner unbounded, which risks a scan that never completes. offline boolean false Run in offline mode, skipping DB updates and check-update calls. When true, this scanner runs offline even if ASH does not. ASH's own offline mode (--offline or ASH_OFFLINE) applies whatever this is set to; false follows it. scanners list of one of vuln, misconfig, secret, license ["vuln", "secret", "misconfig", "license"] List of what security issues to detect with Trivy Repo specifically license_full boolean true Eagerly look for licenses in source code headers and license files ignore_unfixed boolean true Display only fixed vulnerabilities disable_telemetry boolean true Disable sending anonymous usage data to Aqua (--disable-telemetry). Only the operator sets it to false, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, may set it to true but not to false. Offline, trivy sends none whatever this says. config_file path, string, or null null A trivy config file (trivy.yaml), passed as --config. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; otherwise it is ignored with a warning. A relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides, not from the source directory. Unset or ignored, ASH passes TRIVY_CONFIG when that names a file outside the scanned tree (a relative path in it is taken from the working directory), and otherwise an empty config of its own, so trivy does not load a trivy.yaml from the directory it runs in. A path that does not exist fails the scan. module_dir path, string, or null null A directory of trivy modules, passed as --module-dir. Unset, ASH passes an empty directory of its own. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The directory is used, and a relative path taken, as for config_file. A path that is not a directory fails the scan. ignore_file string or null null A trivy ignore file, passed as --ignorefile. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; a relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides and the environment variable. Unset, TRIVY_IGNOREFILE is used the same way, and otherwise trivy gets an empty one, so a .trivyignore in the scanned repository does not remove findings. secret_config_file string or null null A trivy secret scanning config (trivy-secret.yaml), passed as --secret-config. Used only when the operator sets it, with --config-overrides or in a config file outside every git checkout and the scanned directory: a config file inside one, or one an MCP client delivered, does not choose it. The file is used only when it is outside the scanned tree; a relative path is taken from the directory of the config file that sets it, or from the working directory for --config-overrides and the environment variable. Unset, TRIVY_SECRET_CONFIG is used the same way, and otherwise trivy gets an empty one, so a trivy-secret.yaml in the scanned repository does not disable secret rules.
